reviews.summary: `nerva chat -z "prompt"` runs one turn non-interactively and puts only the final assistant text on stdout — whole escape sequences and C0/C1 control bytes stripped, newlines and tabs kept — with every other word on stderr. The prompt resolves the way `nerva send`'s body does (argument, else `-f PATH` where `-` is stdin, else piped stdin) and a terminal is never read, by either spelling: `-f /dev/tty` is refused rather than blocking forever. A prompt over the hub's own 4,096-character `ChatRequest` bound is a usage error before the request, not an HTTP 422 a script reads as a failed turn. The ladder is stated in `--help`: 0 answered · 1 the turn did not complete · 2 usage · 3 no hub · 4 not authorised · 130 interrupted; Ctrl-C returns 130 with one stderr line instead of an uncaught traceback that could spill a partial answer. **The governance clause is implemented against Hermes, not after it:** no flag auto-approves, a turn that queues an action stays queued, and the verb exits 1 naming the pending id to decide with `nerva approvals`; a test asserts the one-shot path issues no decision call at all. For a queued action the verdict no longer rests on the reply text. The hub reports what the turn queued: `ChatResponse.pending_approvals` on `POST /chat`, and the same list on `/chat/stream`'s end event. A per-turn collector (`agents/core/turn_approvals.py`) gathers the ids at the gated Tool-RPC enqueue, and they are still reported when the turn raised after queuing. Any reported id makes `-z` exit 1 with the id on stderr, whatever the reply says, so a model that writes a plausible answer around a queued action does not exit 0. The reply text is a second detector, for stops that queue nothing and for a hub that reports no ids. It is matched by containment over the sanitised text, so the deterministic `[athena]: …` join that the synthesis pass falls back to still matches. The table holds the approval reply, the busy/compaction/continuation refusals, the no-local-model reply, the hub's two failure replies, the five tool-loop stops and a prefix rule for the stop built with an f-string. A drift test imports the eleven runtime constants and asserts each is matched both verbatim and wrapped. Sanitising happens before the verdict, so a reply of pure control bytes is an incomplete turn rather than exit 0 and a blank line. `--usage-file PATH` writes `nerva.chat.usage.v1` atomically on every path including the interrupt, cleans up its temp file when a write fails, survives a field it cannot encode (a warning, never a crash after the answer is already out), says so when given an empty path, and refuses to call a turn completed while naming an approval it left queued. A hub that reports `pending_approvals` in a shape this version cannot read is told so, rather than the string being exploded into one fabricated id per character. 76 tests in tests/test_nerva_oneshot.py; the hub-side report is pinned by tests/test_turn_pending_approvals.py. Thinking-exhaustion follow-up (2026-10-09): the exact backend THINKING_EXHAUSTED_REPLY is now in the stdlib-only refusal table. Direct, specialist-wrapped and control-padded forms make one-shot chat exit 1 with empty stdout and a fixed reason; the persisted receipt is refused/incomplete. Interactive stdout and exit 0 remain compatible while its optional receipt reports the refusal. Both constant drift guards include the real backend sentinel. This does not classify model-rephrased or mixed outcomes and never retries or decides an approval. Session receipt attribution (2026-10-09): new v1 receipts always include requested_session_id for the caller intent and use session_id only for the exact valid ID returned by a decoded normal POST /chat response. Returned/requested mismatch, /new HTTP selection, refused/queued replies, legacy/malformed IDs, interruption and vision separation are covered. Missing confirmation remains null with no fallback or coercion; the original request body and outcome are unchanged. Historical v1 receipts without the new key remain caller-echo evidence. The current contract and migration note are in docs/cli-chat-receipts.md. Usage/cost fields remain unavailable.
reviews.remaining: Two parts of the row are open. (1) THE CLI RECEIPT STILL HAS NO PER-TURN USAGE ATTRIBUTION. _usage_report initializes model, provider, api_calls, input_tokens, output_tokens and estimated_cost_usd to null with cost_basis unavailable; cmd_chat.finish does not fill them from the hub. These are unavailable values, not measured zeros. (2) A STOP THAT QUEUES NOTHING IS STILL JUDGED BY TEXT, AND ON A LIVE HUB THAT TEXT IS USUALLY REWRITTEN. The hub reports ids only for approvals queued through the gated Tool-RPC path. The tool loop's own stops are recognised only by containment over the reply. A turn routed to a specialist is not handed back verbatim: the orchestrator sends it through synthesis (`was_synthesized = len(responses) > 1 or "jarvis" not in responses`). With a `jarvis` agent and a router loaded, `jarvis.synthesize` rewrites it through a model; only the fallbacks (no `jarvis` agent, no router, a failed synthesis call) produce the `[athena]: …` join that containment survives. So a specialist's tool-loop stop can come back reworded and exit 0. The exact THINKING_EXHAUSTED_REPLY and containment-preserving wrappers are now refused; a differently worded synthesis result remains outside this text-only classification. Also open: the CLI receipt records no trace or invocation id; actual returned-session attribution is implemented, while older hubs without a usable ID remain explicitly unknown; `-z` does not silence hub-side logging; there is no `--output-format` beyond the existing `--json`; a piped body is read whole up to the bound rather than streamed; and `os.replace` onto a symlinked `--usage-file` path replaces the link with a regular file instead of writing through it.

reviews.summary: `nerva doctor` rulează `scripts/doctor.py` fără să schimbe nimic, cu un motiv numit pentru fiecare verificare, `--json` și `--smoke`. Are cinci verificări obligatorii (python, venv, locks_in_sync, bind_is_loopback, data_root_writable) și nouă consultative (runtimes, readyz, runtime_resolves, voice din H613, config_sources, smoke și, din H501, host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords, container_storage; scripts/doctor.py:111-113). Iese cu 1 doar când pică una obligatorie; o consultativă care pică e `warn`. Din HEQ lot 1 (H242), `runtime_resolves` verifică dacă ruta pe care o ia un turn Jarvis chiar se rezolvă la un model utilizabil, nu doar dacă răspunde un runtime. Citește verdictul strict al hub-ului, blocul `model` din `GET /api/onboarding/command-center` (același select_backend, fără generare), cu un singur credențial local: `JARVIS_USER_TOKEN`, altfel `JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN`, pe care îl trimite doar unui hub de pe această mașină, decis după adresă, nu după ortografie (scripts/doctor.py:346, scripts/doctor.py:393-400). E `ok` doar pe `ready: true` care numește ruta, providerul și modelul. Altfel dă motivul numit (`configured_not_resident`, `route_unselected`, `needs_token`, `malformed_reply` …), iar fără un hub gata e `skip`. `readyz` și această citire folosesc aceeași adresă de hub ca `nerva status` (`NERVA_HUB_URL`, altfel `JARVIS_HOST`/`JARVIS_PORT`; o adresă wildcard e apelată prin loopback). Din H273, `config_sources` arată, informativ, din ce strat vine fiecare cheie de configurare (mediul procesului > `.env`-ul repo-ului > `.env`-ul din data home) și ce valori din `.env` sunt acoperite de un strat de mai sus — doar nume, niciodată o valoare. `nerva status` arată același verdict pe o linie `runnable:`, separat de vechiul `model_state`, afișat acum „resident”. Alte diagnostice sunt verbe separate: `nerva desktop status` (ce îi lipsește host-ului pentru operatorul desktop), `nerva security audit` (vulnerabilități cunoscute, prin OSV) și `nerva extensions doctor`.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc jumătățile de reparare și de operare ale rândului: nu există `--fix` (reparări numite, în tier reversibil, cu tot ce atinge credențiale sau postura pus în coada de aprobare), `--live` (rulare continuă) sau `--ack ADVISORY_ID`. Lipsesc și verificările cerute pentru o instalare deja configurată: accesibilitatea serverelor MCP, token-urile canalelor, postura kernel/flag-uri, integritatea lanțului de audit și credențialele/conectivitatea fiecărui provider configurat. `runtime_resolves` judecă doar ruta pe care o ia acum un turn Jarvis, iar o rută cloud trece pe decizia de disponibilitate a routerului, fără un apel care să verifice credențialul la provider.

Un advisory fără severitate declarată pică orice prag; o bază de date de neatins, un lot rămas paginat după 20 de pagini sau un audit care nu se încheie înseamnă exit 5 și nicio afirmație. O distribuție cu metadate nedecodabile e sărită și numită; textul advisory-urilor e curățat de caractere de control înainte de terminal. MCP (comenzi stdio configurate de owner) e listat ca neauditat, cu motivul. Probat live: 48 distribuții curate; un pin `requests 2.19.0` dă 5 constatări după unirea a 5 oglinzi PYSEC. Recenzie adversarială independentă: nouă defecte, toate remediate în același PR.
reviews.remaining: Suprafața MCP nu e auditată: comenzile stdio (`npx …`, `uvx …`) din configurația persistată nu sunt rezolvate la pachete și versiuni. Descriptorii de extensie trebuie numiți pe linia de comandă; catalogul pachetelor achiziționate e pe partea hub-ului și nu e citit offline. Nu există `nerva security` implicit (cli-d.security-default) și nici `--skip-venv/--skip-plugins/--skip-mcp`. Vectorii CVSS nu sunt scorați: un advisory doar cu vector rămâne `unknown` și pică orice prag dacă nu se unește cu un frate GHSA evaluat. Pragul implicit `--fail-on low` e deliberat mai strict decât `critical` din Hermes. Nu există setare de proxy pentru operator (H281). Din procesul CLI nu există mediere kernel și registrul de egress nu persistă. Scara de ieșire e cea Nerva (0/1/2/5), nu 0/1/2 din Hermes. Fără probă pe o mașină fără proxy transparent.

The port-conflict diagnostic, plus one stale line of evidence corrected. `serve.py` gains `probe_bind(host, port)`, called from `main()` after the posture guards and before uvicorn binds: a taken port prints the exact address, the command that identifies the holder (`nerva status`) and the way out (`JARVIS_PORT`), then exits **12**; `EACCES` exits **13**, and since #1177 that arm branches on the port number instead of asserting a cause it cannot know — below 1024 it names the privileged-port rule (root or `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`; move `JARVIS_PORT` above 1024), at or above 1024 it says outright that this is *not* the privileged-port rule and root/Administrator will not help, then points at the reservations that actually produce it (Windows `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange tcp`, whose Hyper-V/WSL blocks routinely cover the shipped default 8080; an SELinux `name_bind` denial on Linux) plus `JARVIS_PORT`. Both codes are deliberately distinct from uvicorn's `STARTUP_FAILURE` (3), which it uses for *every* startup failure — that collision was the actual defect, because a supervisor could not tell "the port is taken" from "the lifespan crashed". The probe is a **diagnostic, not a lock**: it binds and closes, reserves nothing, and any `OSError` outside the two named arms is swallowed, so an unexpected probe failure can never turn a boot that would have worked into a refusal. The socket **constructor sits inside the guarded region** too — a first cut that built it above the `try` turned `JARVIS_HOST=::1` on a box with no IPv6 stack into an 8-frame traceback + exit 1 in place of uvicorn's one-line error + exit 3, the diagnostic making the boot worse than no diagnostic. It also mirrors asyncio's own flags rather than stricter ones: `SO_REUSEADDR` on POSIX, because `uvicorn.Server.startup` binds through `loop.create_server` where asyncio sets it, so a probe without it would refuse a port merely holding a TIME_WAIT connection from the instance the owner just stopped — a boot uvicorn would have completed; and `IPV6_V6ONLY` on an AF_INET6 probe, so an IPv4 listener on the same port cannot turn a working v6 boot into exit 12. **The frozen 2026-09-07 evidence was stale on one point**: it recorded "no --status", but `nerva status` has existed since the unified CLI (the `status` verb in `agents/cli/nerva.py`). 13 `test_probe_bind_*` functions, 16 collected cases (the IPv6-conflict case skips on a box with no IPv6 stack). Both exit codes are asserted **by execution** rather than by reading the branch — the sub-1024 `EACCES` arm runs in a child dropped to an unprivileged uid with `setpriv`, because pytest runs as root here and a sub-1024 bind simply succeeds; the high-port `EACCES` arm is driven through a stubbed `bind()` that answers `EACCES`, parametrised over 1024/8080/49152/65535, because its real reproduction is a Windows excluded port range that cannot be staged on Linux, and a sibling test pins that port 80 still gets the privileged-port sentence. ENV-122 in `docs/test-manual/01-environment-and-boot.md` moves from a message-quality finding to an asserted string plus exit code.
reviews.remaining: Hermes's row is start, check **and stop**, and the stop half is entirely absent: no `stop` verb, no pidfile, no ready file. The row cites `hermes dashboard --status/--stop` plus backend ready sentinels and a ready file (06-cli-f.md, 16 entries); Nerva has `nerva status`, which reads the HTTP surface and so cannot report a hub that is starting or wedged before the port opens, and Ctrl-C. Hermes also signals the conflict as a machine-readable `BACKEND_PORT_IN_USE`, where this slice signals it as an exit code and an English sentence — enough for a supervisor, not enough for a caller parsing a status stream. Not delivered either: `--isolated`, `--skip-build`, `--no-open`, the SSH session-token file and owner-nonce, or the interactive auth-setup prompt. **One known limit, in the safe direction:** the probe picks a single address family from the host string while uvicorn binds every address `getaddrinfo` returns, so a dual-stack name like `localhost` is probed on v4 only and can miss a conflict held on the v6 address — it misses silently, and uvicorn then reports it exactly as it does today. The Windows half of the `SO_REUSEADDR` choice is read off asyncio's `reuse_address = os.name == "posix"` line and has never been executed here; that test skips off POSIX and the docstring says so.

reviews.remaining: Rândul cere și jumătatea de instalare pe care Nerva o rezolvă altfel: Hermes are `computer-use install` care aduce și repară un binar cua străin, plus `status` și `doctor` separate. Nerva își construiește propriile drivere, deci nu există binar de adus — dar nu există nici instalarea dependențelor opționale dintr-o comandă (pywinauto/uiautomation/pyobjc/PyGObject rămân în sarcina owner-ului), nici un `doctor` dedicat operatorului, nici o suprafață în HUD pentru aceeași cale. reviews.summary: `nerva prompt-size` există și raportează costul fix per apel, pe componente, cel mai mare primul — offline, fără hub, fără backend, fără nicio cerere: citește personele de pe disc și cere registrului specurile pe care oricum le declară. Exact asta îl face utilizabil pentru întrebarea la care răspunde („cât plătesc înainte să înceapă conversația") pe o cutie unde hub-ul nici măcar nu rulează. `agents/core/prompt_size.py` sparge costul în: câte o linie per persoană de agent găsită pe disc, câte una per unealtă — costată ca **JSON-ul care chiar traversează sârma**, nu ca numele ei, fiindcă un `input_schema` stufos poate cântări cât o persoană întreagă — indexul de skill-uri randat exact cum îl randează `build_prompt`, și schela de tură pe care fiecare cerere o plătește. Numărul pe care raportul îl scoate în față e **podeaua per apel**, nu suma: cele 18 persoane sunt listate separat fiindcă o cerere reală trimite una singură, a agentului rutat. Prima versiune a raportului aduna toate cele 18 și anunța 71,8 % dintr-o fereastră de 32k, când o cerere reală plătește ~6,5 % — un număr greșit e mai rău decât niciun număr, așa că podeaua per apel e ce se citește primul și un test o fixează. Fără agent numit se folosește persoana cea mai grea, deci cifra e cazul realist cel mai prost, nu unul măgulitor; un agent inexistent nu e taxat tăcut pe seama altcuiva. Raportul spune despre el însuși că cifrele sunt estimări din aceeași funcție pe care o folosește bugetul la runtime, și trimite la H673 pentru singura măsurătoare exactă — cea raportată de provider. Ieșire text tabelară sau `--json`.
reviews.remaining: Rândul Hermes cere și componente pe care Nerva nu le are separate azi: „cele trei tiere de prompt" și „user profile" nu există ca blocuri distincte în asamblarea promptului (`Agent.build_prompt` are soul + skills + agent memory + schelă), iar `<available_skills>` e un index Hermes; echivalentul livrat e blocul `Available skills:`. Memoria nu e costată: e per sesiune și variabilă, nu cost fix, iar a o raporta ca „fix" ar fi exact tipul de cifră greșită pe care livrarea asta o evită. reviews.summary: A message that arrives while a turn runs on the same session waits for that session's turn lease (`Orchestrator.turn_lease`, agents/core/orchestrator.py:1711, taken by `_channel_turn` at agents/core/orchestrator.py:1648 and by the web /chat path at agents/web.py:1257). After `_TURN_LEASE_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (180 s, agents/core/orchestrator.py:263) it gets the single busy string `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:265) and no second turn starts on that transcript (tests/test_turn_lease.py:72, tests/test_turn_lease.py:118). `/pause` and `/stop` are owner-only (ADMIN tier) slash commands that engage the e-stop (agents/core/commands.py:410, agents/core/commands.py:411). They say plainly that work already in flight finishes (agents/core/commands.py:240, tests/test_slash_commands.py:124). Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. reviews.remaining: No busy-input semantics. A mid-turn message cannot redirect or interrupt the running turn. There is no explicit FIFO `/queue`, no `/steer` into the running turn and no configurable mode between these with downgrades. `/stop` is not a hard kill: it engages the e-stop but does not cancel the running turn or unlock the session. It is also dispatched inside `handle_input` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1973), so it waits behind the same lease. While a turn holds the lease past the wait bound, `/stop` itself is answered with `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` (named at agents/core/orchestrator.py:3742). There is one busy string, not a set of acks saying whether a message was queued, steered or interrupted. None of the protective demotions exist (running subagent, in-flight compression, photo burst, very fast follow-up merged as the same intent). The lease is the only slot reservation; there is no pending-agent sentinel. `SlashCommand` (agents/core/commands.py:61) carries no `busy_policy`.

reviews.summary: Turns are serialized per resolved session. `Orchestrator.turn_lease` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1711) holds one asyncio.Lock per key, and `_lease_key` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1701) follows `_resolve_session`'s order, so the lease names the session the turn will actually use rather than the routing key. It is taken by channel turns (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1648) and the web /chat path (agents/web.py:1257), and it is re-entrant within one turn. After 180 s a waiting message is answered `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` instead of starting (tests/test_turn_lease.py:72, tests/test_turn_lease.py:118, tests/test_turn_lease.py:104). The lease table is capped at 1024 entries and prunes unlocked locks when full (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1730, tests/test_turn_lease.py:163). The `_active_session` ContextVar (agents/core/orchestrator.py:305) keeps concurrent turns from reading or writing each other's session (tests/test_concurrent_session_isolation.py:93). Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability.
reviews.remaining: No run generation lets a late callback from an abandoned turn detect that it no longer owns the session. The only compare-and-set is the checkpoint-clock commit of a compaction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4052), and it guards a summary, not turn ownership. There is no active-session slot claimed before the first await and no `max_concurrent_sessions` cap: turns on different sessions run concurrently without bound (tests/test_turn_lease.py:88). No watchdog evicts a session whose turn is wedged: its lease stays held until the turn ends, and later messages only get the busy reply. There is no eviction of an in-memory slot whose durable routing row ended, and no single per-session `SessionState` object with explicit lifetimes. There is no per-session warm agent cache and no memory-pressure eviction. Agents are process-wide: every session shares `orchestrator.agents`, which the compaction-boundary persona refresh walks as a whole (agents/core/orchestrator.py:446).

Of the outbound-rendering set, only streaming edits exist, and only on Telegram. `TelegramDraft` in agents/core/channels/telegram.py sends the first token as a message, then edits it at most once per `STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL` (1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; `finish()` settles the final text in the edited message, sends the overflow as new messages and retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text. `Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft` opens a draft only for an adapter whose descriptor declares `supports_edit`, while the Settings DB toggle `channels.streaming_replies` is on and the delivery router would send, and never for Slack or Discord: their workspace replies are governed `channel.reply` approvals delivered whole through `render_outbound` after approval (tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py `test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens`, tests/test_telegram_streaming.py). The Telegram chat-action indicator (`send_action`) is sent only while an attachment is read (`typing` in `_read_attachment`) and while a spoken reply is synthesized (`record_voice` in `_speak`). Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. reviews.remaining: The reduced set the row accepted beyond streaming is absent: no long-running 'still working, N min' message on a chat channel while a slow turn runs (`TURN_BUSY_REPLY` only answers a second message sent while a turn holds the session); no `tool_progress: log` per-turn append-only record of which tools ran; no quiet/show-tools level with a tool-progress message and its cleanup after the final answer, and no `/verbose`-style chat command to switch it (the slash-command registry has help, status, sessions, pause, stop, resume, jobs, remind and voice); no typing indicator on an ordinary text turn; no single RO/EN reply-string catalog: the decision-inbox cards still hardcode Romanian labels (`✅ Aprob`, `❌ Resping`) while channel notes and slash-command replies are English. Neither Slack nor Discord implements an edit call — no `begin_stream`, Slack posts only through `chat_postMessage`, Discord has no message PATCH — although both descriptors declare `supports_edit=True`, so the edit path is missing as well as the approval contract below. Slack and Discord replies are not streamed until one edit stream can be approved as a single `channel.reply` decision (H104). The missing typing indicator on an ordinary text turn is counted once, under H683's acknowledge-at-ingest gap.

reviews.summary: Un mesaj vocal pe Telegram e transcris înainte să-l vadă agentul — echivalentul lui `stt_enabled` din Hermes. `InboundVoiceReader` întreabă poarta înainte de descărcare, mărginește octeții, îi trimite prin `BytesIO` direct la decodor (vorbirea nu atinge discul) și transformă fiecare eșec într-un motiv numit; santinelele motorului nu ajung niciodată la model ca vorbire. Transcriptul circulă ca o tură obișnuită, nu în gard: sunt chiar cuvintele expeditorului, iar protecția reală e filtrul de halucinații (H530). Jumătatea rostită: `/voice off|voice|always` e mod per conversație (`voice_mode.py`, magazie JSON `canal:chat`, implicit off, setat de chat pentru chat), `stt_echo_transcripts` e setarea `voice.stt_echo_transcripts` (o linie de serviciu „am auzit: …” înaintea răspunsului, niciodată rostită), iar `spoken_reply.py` transformă textul livrat într-o notă vocală peste motorul TTS al gazdei — doar proza (fără cod, linkuri, marcaje), tăiată la o limită de propoziție, fișierul șters după citire, nimic din text în log. Cârligul stă unde textul chiar ajunge (`send()` și `finish()` al draftului în flux), deci modul nu poate livra ca audio ce ruterul n-ar fi livrat ca text; orice eșec costă nota vocală, niciodată textul; un 400 pe `sendVoice` reîncearcă o dată ca `sendAudio`. `/voice` numește motorul care ar vorbi și spune „cloud” când e edge-tts. Reevaluarea inițială a raportat 15/15 mutanți uciși; numărul nu a fost reprodus la recitirea din 2026-09-22.
reviews.remaining: Consumatorul TTS în flux care începe să rostească propozițiile terminate cât timp modelul încă generează (nota vocală se sintetizează după răspunsul complet). Intrarea/ieșirea dintr-un canal de voce pe Discord e sărită deliberat de rândul original (funcție de comunitate, nu de asistent). Doar Telegram: pe Slack/Discord replica trece prin brokerul `channel.reply`, fără audio. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun mesaj vocal Telegram adevărat, niciun model Whisper încărcat, niciun `sendVoice` real — Telegram acceptă `.mp3` ca mesaj vocal după documentație, iar căderea pe `sendAudio` e plasa pentru cazul în care nu.

Edit-based streaming replies exist on Telegram. `TelegramDraft` in agents/core/channels/telegram.py sends the first token as a message and edits it in place at most once per `STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL` (1.2 s), skipping frames whose visible text did not change; the preview is capped below the message limit, and `finish()` writes the first chunk of the final text into the edited message and sends the overflow as continuation messages, retrying rejected markup as plain text and falling back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. `TelegramChannel.begin_stream` returns a draft only for a chat id; `Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft` opens it only when the adapter's descriptor declares `supports_edit`, the Settings DB toggle `channels.streaming_replies` is on and the delivery router would send to that source; observed group messages never open one and a draft that never started falls back to the normal send (tests/test_telegram_streaming.py). Slack and Discord are refused a draft on purpose: their workspace replies are governed `channel.reply` approvals delivered whole after approval, and edit support alone cannot publish unapproved tokens (tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py `test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens`). Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. reviews.remaining: Neither Slack nor Discord implements an edit call — no `begin_stream`, Slack posts only through `chat_postMessage`, Discord has no message PATCH — although both descriptors declare `supports_edit=True`, so the edit path is missing as well as the approval contract below. Slack and Discord replies are not streamed: both descriptors declare `supports_edit`, but `_begin_channel_draft` refuses them because the row's governance clause requires one edit stream to be a single `channel.reply` approval decision and no such contract exists yet; until it does, their replies arrive whole after approval. The Matrix adapter (`MatrixChannel`, a webhook channel), another edit-capable platform the rationale names, posts whole `m.room.message` events: its descriptor does not declare `supports_edit` and it has no edit (`m.replace`) or draft path.

reviews.summary: Telegram photos are read, not only recognised. `classify` (agents/core/channels/inbound_media.py) recognises the ten attachment kinds in `RECOGNISED_KINDS` and turns a missing file handle, a declared size above the 20 MB bot ceiling or an unreadable kind into a named reason, so the sender gets one plain line from `describe` instead of silence. `InboundImageReader` (agents/core/channels/media_reader.py) describes a photo through a proven-local VLM and hands the description to the turn as data, never as instructions. Locality follows the `screen_locator` rule: `is_local` derives only from `resolve_vlm_config().is_local`, `TelegramChannel._read_image` asks `refusal()` before any download, and `_backend_call` checks again against the `VLMBackend` built for the URL it will actually post to, so a non-loopback VLM receives no bytes. `_download_file` bounds the transfer by the bytes that actually arrive, not by the sender-chosen `file_size`, and `_safe_file_path` rejects any `getFile` path that is not Telegram-shaped before it enters the bot-token URL. The description is folded to one line, capped and wrapped in the Wave 5a `fence_tool_result` fence, deliberately without the `spotlight` datamark, which would replace spaces with '▁' and blind the gateway's `detect_injection`; a photo with '<<END UNTRUSTED>>' written on it cannot close its own fence. The caption never reaches the describer: it travels separately as the sender's question. The turn goes through the normal door, so `Gateway._inbound_meta` marks it `inbound:telegram` and runs the detector over exactly what the model reads. Voice notes are read on the other path: a transcript is the sender's own words and travels unfenced as an ordinary turn (`inbound_voice`, row H071). `ChannelDescriptor` separates `recognises_media` from `reads_media` with the subset invariant checked at construction, and `READABLE_KINDS` is exactly {photo, voice}.
reviews.remaining: Only photos and voice notes, only on Telegram. Not delivered: reading audio files, video, video notes, animations, documents and stickers (recognised, answered with 'reading … is not wired up yet'); a disk cache under a media directory so vision tools can open a local path (bytes stay in memory for one call); location and venue pins (recognised as `location`, deliberately not echoed, not read); caching of media from observed group messages and from replied-to messages; media ingestion on WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Google Chat and email (those adapters pass text only). Documented limitation, not solved: taint cannot be tracked through the model; what travels is the coarse fact that the turn read untrusted material, and the channel's `inbound` origin is what keeps an action derived from a photo in approval. `mark_turn_recall_tainted()` is not called here because it would be a no-op (escalate-only over an already untrusted origin). UNVERIFIED on real services: the suite is hermetic; no real Telegram message received, no local VLM actually called, `getFile` and the download exercised only against a fake client.

Streaming is therefore derived from capabilities: ntfy, email and other non-editable channels never receive streamed partial output, and Slack and Discord are excluded outright. The hub's own log is readable from the UI. GET /api/admin/logs (agents/core/routers/admin.py:645) is admin-only and read-only; it reads off the event loop and answers a refused filter with 400, its reason and no-store. Behind it, agents/core/log_tail.py reads the file the hub's own setup_logging actually opened, or reports the error it met (FILE_LOG_STATE, agents/core/log.py:19; _writer_state, agents/core/log_tail.py:95), falling back to the configuration for a process that never set logging up ($JARVIS_LOG_FILE, else data_path('logs','jarvis.log') with system.log_to_file: configured_log, agents/core/log_tail.py:86). It lists only that file and its rotations named with ASCII digits, and only regular files by lstat, so a link, a pipe or a directory is never listed (list_files, agents/core/log_tail.py:114; _listed, agents/core/log_tail.py:105); a file is chosen by one of those names, and it is opened without following a link or blocking and checked to be a regular file (_read_window, agents/core/log_tail.py:197). The read is bounded: at most the last 4 MiB, read in one go and closed before parsing, at most 500 records, each at most 8,000 characters (read_path, agents/core/log_tail.py:279). Lines are grouped into records by the log format's header, so a traceback stays with its error: a record over the limit keeps its header and its newest lines behind a "[… N lines not shown]" marker, so the error line is always there; lines above the first header read (a record whose header rotated away, a file not in the log format) are records of their own, beyond the window too. Filters: File, a minimum Level (WARNING shows WARNING, ERROR and CRITICAL; a line with no level is not shown under a floor), a Component (a logger and its children) and Lines (1-500), decided on the record as written, so only returned records are redacted. Redaction runs on every returned field, each line whole before anything is cut, so a secret is never split into a visible half: the H495 secret scanner, an assignment rule for names ending like a credential (`SMTP_PASS=`, `?token=`, `password:`), and the known values of the process's secret-named environment variables and encrypted settings, so it masks at least what /api/admin/env masks (_Redactor, agents/core/log_tail.py:159; _known_secret_values, agents/core/log_tail.py:137); when the scanner cannot be loaded nothing is shown, with a note (_redactor, agents/core/log_tail.py:181; _record, agents/core/log_tail.py:251). Terminal escape sequences, C0 and C1 controls and bidirectional overrides are removed (_clean, agents/core/log_tail.py:190). The answer carries the components seen (redacted), the bytes scanned and whether only part of the file was read, and an honest note: file logging off and how to turn it on, a file the hub could not open at start, no file yet, or a file that may no longer be written (read_log, agents/core/log_tail.py:327). The HUD's Logs panel (frontend/src/panels/logs.tsx:54, registered in the Console's Observe group) has the File / Level / Component / Lines filters, colours records by level (ERROR/CRITICAL red, WARNING amber, DEBUG muted/readable), shows them newest first as text, never markup, auto-refreshes every 5 s while switched on and the page is visible, skipping a tick while a read is in flight and stopping on a refused credential, shows LIVE only while the hub writes its file, shows no old records after a refused filter (and goes back to the current log when a rotation is gone), and names the admin token on a 401 or 403. `nerva logs -n N` (cmd_logs, agents/cli/nerva.py:1329) reads the same bounded, redacted tail (N counts records), says when only part was read, and refuses cleanly on an unreadable file or a missing redactor. tests/test_log_tail.py (33 cases) covers the resolution and the off state, rotations and refused names, records and tracebacks, the caps, the level floor and component children, the byte budget, a partial last line, bytes that are not UTF-8, control characters, redaction (current file, rotation, traceback line, filtered fields), the route and the CLI; tests/test_h145b_log_review.py (32) covers the first review: a secret across the cut (four offsets, and in a continuation line), a long traceback keeping its error line, links and a link swapped in after listing, a pipe, secret-named environment values and credential assignments (and ordinary numbers left alone), a redactor that cannot load (route and CLI), C1 and bidi controls, filtering before redaction, the writer's error and its path, setup_logging's record, no file yet, plain lines beyond the window, the 4 MiB budget, level-less lines under a floor, component redaction, the CLI's records, window note and -n 0, rotation names, a directory and the 400's no-store; frontend/src/test/logs-panel.test.tsx (14) covers the registration, the query, the admin read, order and colours, each filter, the 5 s auto-refresh, a tick skipped in flight, a hidden page, stale records after a refusal, LIVE only while writing, the off note, no match and a partial read, 401 and 403, a kept component and text-only rendering. The first review (two majors: a secret split by the cut came back in part, and a long traceback lost its error line; ten minors; nine nits) is answered; the feature's 29 mutants were caught but one equivalent, and this round's 26, all but one equivalent (the regular-file check after open, which lseek or read also enforces), two after their cases were added (a pipe, the partial first line). Test manual: PNB-169, PNB-170; the API sweep lists the route. An agent's persona can now be edited in the UI and is live on its next turn. That is Hermes' persona editor, over the version history Nerva already kept. Until now the history was a side record: a commit or rollback in the Prompts panel changed a JSON file while the agent kept its old persona. agents/core/soul_edit.py holds the one path an edit takes, apply_soul (:152). (1) Refusals. An agent the hub has not loaded is refused (404; agent_folder, :100, returns an enumerated folder name in the id alphabet, so no request value reaches a path). So is text over MAX_SOUL_BYTES (256 KiB of UTF-8, :40; 413), safe mode (:171; 409, because overlays are not read there, H275) and a persona the H387 guard would drop (:174; 422 with the verdict). guard_verdict (:60) runs the same scan and cap as Agent._load_soul, and GET /api/agents/{id}/soul now reports it through the same function. A line the guard only quarantines is applied, and the verdict names it. (2) Nothing live is lost. The first edit keeps the file on disk as v1 ("on disk before the first edit"). A file changed on disk since the last version, such as a hand edit, is kept as its own version ("on disk, changed outside the editor") before it is replaced (:185). An agent with no persona file has nothing to keep. (3) Written where the model reads it. The text goes to the owner's overlay (overlay_path, :115): souls/<id>/SOUL.local.md in the data home, else the repo-local SOUL.local.md, never the shipped SOUL.md. The write is atomic (_write_atomically, :126: temporary file, fsync, replace; a failure leaves no temporary file and records no new version). (4) Versioned, then live. The text is committed (:195; the same text twice is one version). The agent re-reads its persona (_load_soul, :197), and the result says whether the running agent now reads the written file. (5) Audited without the text. A SETTINGS_CHANGE row names the agent, the version and its hash. Every configuration key is reachable and searchable from the UI, and every one but a secret or a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) is portable and resettable. The backend it builds on: `GET /api/admin/settings` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:73) returns every category, and the per-category PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:194) validates with `validate_category` and answers 422 before any write, auditing the changed key names and the new value of a choice only (`_audited_values`, agents/core/routers/admin.py:124). New in H157: `GET /api/admin/settings/export` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:78, registered before the `/{category}` read so it is never taken for one) returns the declared settings as a `nerva-settings/1` document with an attachment disposition, leaving out every secret (encrypted at rest, or named like a token, secret, password, client id or API key), `mcp.servers` (it holds credentials by design) any URL that carries a password (`http://user:pw@host`, in a list too), and any free-form value the H495 secret scanner would mask (or every free-form value, when the scanner cannot run), and naming each left-out setting with its reason (export_settings, agents/core/settings_db.py:1064; is_secret_setting, agents/core/settings_db.py:1010; _looks_like_credential, agents/core/settings_db.py:1043; _url_password, agents/core/settings_db.py:1027). `POST /api/admin/settings/import` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:325) takes such a document (at most 1 MB and 1,000 keys, the body counted as it streams in, so a chunked upload is bounded too: _bounded_body, agents/core/routers/admin.py:312). The import and the reset take only an `application/json` request (415 otherwise, a type a browser must pre-check before sending) and refuse one the browser marks cross-site (403), since the admin guard trusts loopback on a default install (_refuse_cross_site_write, agents/core/routers/admin.py:298); every reply is no-store, and only a JSON `true` makes a dry run. A NaN, an Infinity or nesting too deep to store is refused (422), never stored, an `mcp.servers` entry needs a name (validate_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:870, via _mcp_servers_problem, agents/core/settings_db.py:933; the loader skips a nameless entry too, MCPManager.load_from_config, agents/core/mcp/client.py:814), and 2000 and 2000.0 are the same number, so no change (_same_value, agents/core/settings_db.py:1152). In the document every key must be declared and passes the same `validate_category` a single write does, so a posture flag or an out-of-range value is refused like any other; one refusal and nothing is written (422 with every reason) (plan_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:1096). Only the keys whose value differs are written, in one sqlite transaction, all or nothing, secrets encrypted as a single write encrypts them (apply_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:1186), with one audit row naming the settings (and the new value of a choice); `"dry_run": true` answers what would change, a secret's values shown as `(secret)` and a credential-shaped free value as `(hidden)`, so the preview never echoes one (describe_changes, agents/core/settings_db.py:1160). `POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:391) puts one category back to its declared values and names the keys that moved, with an audit row; it keeps the category's secrets and its route-only rows (the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and names them (kept, reset_kept, agents/core/settings_db.py:1202; the HUD counts every kept row as a secret) and names the settings the product posture still forces (overridden, posture_overridden, agents/core/settings_db.py:1211), where the global reseed (agents/core/routers/admin.py:430) was the only reset (reset_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:1306). The v2 console SettingsPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2751; widgets typed by settingsField, frontend/src/gap.tsx:2728) now has a search across every category matching a setting's category.key or label, with a match count and an honest no-match line (settingMatches, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:37); a reset per category heading (only one with declared rows) that asks first, by a second click that names how many settings go back and moves the focus to itself, drops the category's unsaved edits once it runs and names what was kept and what the posture still forces (ResetCategory, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:92); edits hidden by the search are counted beside the save; and a MOVE A CONFIGURATION section (SettingsTransfer, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:187) that downloads the export and names what the hub left out, and imports a pasted or chosen file by showing the hub's dry run (each change old → new) and applying it only on a second step, listing every reason on a refusal; a pasted `dry_run` is dropped so the apply step is never a dry run, the text is held while the hub answers, and the file picker is reachable from the keyboard. The standalone /admin app's GlobalConfigPage (agents/web/static/admin.js:447) is unchanged, and `nerva config list|get|set|check` (cmd_config, agents/cli/nerva.py:863) still edits single keys offline. tests/test_settings_transfer.py (28 cases) covers the export (every declared key either exported or named as left out, secrets, client ids, mcp.servers, a token-shaped value, a scanner that cannot run, the stored value), the import (an export imports back as no change, valid changes, every refusal a single write makes, nothing written on one refusal, one transaction, the posture flag, a secret encrypted and never echoed, the bound), the per-category reset, and the routes (admin only, the export not read as a category, preview then apply with one audit row, every reason on a refusal, no row when nothing changes, reset and 404); tests/test_h157b_settings_review.py (30, the first review) covers the JSON-only and cross-site refusals, URL passwords, a credential in a list, the hidden preview, NaN, Infinity and deep nesting, nameless MCP servers, number equality, secrets kept on a reset, the posture's settings named, the change listeners, the 1 MB bound for a sized and a chunked body and the JSON-only dry run; frontend/src/test/settings-tools.test.tsx (12) covers the search, the two-step reset, the export note, the dry-run preview and the second-step apply with the admin credential, a refusal's reasons, text that is not JSON, an import that changes nothing, a reset that drops unsaved edits and names kept secrets, edits hidden by the search, a pasted dry run never applied and the keyboard-reachable file button. 25 backend mutants, all caught (one after its case was added: a scanner that cannot run). reviews.summary: Governed SSH terminal execution remains available only for declared, enabled targets. The runner applies hardline, audited target policy, durable approval, the terminal.exec contract and Action Kernel before the built-in SSH transport; the transport reconstructs a quoted remote argv, pins known hosts, requires key authentication, bypasses user SSH config and agent, and disables forwarding and ControlMaster (agents/core/environments/execution.py:156-224,380-394,614-742; agents/core/environments/ssh_transport.py:310-344,346-410). reviews.remaining: Rândul cere mult peste execuție și restul nu e livrat: manager de conexiuni ControlMaster, erori clasificate, sugestii de gazde din ~/.ssh/config, bootstrap care refolosește-sau-pornește un serviciu remote, revalidare de liveness, tranzacție de update cu jurnal de recuperare și linii de restore per profil, fan-out "update all instances". ControlMaster e o divergență deliberată, nu o scăpare: un socket de control partajat e un canal autentificat reutilizabil lăsat pe disc, iar transportul îl dezactivează explicit. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: nicio sesiune SSH reală nu a fost deschisă din această livrare — suita e ermetică, fără socket și fără binar ssh, deci interoperabilitatea cu un sshd real rămâne nedovedită.

reviews.summary: Default-off per-turn keep-awake with host.control gate, refcount and release. Battery/resume state via guarded snapshot/SSE, scheduled tick and background job deferral. Desktop background-throttling policy on both webviews. Current verification: 75 passed, 1 rustc skip; power-chip Vitest passed in 23-test group; no native Windows/systemd/macOS acceptance.
reviews.remaining: Windows keep-awake state can be falsely reported active: _windows_set_state ignores SetThreadExecutionState return value (zero means failure), while KeepAwake._start unconditionally sets _win_held=True (agents/core/power.py:173-177, :280-283). SetThreadExecutionState is per calling thread, but acquire/release may execute on different turn/shutdown threads; release on another thread may not clear the original assertion. Use one owning thread or a host-supported process-level mechanism, validate return and release on that owner; cover failure and cross-thread behavior. Host-bound systemd/macOS/Windows and browser background behavior has no live acceptance in this review; H182 cannot be claimed fully equivalent from mocks alone.

Built in #1207 together with H153 (critic note 7: one spec, one panel), then fixed after an adversarial review. The v2 console has a Webhooks panel, WebhooksPanel (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:187), registered in the Interop group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:50; frontend/src/gap.tsx:5069). Interop mode's WEBHOOKS list links to it by an accessible name (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:341). Every panel call sends the admin credential. The backend stays admin-only CRUD: list, create, switch and delete all carry Depends(admin_guard) (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:175, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:181, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:194, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:221).

Interop mode is built from its four sources alone (hydrateInterop, frontend/src/api/live.ts:126). All four (A2A peers, MCP servers, widgets, webhooks) are admin-only routes and are fetched with the admin credential, and so is the webhooks settings category: while the receiver switch is off every webhook row reads "receiver off", and a switch it could not read is said under WEBHOOKS (frontend/src/api/live.ts:119, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:342). A section whose source failed is empty and says "not connected", and an empty real list says "none" (Section, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:302); the demo seed's rows are never shown under the LIVE chip. When no source answers nothing is overwritten, so the mode stays "Not connected" and DEMO keeps its seed. The review found that fetching only the webhooks list with the credential had marked the whole mode LIVE over seeded peers, MCP servers and widgets.

The five accepted parts:
(1) Create dialog: name, agent or workflow target, target id and an HMAC-signed toggle, and, since H153, a description, an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only, posted to POST /api/webhooks. A refusal shows the hub's own reason, and an empty target is refused before any request. The create button is held while the call is pending and while a new hook's credentials are on screen, so a second hook cannot replace a secret before it was saved.
(2) Created result, shown once (Reveal, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:145): the absolute trigger URL (triggerUrl, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:52: the page origin, the base path and the encoded id), and the token, or the signing secret for a signed hook, each with a copy button that says "copied" in a polite live region, plus the header the sender must send. Only the warning sentence is an alert, so a screen reader does not read the secret aloud. On a loopback origin it says a sender elsewhere needs an address it can reach. The secret lives only in the panel's state and is dropped on "I have saved it" (focus returns to the create form) or unmount. The list never carries it: WebhookStore masks the token to a 4-character hint (agents/core/webhooks.py:635).
(3) Detail pane: clicking a hook expands its trigger URL, auth header (with the token hint), calls, last call and creation time, the deliveries its event list skipped and the last event skipped, and an editor for its event list and prompt template (H153). The row shows target_type:target, an HMAC or token badge, an on/off badge and an event-count badge.
(4) Delete with confirmation: "delete…" arms an inline confirmation that explains the sender's credential dies with the hook and moves focus to "delete for good", which sends DELETE; "keep it" returns focus to "delete…". Each row button's accessible name includes the hook's name. A row's buttons are held while its call is pending, and every switch or delete reloads the list whatever the hub answered: a hook already deleted elsewhere is reported as gone ("ci was already deleted", "ci no longer exists") and its row disappears, with focus moved to the create form; a refused delete keeps the confirmation and says why. A per-hook on/off switch (PATCH, H153) is offered as the reversible alternative.
(5) Governance: creating, switching and deleting a hook each write a SecurityEvent (_audit_webhook, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:143, called at agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:190, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:215 and agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:227). It names the hook id, the target as a JSON string (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:137), so a target cannot pass its own text off as the row's id or flags, and the signed and enabled flags as the store reads them, never the token or signing secret. A delete of an unknown id writes nothing and answers 404 "webhook not found".

The receiver-disabled banner: when the receiver switch (H153, the setting webhooks.receiver_enabled) is off, the panel's receiver row says every delivery is refused until it is switched back on (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:352). The restart-gateway banner is not needed: a delivery sees the switch at most a second old (at once after a write in this process), and hook CRUD is served live; the receiver row says so. Not built, and not part of this row: a `nerva webhooks` CLI verb (critic note 7 places it with H409, as `nerva webhooks inbound|outbound`) and a mobile screen.

reviews.remaining: Both gaps the rationale accepts are absent. (1) Per-agent skill enable/disable as a capability grant: the permission ledger's SURFACES (agents/core/permission_ledger.py:69) has no skill surface. reviews.summary: The HUD's keyboard shortcuts live in one registry, as in Hermes. frontend/src/shortcuts.ts defines every action once (ACTIONS: id, category, label, default chord, scope): the ten mode keys, World (w), the Console (`), Ambient (a), Cinema (m) and its three stages (o, n, b, scope cinema), focus the message box (/), the command palette (mod+k) and the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (mod+/). app.tsx (World's key included: WorldAwareApp passes onWorld and shares the live overrides through useShortcutOverrides) and the cinema overlay in shell.tsx dispatch through matchAction over bindings(overrides) instead of literal key maps, and every key hint (palette, top bar, World, Console, cinema stages) is read from the registry (chordOf, displayChord). A matched action takes the key from the browser (preventDefault); Shift+letter falls back to the bare letter unless it is bound itself. frontend/src/shortcuts-panel.tsx is the panel mod+/ opens: categories Navigation, View, Composer and Session with search (searchBindings); click a chord to record a new one ("Press a key…", Esc cancels, a lone modifier keeps listening; chordFromEvent, rebind); the palette and the panel take only a chord held with Ctrl/⌘ or Alt (acceptsChord), fire in an input only then (firesInInputs), and the palette always has a Keyboard shortcuts entry, so no rebinding can lock the panel out; Space is spelled "space", and a chord with no key is refused on record and on read; Esc closes the panel without closing what lies beneath; per-binding reset and Reset all (resetBinding); an "Also bound to X" note when two actions share a chord (conflictsFor). Overrides persist per viewer in localStorage under hud.shortcuts, validated on read (readOverrides, loadOverrides, saveOverrides), and survive storage that is off. Governance: defineActions refuses any action whose id, category or label names an approval, a decision, an accept, reject, deny or consent (FORBIDDEN_TARGET), so no chord can reach a Decision Inbox action. Archived chats exist, as in Hermes. CheckpointManager.set_archived stamps or clears archived_at in a session's metadata without creating a session. get_sessions(archived=...) filters on it in SQL, read only from valid JSON, so the limit counts only the view asked for. agents/core/routers/sessions.py serves several routes. GET /sessions leaves archived chats out; ?archived=true lists only them, each row with archived_at. POST /sessions/{id}/archive and /unarchive (user_guard) are 404 for an unknown session and 400 for an invalid id. Resuming a chat through POST /sessions/resume unarchives it. agents/core/session_archive.py holds the rest. run_auto_archive archives sessions whose ended_at, else started_at, is older than memory.auto_archive_days (0 = off, at most 3650) and never touches the active one; SchedulerService.schedule_auto_archive runs it daily at 03:40. DELETE /sessions/{id}?confirm=DELETE (admin_guard) holds the session's turn lease (409 session_busy) and the memory locks. It refuses the chat in use (409), a chat another chat continues (409 has_continuations), and an id that is not a session or whose snapshot is not this session's (404). delete_session first writes an encrypted, fsynced, read-back backup (the backup cipher, key under JARVIS_KEY_DIR) of the session's rows (session, checkpoints, clock, continuation seed, history binding), transcript snapshot and log (unreadable ones byte for byte), compaction archive, checklist and note. The backup goes to <data root>-forget-archives/sessions/<id>-<stamp>.json.enc, outside the data root, keeping the newest JARVIS_SESSION_BACKUP_KEEP=10. Only then does it delete them and clear the live conversation, with the chat's turn embeddings (VectorStore.remove_where; 503 recall_unavailable if the store cannot) and with secure_delete plus a WAL truncate. Facts already extracted into the knowledge graph, and the audit log, are not touched. A backup that does not land raises backup_failed and deletes nothing. The file work runs off the event loop. The HUD SessionsPanel (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx) has chats and archived tabs, archive, unarchive and a two-step "delete permanently" that names the backup. llm.project_dir only sets the folder whose convention files H594 reads (project_context.start_dir); file tools (FileScope.resolve, list_dir, search_files) and the terminal cwd still resolve relative paths from the first file root, and the setting's label says so. Hermes' "what can it do right now" view is here: one read-only answer, for one agent as seen by one principal, built from the code a turn runs and served on three surfaces. agents/core/inspector.py holds it; build_inspector (:108) returns up to five sections (SECTIONS, :63). (1) Views. VIEWS (:56) names the five tool-profile postures: the owner and a guest on the HUD (owner, guest), the owner and a stranger on an external channel (inbound-owner, inbound; Telegram stands for every channel, under the inbound action origin a real channel turn has) and no human (internal). The look binds that principal and origin in a task of its own (:125), so nothing it binds, and nothing the runtime notes while resolving the offer, outlives it. (2) status (_status, :155): version, the backend and model the router serves, the local model's state through project_llm_status, the transcript budget llm.tool_loop_context_tokens (0 reads as 75 % of the model window), the tool loop and safe mode. (3) tools (_tools, :194): the tool runtime's own resolved offer for the agent under that principal (_resolve_offer: registry or the capability registry's view, job toolset, posture, the agent's tools: list, the shared-session rule), not the raw registry. Each row says whether the tool is gated and whether its output is fenced as untrusted, with the description cut to DESCRIPTION_CHARS (160, :65). The withheld names are listed, a resolver failure offers nothing, and loop_enabled says whether the model sees any of them (with the loop off they are what the posture would offer). (4) skills (_skills, :215): the rows prompt_catalog gives the prompt under that principal and that offer, or none when llm.skills_in_prompt is off. (5) mcp (_mcp, :225): each server's transport, trust tier, transport-aware liveness (is_connected, so an HTTP server reads connected; a probe that raises is down) and visible tools, with no URL or command line. (6) system_prompt (_prompt, :253): the agent's system prompt and the user part Agent.build_prompt sends for an empty user message: persona, agent context, the core-memory block, the runtime, language and grounding rails and the skills block. tokens (:266) estimates what that fixed part costs every turn before history. The texts are masked by the log redactor (SecretRedactionFilter; nothing is shown when it cannot load, _redactor :73) and capped together at PROMPT_CAP_BYTES (64 KiB, :64) on a character boundary. The core block is read with freeze=False (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3198, :3258, :3338): the frozen block when a turn froze one, else a fresh render that is not kept, so a look never fixes the day's snapshot. (7) Surfaces. GET /api/admin/inspector?agent=&view=&section= (agents/core/routers/status.py:123, admin-guarded; 404 for an unknown agent, 400 naming the views or sections, 503 before the hub is up). nerva inspect [agent] [--as VIEW] [--section tools|skills|prompt|mcp|status] [--json] (cmd_inspect, agents/cli/nerva.py:1025; render_inspector :1046) prints the same payload section by section, or as it came. The HUD's Inspector panel (frontend/src/panels/inspector.tsx, Console → Admin) reads the same route with a status line, an As switch and folding sections. It covers the guest's tools equal to ToolProfileResolver's set and not the registry, every view's posture and bindings, the agent's list, the marks and the cut, the loop off, a failing resolver, an unwired runtime, the skills, the prompt (skills block, core memory, rails, empty message, tokens), the unfrozen core block, masking, the withheld prompt, the 64 KiB cap on a split character, no leaked binding, MCP liveness, the status line and safe mode, section order, the route (payload, defaults, refusals, admin token, guard snapshot, 503) and the CLI (--json equal to the payload, rendering, --section, the loop-off line, the tree, one list of views and sections). frontend/src/panels/inspector.test.tsx has 4. 82 mutants: 79 caught, ten after survivors got cases. Nerva now knows which surface holds each microphone. A surface arms only if the owner allowed its kind; one device's microphone has one holder at a time; and arming, pausing, resuming and stopping carry the surface's identity and are audited. This is the adaptation's missing concept, on top of the voice primitives that already existed (wake word, push-to-talk and hands-free capture, TTS, STT, capabilities, and H222's listening indicator). The lease table is agents/core/voice/mic.py (MicArbiter, agents/core/voice/mic.py:93; one process-wide ARBITER, agents/core/voice/mic.py:232).
(1) Surfaces and devices. A surface is kind:client: host:hub (the hub's own wake-word pipeline), hud:<tab> or mobile:<device> (ARMABLE, agents/core/voice/mic.py:39). A Wyoming satellite has its own microphone and is not armed here. A lease is for one device. host is the machine the hub runs on, and a browser that the route sees on loopback shares it. The route decides that from the address a trusted proxy vouches for (_mic_device, agents/core/routers/voice.py:527), so a LAN client cannot claim to be local. Otherwise a browser gets remote:hud:<tab>, and every phone gets mobile:<device>.
(2) One holder per device. A second surface arming a held device is refused, naming the holder (MicRefused mic_busy, agents/core/voice/mic.py:49; HTTP 409). With take_over, it pauses the holder and tells it (on_change, agents/core/voice/mic.py:144). A pause frees the device (agents/core/voice/mic.py:199). A resume asks again, both for consent and for the device's holder (agents/core/voice/mic.py:212). A stop releases the lease (agents/core/voice/mic.py:221).
(3) Consent. A kind arms only if the setting voice.mic_surfaces allows it (allowed_kinds, agents/core/voice/mic.py:59). The setting is a declared tags setting whose values are validated against host, hud and mobile (agents/core/settings_db.py:219, :902). The default is hud and mobile (DEFAULT_ALLOWED, agents/core/voice/mic.py:40): surfaces someone uses on purpose. The hub's always-on listener needs host added. So VoiceChannel.start (agents/core/channels/voice.py:29) opens the host microphone only with a lease. Before this, it started at boot with no check. It stops the pipeline when taken over and starts it again when given back (_on_lease, agents/core/channels/voice.py:48). Withdrawn consent ends a lease at its next renewal.
(4) Leases lapse. A browser or phone lease lapses LEASE_SECONDS (45, agents/core/voice/mic.py:42) after its last renewal (_expire_locked, agents/core/voice/mic.py:108). The host pipeline's lease does not lapse. The table holds at most 32 leases.
(5) Audit. Every arm, take-over, pause, stop and refusal is one audit row naming the surface and the device. A renewal is not.
(6) Routes, all user-guarded. GET /api/voice/mic answers who holds each device, the paused leases and the allowed kinds (agents/core/routers/voice.py:548). POST /api/voice/mic/arm (agents/core/routers/voice.py:557) takes hud or mobile and answers 403 or 409. /pause, /resume and /stop act on a lease by name (agents/core/routers/voice.py:576, agents/core/routers/voice.py:587, agents/core/routers/voice.py:601).
(7) The HUD. The voice loop arms its lease before getUserMedia (frontend/src/voice.ts:414; armMic, frontend/src/mic-lease.ts:47) and renews it every 20 s (frontend/src/voice.ts:434). It releases the lease on every end of the loop (frontend/src/voice.ts:135). If a renewal is refused, it stops and says who took the microphone. Only a hub refusal blocks: a hub that cannot answer does not. The loop offers take over (takeOver, frontend/src/voice.ts:454; the voice pill, frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:255). The voice settings list the holders, with pause, resume and stop (MicLeases, frontend/src/mic-leases.tsx:17).
Tests: tests/test_h247_mic_lease.py has 27. They cover consent, kinds, client and device names, withdrawn consent, a conflict and a take-over, renewal, lapse, pause and resume, stop, the bound, status, the numbers, the setting and its reading, the voice channel's lease, loopback against LAN against a phone, the routes and their guard. frontend/src/test/mic-lease.test.tsx has 10: arm before the mic, a named holder and take-over, no consent, an unreachable hub, renewal and loss, a cancelled start, an unmount, a click handler, the pill and the settings list.

A settings reset now shows what it will change, never touches a secret and can be undone, and the HUD marks every setting that differs from its default. Hermes' config-reset and defaults surface is covered, on top of H157's search, secret-free export, dry-run import and per-category reset. (1) Defaults. Every declared row that is not a secret carries its declared default (agents/core/settings_db.py:618, in _mark_overlay :608, used by GET /api/admin/settings and each category read). A secret carries none. The Settings panel marks a row whose value, or staged edit, differs from its default ("changed", with the default in its tooltip); a ↺ button stages the default and the usual save writes it through the validated PUT (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2853). (2) A preview before any reset. plan_reset (agents/core/settings_db.py:1263) computes what a reset of one category, or of every category, would write: each declared setting that is neither a secret nor a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and whose stored value is not its default. POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset and POST /api/admin/settings/reseed take {"dry_run": true} and answer the changes as current → default without writing anything (agents/core/routers/admin.py:391, :430; _dry_run_asked, :379; only a JSON true, in a body of at most 4 KB). The changes use describe_changes, so a credential-shaped value shows as (hidden). Arming the reset in the HUD asks for that preview and lists it, and counts the settings kept (secrets and route-only rows, all labelled secrets) and names the settings the posture still forces (ResetPreview, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:64; ResetCategory, :92). (3) The reseed no longer deletes the store. It used to run DELETE FROM settings, wiping every setting, secrets included, with no preview and no way back. It is now the per-category reset over every category: secrets and route-only rows are kept (and named), rows nothing declares are left, it takes a JSON request from this origin only (415/403 otherwise, as H157's writes), and it is audited with the settings that moved (agents/core/routers/admin.py:430). A setting changed since that reset, one its declaration no longer accepts, or one no longer declared is left as it is and named in skipped. The undo is audited, and the listeners hear every value a reset or an undo writes, so the webhook receiver switch follows it. GET /api/admin/settings/resets (agents/core/routers/admin.py:91; list_resets, agents/core/settings_db.py:1344) lists the resets, newest first, naming settings but never their values. The HUD shows "last reset: <scope> · N settings · <time>" with "undo…" (UndoReset, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:135). Every reset and undo in the HUD is a two-step ConfirmAction at the REVERSIBLE tier (H168). Hermes' contract has two halves and Nerva has only one of them. Outbound (what a child inherits) is genuinely stronger than Hermes and is tested: scrub_child_env (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:172-210) is default-deny with SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES (:17-33) plus the three-name JARVIS_CHILD_ALLOWED_ENV (:47-51), covered by tests/test_environment_primitives.py:62,90; STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST (agents/core/mcp/client.py:161-173) with stdio_env_baseline (:245-280) drops a credential-shaped name even when it is on the static list (:275, _SECRET_LIKE :174-176), covered by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:351 — and since H502 the baseline is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in: stdio_env_baseline_enabled() returns env_flag(STDIO_ENV_BASELINE_FLAG, True) (:179-190; flag :90 "Default ON"), docs/FLAGS.md says "on by default since H502" (its MCP defaults block, the JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE entry and the flag table row), and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins unset-flag → OPENAI_API_KEY withheld and =0 → full inherit (the row previously cited :395-399 as pinning the opposite; that was the pre-#1174 test, which at 45be62bd read "Flag off (default): historical behaviour — inherit everything"). The outbound allowlist's one deliberate exception is the owner's own: a name listed in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — owner-declared and host-wide, not an inbound gate. What #1179 changed here is disclosure, not policy: the module docstring (:17-39) now names the filesystem as a second recovery route for a same-UID child (cwd defaults to the hub's, so open(".env") reaches the file the keys came from), cwd_secret_files (:215-242) reports a readable .env/.env.local in the child's cwd, and _merged_env (:561-572) logs a WARNING "withholding is undercut" (:567) beside the INFO count, filenames only — pinned by tests :830-853 and :854-890. None of it touches a name policy, a writer or the override path, so it moves nothing for this row. The fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) is likewise off-subject: it added tool_patterns_over_bounds (agents/core/mcp/client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ (:407-418) and a bounds refusal for tools_allow/tools_deny in admin_mcp_add (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:216-222); none of it reads or writes an env name, and MCPServerConfig still has no env field, so only line numbers moved (client.py +19 from the new helper on and +31 from that __init__ block on; routers/mcp.py +4 from the filter check on). LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER appear nowhere outside the research docs, but PATH and SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are MEMBERS of the two outbound allowlists — deliberately, because a child needs them as plumbing — and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 pinning that collect_tokens keeps only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
