Built in #1207, then fixed after nine adversarial reviews. The model keeps a checklist of its own work and re-reads all of it on every change. The owner can read the same list, with who wrote each item and whether its text is trusted, before any approval card it leads to.

The tool. agents/core/todo_tool.py registers `todo` on the ToolRPC server, ungated (agents/core/todo_tool.py:590), with the schema {todos: [{id, content, status, parent?}], merge} (agents/core/todo_tool.py:90); the optional parent is H666's.
- Items use Hermes' four statuses: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled. A call with todos replaces the list. With merge=true it updates items by id, changing only the fields sent, and appends new ones. A call without todos reads the list. Every call answers with the whole list and its counts.
- TodoStore.apply (agents/core/todo_tool.py:296) is bounded: at most 50 items, content of one printable line up to 200 characters, ids of 1 to 64 characters, 7,000 bytes for the whole list in the UTF-8 the tool sends it in, and at most one item in progress. A merge that only moves statuses is never refused as too long.
- Control and format characters are dropped, text is NFC, each character keeps at most three combining marks (enclosing marks included), and whitespace runs collapse. Text that renders blank (only fillers or marks) is no content; punctuation or a symbol alone is content (agents/core/todo_tool.py:136, agents/core/todo_tool.py:160-163). So what the owner reads is what was written. Two ids that are canonically equal are one id; look-alikes from another script or width stay two.
- Every refusal is named, and each comes with a sentence the model can act on: todo_too_many, todo_content_too_long, todo_content_required, todo_bad_status, todo_bad_id, todo_duplicate_id, todo_one_in_progress, todo_bad_list, todo_bad_item, todo_bad_merge, todo_no_session, todo_unknown_field (a key the schema does not have, top level or item), todo_plan_too_long and todo_shared_session. A refused call changes nothing, because a merge is built on a copy.

Whose plan it is. The coordinator passes the session, the turn's posture and whether the turn runs on the shared default session (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1066; Orchestrator.on_shared_session, agents/core/orchestrator.py:908). A turn keeps the answer it got when it resolved its session (agents/core/orchestrator.py:311), so an owner resuming another session does not let an in-flight turn in. A turn that binds no session of its own runs on that shared session, and the plan kept there is the owner's. Such turns include the HUD, the web widget (its route binds none), voice, rooms, notes, workflows, MCP ask_*, a webhook, a job, a subagent and a direct POST /api/toolrpc/call.
- On it, only an owner's turn keeps a plan. Anyone else is refused todo_shared_session and is never read the plan (agents/core/todo_tool.py:561). Neither the turn's offer nor a script's reach includes the tool for them (SESSION_SCOPED_TOOLS, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:235; agents/core/code_tools.py:362). Voice carries no identity, so even the owner's voice is a guest's turn there and keeps no plan.
- A turn on any other session keeps that session's plan, whoever it is. That covers a chat of its own and an explicit session a user token continues. Text written there by a turn that is not the owner's (a household member, a guest) is untrusted to the owner, and the owner's next turn reads it as DATA (agents/core/todo_tool.py:574).
- Otherwise it is offered like any ungated tool. An inbound guest reaches it through `llm.guest_tools`, whose default is now echo, time and todo (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:84). An install that still holds the old default (echo, time) gets the new one once, at start (agents/core/settings_db.py:560). A list the owner changed is left alone. An owner who empties it keeps guests off the tool loop entirely.
- At most 256 plans are kept in memory. The one the agent least recently wrote or read is dropped first, and an empty list frees its slot.

Where its text came from. Each item records three things: the posture of the turn that set its text (by), which turn that was, and whether it was untrusted (tainted). A turn is untrusted when it came from an inbound channel (the owner's own Telegram DM included), is not the owner's, or had already read untrusted content.
- A status set by an untrusted turn taints the item too. A clean rewrite of the text keeps the taint, in a merge or a replace alike, because the id came from whoever wrote it first (review-H315f n3). The same text again is no write, in a merge or a replace: the item keeps its writer, its turn, its taint and the plan's labels, and a status or place moved by an untrusted turn still taints it (review-H315e n2; agents/core/todo_tool.py:367). A status re-sent unchanged moves nothing in either mode.
- A call that answers with a tainted item another turn wrote says so (agents/core/todo_tool.py:587). The loop then fences the answer as DATA and raises the reading turn's taint. An item the reading turn wrote itself is its own argument, already in its transcript, and is not fenced (agents/core/todo_tool.py:472; the loop gives each run a turn token, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:413).
- So the owner's HUD turn that reads a plan written from Telegram is tainted by it. That follows the kernel's inbound policy, and the HUD tags such items "untrusted source".
- A script's own writes cannot launder text into the plan (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:37). The broker for an execute_code script's calls reads an answer as the loop reads a result (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:106): it raises the origin once a tool that declares untrusted_output answers ok, an answer says tainted, or the answer is flagged as the loop's fence flags one (an injection pattern anywhere in it, or the fence's own markers). Once the run is tainted, by the broker's own flag or by the origin an earlier read raised, nothing is scanned: the K1 loop builds a broker per request, so the origin is what carries it there (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:104; review-H315f m3). Otherwise a small answer (under 16 KiB as it encodes, counted exactly with the encoder's own string function: a newline costs two characters and a quote two, non-ASCII one, bytes as str() spells them, and the separators between items (review-H315i m1, n4; review-H315j n1, n2), a container wider than what is left is refused before it is listed, and a value JSON spells through str(), a huge int or an object, is never small) is scanned inline, where it costs microseconds, and a larger one on the scan's own single thread, never the loop's default pool, so one script's small calls do not queue behind other scripts' multi-megabyte scans (review-H315g m2). One thread, not four: the scan holds the GIL, so more gave no throughput and made the loop wait 4-5x longer at p99 (review-H315h m2, review-H315h n1). An answer too deep to encode is flagged, never raised out of the broker. It covers the whole answer in overlapping 64 KiB slices, and a slice never ends inside a word of up to 256 more characters, so a pattern's closing boundary is the answer's own (review-H315g n2); no single regex call holds the interpreter lock for a large answer, and a forked child gets a pool of its own (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:224, agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:140-148; review-H315e m2). A refusal, or a tool that raised, taints nothing. Every later call of that run then writes tainted items.
- A script's calls belong to no model turn (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:89), so what it wrote is data even to the turn that ran it.
- A session kernel that has held untrusted text taints every later cell's calls until a reset replaces its record (agents/core/session_kernels.py:829). It has held it once a cell read it, or ran in a turn that had. Each interpreter gets a mailbox directory of its own, removed with it (a reset, a crash, an idle expiry, an eviction, a failed start). The directories sit under one per manager (p<pid>-<token>), whose lock (an exclusive flock on its .lock) the manager holds while its process runs. The directory is made and locked under a temporary name and only then renamed into place, so no start ever finds it with a lock nobody holds; before each mount the manager checks that the lock it holds is still the file there, and when it is not (the file is gone or another file has the name) locks a new file there again, where its live mounts are (made and locked under a staging name, then renamed over .lock, so the name never holds a file nobody has locked: review-H315i m2), taking a new directory only when that cannot be had and giving no mount when no lock can be had at all (review-H315g m1). An owner path that is no longer a directory (ENOTDIR, a link loop) or an fd that is gone (EBADF) reads as lost too, and closing that dead fd never fails the mount (review-H315i n1, review-H315j m2); any other error reading the lock (ESTALE, EACCES) says nothing about it, so the lock is kept: giving it up let the next start remove the live mounts under it (review-H315h m1; agents/core/session_kernels.py:129, agents/core/session_kernels.py:160). With no flock (Windows) a kernel is mounted as before, and the directory ages out. A start removes an owner directory whose lock it can take and that is still the file at .lock after it took it (a file an owner relocked away from is an orphan that says nothing about it: review-H315j m1), which is a process that ended, in any pid namespace sharing the root: a pid is not asked, since the hub is PID 1 on every container start (review-H315f m1; agents/core/session_kernels.py:234, agents/core/session_kernels.py:1144). A directory with no lock (an older layout) ages out after the idle expiry, an owner directory by its newest interpreter's time, which a busy interpreter moves. A lock that cannot be asked (another user's, ENOLCK), or a directory that cannot even be looked into (another user's under umask 077), reads as alive and is kept, and one unreadable entry never stops a sweep or a start (review-H315i m3). So two processes on one data root (jarvis-hub and jarvis-runtime, or a container and the host) never delete each other's live mounts (review-H315e m1), and a file a tainted kernel wrote there never reaches the clean kernel after it.
- A run's result says tainted whenever it printed anything, read untrusted text, or ran on a kernel that held some (agents/core/code_tools.py:604), so the loop fences its output and raises the turn's taint whether the run succeeded or failed. A plan therefore cannot carry an injected instruction into a later, clean turn as the tool's own words, and the web tools' taint refusals and the kernel's queueing apply to the turn that ran the script.

The loop. It never replaces the answer with a "same as call N" stub, and never counts a todo call against a per-tool cap (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:126). The cap setting's label says so (agents/core/settings_db.py:194), and a start gives a stored row the current label (agents/core/settings_db.py:546).
- The repeat detector keys a todo call on its arguments and on the plan the model last saw (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1658, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1706). A read after the plan changed is the tool doing its job. The same call with nothing changed in between is stopped like any other repeat: the third is refused and the fourth ends the turn. A failed call leaves the plan the model saw unchanged. A script (execute_code) may have changed the plan behind the model's back. So each one that made tool calls, or did not finish cleanly (a crashed one reports none), opens its own revision, and the next read after it is a new call, however many scripts ran (review-H315e M1; agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1677). The revision is applied after the reads of the script's own step, which answered the plan from before it (review-H315f m2). A script that ran cleanly and called nothing changed nothing, so the repeat stop holds across it (review-H315f n2), as does one execute_code refused before any script ran (switched off, no sandbox, not isolated, no authority) or a session-kernel call refused before its cell (e-stop, expired, denied, no kernel, an empty or overlong cell; review-H315h n2), but not an unconfirmed teardown, which also ends a cell that ran; a handler that raised may have raised after its script ran, and opens a revision. A K2 cell's call count is the host's, never the count the kernel reports, and 0 when the cell had no mailbox (review-H315g n1, review-H315h n2).
- The answer is never cut: 7,000 bytes fits the smallest per-result budget, and the tool is pinned whole even after the turn's allowance is spent (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:100).
- The description asks the model to mark the item it starts in_progress, and completed when it is done.

The owner's view:
- A write leaves a todo_updated event in the tool trail (agents/core/todo_tool.py:484). It carries the session, the statuses, the position of the item in progress and the total. It never carries the text or the ids, which are free text too. A read or a refusal leaves no event.
- GET /sessions/todo and GET /sessions/{id}/todo (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:145, agents/core/routers/sessions.py:154) are user-guarded and no-store; an invalid id is a 400.
- Each item carries its by and tainted, never its turn. The recent list puts first the plan the agent most recently wrote or read. A plan's labels (when, which agent, whose turn) move only when its list changes.
- `nerva todo [SESSION]` (agents/cli/nerva.py:1727) prints the plans with [ ] [>] [x] [-] marks and each item's tags (agents/cli/nerva.py:1685): guest turn, household turn, background turn, untrusted source. A bad session id exits 2 before any request. A malformed reply, a non-object item included, exits 1.
- The Decision Inbox shows the plans with open work under the decisions (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:65, mounted at frontend/src/gap.tsx:3372). It shows at most three plans of eight items each, how long ago each plan was written, and every tag of each item (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:39). A failed read is shown as failed, with its reason, not as "no plans".
- The capability registry calls the tool reversible session state with a compensating rollback: a later call can write back what a call replaced, and the tool keeps no copy of it (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:287).
- A forget clears every plan (agents/core/data_purge.py:561) and lists todo_plans in live_stores_cleared. A turn already running when the purge starts can still write its plan afterwards, just as it still saves its reply.

Adapted: Hermes classifies todo as mutating in its loop guardrails. Here it is ungated because it writes only its own session's list: the shared session's list only for the owner's turns, and every item's origin is kept and shown.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, with H340 in the same change (critic note 21: one skill_view), and fixed after seven adversarial reviews. The first (review-H318: two majors, six minors, nine nits) found an unkeyed signature counted as a vouch and approved changes that never landed. The second (review-H318b: two majors, seven minors, seven nits) found that an approved change disabled the skill it improved (a bundled skill unbundled, a signed or approved one losing its standing) and that the owner still approved without seeing the change. The third (review-H318c: one records major, eight minors, seven nits) found a write between the standing read and the renewal could ride into the vouch, a renewal failure reported as applied, a keyed signature overwritten while its key was missing, a publish that silently dropped a linked file, and cards that could be lost or left pending. The fourth (review-H318d: one major, five minors, six nits) found that text-mode SKILL.md writes made every vouched apply fail on Windows, a partial renewal left a new signature over the old text, publish still followed a link planted after its check, and cards beyond the route's page were called inert. The fifth (review-H318e: two minors, seven nits) found the old SKILL.sig read after the write with no rollback behind it, text-mode test fixtures on the Windows lane, a signature that could not be put back reported as the old text staying, a truncated write, the review superseding by the record's origin, a /v1 card approvable without its diff, and publish describing another read of SKILL.md. The sixth (review-H318f: one minor, four nits) found the whole-file write staging its temporary file inside the skill, where one a crash left would void the signature. The seventh (review-H318g: two minors, five nits) found a standing that could not be read for a moment read as unsigned, and the crash-safety claim wider than the code. All are fixed or stated below; two nits are stated by decision below. Hermes gives the agent skills_list, skill_view (a skill's SKILL.md or one of its linked files) and skill_manage (create, patch and delete). Nerva now offers all three powers under its governance: the two reads as ungated read-only ToolRPC tools, and authoring as a proposal the owner approves.

The three tools are in agents/core/skills/tools.py; register_skill_tools (agents/core/skills/tools.py:192) registers them on the orchestrator's ToolRPC server in AutonomyCoordinator, next to todo (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1153).

The trust gate:
- SkillLoader.catalog_gate (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1362) is the prompt catalog's gate, factored out and now shared by the catalog, skills_list and skill_view.
- It says why a skill is not shown: sandboxed (quarantined included), untrusted (a signature that does not verify here), or declared for other agents. prompt_catalog applies it unchanged, and its suite passes as before.

skills_list {query?, offset?, limit?}:
- It returns name, a one-line description and the command names for every skill the gate passes for the calling agent (agents/core/skills/tools.py:265).
- A row whose text is injection-flagged is left out, as the catalog leaves it out. The query matches name or description, case-insensitively. Pages hold at most 50 rows, with total and next_offset.
- Unknown fields and malformed paging are refused by name.

skill_view {name, file?} (agents/core/skills/tools.py:305):
- It returns the SKILL.md body (frontmatter removed; the heading dialect whole) with its template variables rendered (H340), plus the list of the skill's other files, at most 3 KiB of names as the answer carries them (escapes counted) with files_more counting the rest; a file or body is served up to 64 KiB on disk, as always, and refused only when its escapes pass 128 KiB (MAX_ENCODED_BYTES), and the description is cut to 2 KiB escaped (agents/core/skills/tools.py:87-96). With file, it returns one of those files, listed or not.
- It serves the bytes the trust checks ran on at load, kept as Skill.view_files (agents/core/skills/loader.py:334): each file up to 64 KiB as bytes, at most 1 MiB of a skill, any other file only as its size (listed, refused by name). An edit on disk after the signature check is not what the model reads, and a skill's assets are not held for the process's life. Signing a skill loads it again, so the view follows the signed bytes.
- A path can only name a file of that snapshot. It must be relative, with no '..', leading '/' or backslash, and it is normalised (agents/core/skills/tools.py:182). The snapshot refuses links when it is taken.
- Only text is served (a NUL or bad UTF-8 is refused, a BOM dropped), at most 64 KiB (MAX_FILE_BYTES, counted in bytes) after the template variables render and 128 KiB once escaped. The tool declares the escaped ceiling, the file list's and the description's bounds and 4 KiB of envelope as its own result budget.
- An unknown skill and one this agent is not shown answer alike (skill_unknown).
- The answer is tainted, and carries a warning sentence saying why next to the content, in two cases (agents/core/skills/tools.py:248):
  - the body or the description is injection-flagged;
  - the skill comes from outside the product and the owner has not vouched for it.
- Skill.owner_vouched (agents/core/skills/loader.py:788) is true for a bundled skill, or for an outside one with a keyed signature or the owner's approval of these exact bytes. That is the same rule that decides whether its code may load in-process.
- An unkeyed SKILL.sig is a sha256 anyone can compute. It verifies as integrity-only, but it is no vouch, so a self-signed import stays data (review-H318 M-1, SEC-B2).
- The loop fences a tainted answer as DATA and raises the turn's taint.

skill_propose (agents/core/skills/tools.py:392):
- {name, content} proposes a new SKILL.md for an existing skill that this agent is shown. It becomes a pending SkillProposalStore proposal with origin agent:<agent>, plus one skill.patch_proposal approval card bound to it in the ledger (queue_card, agents/core/skills/proposals.py:213). The background review and /refine queue theirs the same way.
- A bundled skill is refused (skill_propose_bundled): it is product source, and an edit would unbundle it and, with its code, stop it loading. A change that would rename the skill is refused (skill_propose_rename).
- What the owner reviews comes from the ledger, never from the card. GET /api/skills/proposals (admin, agents/core/routers/skills.py:782) serves the pending proposals, a page of 20 with more counting the rest, each with its whole diff against the live SKILL.md, whether the skill drifted since, and flags for a rename or a bundled skill (describe, agents/core/skills/proposals.py:272); a proposal from before cards were bound, or whose card is gone from the queue, gets its card there, every pending proposal's, not only the page's, and the answer names every pending proposal's card (cards). The /v1 console's panel holds every skill-change card it has no diff for (one beyond the page, or one no proposal names) with Approve disabled, offering Reject (review-H318e n-4), re-reads the action list once the proposals answer, and says the change is loading, or that it could not be read, and holds Approve until it knows; a change the hub will refuse (a bundled skill, a rename) offers reject only in both consoles. The HUD's Decision Inbox shows these under SKILL CHANGES, whole, with approve and reject on the proposal's own card (frontend/src/panels/skill-changes.tsx), and the /v1 console's action panel shows the same diff under a skill-change card.
- Only the proposal's own card decides it (agents/core/skills/curator.py:217): a card anyone with a user token queued naming a proposal id changes nothing, and the decide route says so.
- Re-sending the same text, from any origin, makes no second proposal and no second card; a card that failed to queue is queued by the retry. A newer proposal from the same origin (the caller's own, even when the text re-sent was another origin's) for the same skill supersedes its older pending one (marked superseded, its card withdrawn), whether the tool, the background review or /refine proposed it (each passes its own origin, review-H318e n-2); binding a card withdraws the unbound cards naming the proposal, and a proposal superseded while its card was queued gets that card withdrawn, and a process takes at most 10 proposals a day, new skills included (skill_propose_limit).
- The owner's decision applies it at once: POST /api/actions/{id}/decide on the proposal's card runs SkillCurator.apply_decisions (agents/core/routers/actions.py:147, agents/core/skills/curator.py:154), one pass at a time, the nightly pass included, not gated by the learning loop's flag or the night window. The apply is hash-checked against drift and backed up under the skill's directory name with a unique suffix.
- The applied bytes keep the skill's standing (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1294, agents/core/skills/loader.py:1325): judged on one snapshot of the tree read before the write; after the write, the tree must be that snapshot with only SKILL.md replaced by the approved text, and the SKILL.sig that verified or the owner's approval is renewed over exactly those checked bytes, never a later read. SKILL.md is read and written as bytes, never in text mode, so the line ends on disk are the ones checked, on Windows too, and written whole: staged beside the skill's folder where it can be (a file a crash leaves inside the folder counts as a member and fails the signature closed; where beside it cannot be, another filesystem or a root the hub cannot write, the folder itself is used: review-H318g n-1), created with the old file's mode, flushed to disk and renamed over it, so a write cut short leaves the old text (review-H318e n-3, review-H318f m-1). The old SKILL.sig is read with SKILL.md, before anything is written (review-H318e m-1); a read of it that fails changes nothing and is tried again at the next decision (unreadable_signature, review-H318f n-1), and so does a standing that could not be read for a moment, which no longer reads as unsigned (review-H318g m-1); a signature that stays unreadable is warned about once per proposal. The apply is not crash-proof: a crash between the rename and the renewal leaves the skill sandboxed (untrusted, never trusted) and the next decision reports it as drifted, and on Windows a SKILL.md another process holds open cannot be replaced, so the change is retried as write_failed. Otherwise, or if the renewal fails, the old SKILL.md and the old SKILL.sig are put back byte for byte, where the old signature and approval still hold, the outcome says changed_during_apply or standing_not_renewed (rollback_failed, with the backup, if the old text could not be put back; signature_not_restored if the old text is back but its SKILL.sig could not be, which leaves the skill untrusted until it is signed again; when the old text could not be put back, its signature is not either, so what was renewed is not undone over the text that stays), and the proposal is marked stale with that reason rather than retried every pass. A standing that cannot be read (a SKILL.sig that is not UTF-8) reads as unsigned, and one proposal that fails never stops the pass. A keyed SKILL.sig whose key is not configured is not overwritten: the change waits (signing_key_missing). A shipped skill is known by its load or by where it lives (a shipped name directly under the product's skills tree), so one whose bytes drifted is still refused, by the tool, the background review and the apply. A skill nothing vouched for gains no vouch, a signature that no longer verifies is not renewed, and code changed on disk since the approval does not ride the patch. The answer reports each outcome with the state the skill is left in (shown, sandboxed, untrusted, hidden) or why it was not applied (bundled_skill, renames_skill, drifted_since_proposal, write_failed). A write that failed stays approved and is retried at the next decision, leaving no backup behind for the attempt. Publishing builds the package from one snapshot of the source, the bytes it read, and its registry row describes that snapshot's SKILL.md (review-H318e n-5): a skill whose folder is a link, a member that is a link or not a regular file, or a file that changed while read is refused (422, skill_source_refused: a link, a special file, or a file that could not be read stably), and a link planted after the check is never followed.
- {description, steps} asks for a new skill, which SkillLoader.generate_skill writes into CDX-8 quarantine (PENDING_REVIEW, never executed until the owner approves).
- Nothing writes a live SKILL.md: the live file is byte-identical after a proposal.
- Only an owner's turn that has read nothing untrusted may propose. A guest, a household member, a job, an inbound channel or a turn that read a web page (the action origin a read raises) is refused by name, and so is a turn whose origin cannot be read. Injection-flagged text is refused, as are mixed or malformed arguments.

Differences from Hermes, by decision:
- Authoring is a proposal, never a write. Deleting a skill and adding supporting files stay owner actions.
- skill_propose is offered wherever an ungated tool is, and refuses every turn that is not the owner's clean one; it is not withheld from the offer (a nit both reviews left).
- The daily limit is per process and follows local time: a restart resets it.
- Publishing a skill to the marketplace signs a staged copy, never the owner's tree, so sharing a skill is not vouching for it (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:391).
- All three tools are ungated, so an inbound guest is offered them only when the owner names them in llm.guest_tools (critic note 22). tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json is regenerated.

Tests: tests/test_h318_skill_tools.py (43 cases), tests/test_h318c_skill_review.py (22, the second review, and one H350 case), tests/test_h318d_skill_review.py (22, the third review), tests/test_h318e_skill_review.py (21, the fourth review), tests/test_h318f_skill_review.py (10, the fifth review), tests/test_h318g_skill_review.py (5, the sixth review), tests/test_h318h_skill_review.py (7, the seventh review), vitest files for the HUD's JSON setting field (3, and one H329 case) and the Decision Inbox's skill changes (frontend/src/test/skill-changes.test.tsx, 12), and the /v1 action panel's skill-change cards, a refused change's included (tests/frontend/tools.test.js), with the live orchestrator's pinned tool list in tests/test_agent_runtime_v2.py. They cover:
- the list against the catalog, query, paging and refusals, and hidden skills;
- view of a bundled body, unknown and hidden skills, linked files and every path refusal, binary and oversized files, and load-time bytes;
- taint and warning for an unsigned outsider and for injected text;
- the template variables;
- patch and new proposals, the posture and turn refusals, and the malformed cases;

Parsing. split_frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:47):
- drops a leading UTF-8 BOM before the fence check (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:56);
- takes the closing fence at column 0 only, as Hermes' `\n---\s*\n` does, so an indented `---` inside a block scalar is content (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:63);
- falls back to key: value lines for a block that is not valid YAML (_naive_key_values, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:83), instead of demoting the file to the heading dialect.

The fallback is stricter than Hermes' line split:
- only column-0 keys count, so a nested `name:` cannot replace the skill's own;
- a value wrapped in matching quotes loses them;
- a fallback that finds neither a name nor a description counts as no frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:77), so a heading-dialect file framed by fences keeps its heading parse.

Identity decisions pass lenient=False (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:72), so a name only the fallback can find never decides one: the Hermes pin gate (agents/core/skills/importer.py:271) and the migration and rescan slugs (agents/core/skills/importer.py:1192, agents/core/skills/importer.py:1376).

SkillLoader._parse_manifest decodes with utf-8-sig on both the snapshot and the path read (agents/core/skills/loader.py:854, agents/core/skills/loader.py:856). A manifest the normaliser cannot read registers under the directory name instead of failing (agents/core/skills/loader.py:871).

The manifest:
- The name is capped at 64 characters and stripped after the cut (agents/core/skills/loader.py:890; the caps are at agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:28-29).

- A list-valued author or license is joined (agents/core/skills/loader.py:895).

contract_fields (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:359), merged into every frontmatter manifest (agents/core/skills/loader.py:902), keeps the keys Hermes recognises:

- platforms, read as Hermes matches them (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:204): a list, or one string as one name. Each name maps through PLATFORM_MAP and matches the OS whose sys.platform starts with it, so darwin and win count and osx and win64 do not. An unmatched name is kept, so a gate refuses it everywhere, as Hermes hides it;

Imported frontmatter is third-party text:

Backend-urile cloud Claude, Gemini, OpenRouter/compatibil și adaptoarele Responses API-key (OpenAI gpt-4.1, xAI Grok) declară `supports_tools = True` și vorbesc nativ protocolul de unelte, deci bucla guvernată din `agent_runtime` rulează și pe ruta cloud: Claude traduce istoricul în blocuri `tool_use`/`tool_result` (id-uri invalide înlocuite consecvent, rezultate paralele comasate, cache pe sistem + ultima unealtă, controale de efort prin `_fit_to_wire`); Gemini trimite `functionDeclarations` și re-emite `thoughtSignature`; OpenRouter/compatibil folosește dialectul OpenAI; xAI păstrează raționamentul criptat pe durata invocației. Streaming SSE există pe calea de text (Claude, Gemini, Responses). Eșecurile sunt ture degradate, nu excepții. Regresii: tests/test_cloud_tool_turns.py, tests/test_openai_responses.py, tests/test_xai_responses.py. Collateral review (2026-10-02, e741f6bc): the shared source diff is confined to a backend-owned cache for typed temperature rejection on selected non-streaming local auxiliary calls. Existing cloud, tool-turn, stream, provider-selection and unrelated consumer branches are unchanged; the focused H277/H513/LM Studio union passes. This does not expand this row’s claimed capability or close its remaining gaps. Streaming auxiliary collateral review (2026-10-03, base 4668be6c): source changes are confined to scoped LM Studio generate_stream retry and the compression worker call context. Nonstreaming producers, ordinary streams, cloud/Ollama adapters and unrelated task/kernel paths retain their existing branches. The row-specific cited tests are included in the 3433-case affected-row regression, which passes. Existing verdict preserved without new feature or live-provider credit.

Task3 actuation collateral review (2026-10-03): guardian-denial stopping changes a terminal approval outcome inside the common tool loop; cloud tool-turn wire formats and text-stream adapters remain unchanged. The missing streamed tool-turn callbacks and Codex adaptation remain gaps; partial verdict retained. Native human-wait collateral review (2026-10-04, base87b2a1b8): the runtime changes only per-run timing scope and tool/wall deadline consumption around verified native human waits. AST/source review preserves existing offer resolution, loop guards, result spill/guidance/taint, provider wire formats, compaction, recovery and conversation clocks claimed by this row. Event-sink limits and ordinary hangs remain bounded. Existing verdict and gaps retained; affected-row regressions and exact native integrations are recorded separately, without fresh mutation/live acceptance or new completion credit. Local auxiliary output-cap collateral review (2026-10-04): Cloud/tool generation methods are unchanged; the cap rung excludes tools and requires the exact guarded local auxiliary role. This preserves the existing verdict and limits from semantic review; no new completion or live acceptance credit.
reviews.remaining: O tură cu unelte nu e streamuită: `generate_tool_turn` nu primește callback de token pe niciun wire, iar bucla din agent_runtime o așteaptă întreagă; streamingul există doar pe calea de text. Pe Claude, blocurile `thinking` ale unei ture cu unelte nu sunt păstrate pe ToolTurn și nici redate înapoi: `anthropic_messages` convertește doar text + `tool_use`. Codex nu e implementat (OAuth/abonament, rezumate de raționament, replay criptat pe OpenAI): adaptorul Responses e API-key și servește doar gpt-4.1, fără raționament. Nu există adaptor Bedrock Converse: `host_protocol.py` doar refuză cererile de alt protocol trimise către hosturile bedrock-runtime. Nu există probe cu provideri live.

Reviewed repair now refuses below-minimum effort before HTTP/retry/usage, and explicit empty declarations suppress all reasoning controls. Budget-only mappings remain distinct from native effort fields; canonical clamping and constructor/registry empty precedence are verified. CLI chat now accepts canonical --reasoning for one invocation and sends the optional HTTP/SSE request field without writing settings. Missing/null preserves configured defaults; explicit none retains existing provider-specific disable/refusal semantics. Nested null frames retain explicit ancestor revocation, and expired scopes cannot issue subsequent retries. Actual CLI-to-HTTP-to-mocked-provider, SSE lifetime, concurrency and stdlib-only CLI regressions pass independent review. It preserves cloud/local-only and approved-model gates. Both real HTTP dispatch paths check invocation lifetime, including prebuilt payloads and nested null scopes; unsupported models refuse before HTTP. Canonical invocation effort uses nearest-weaker resolution, below-minimum local refusal and explicit-empty omission. Actual text/stream/tool requests preserve encrypted native reasoning and function-call order only inside a revocable backend/model/session-bound invocation. Mismatched, missing, expired, oversized or truncated replay refuses before HTTP/tools; no plaintext reasoning or replay state enters persisted conversation history. Existing local-only and approved-model policy remains authoritative. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. This does not expand this row’s claimed capability or close its remaining gaps.
reviews.remaining: The referenced providers.flags-model-overrides contract still lacks invocation-only chat --model and --provider authoring (HTTP/CLI); --reasoning is implemented. Named vendor declaration/translation coverage from the referenced ladder inventory, such as Kimi, DeepSeek and GLM, is not produced by the generic owner-supplied compatible declaration mechanism. Future mappings require verified current supported schemas and must preserve H679 no-escalation rather than copy historical stronger-level overrides. The xAI adapter supports only exact Grok4.5/4.6, not unverified legacy aliases or general OpenAI reasoning-model replay. Unknown models remain undeclared/refused as appropriate; explicit none may locally refuse when disabling cannot be honored. No live-provider acceptance or billing proof.

Nerva now reads each provider's quota off every cloud response and shares a 429 with every process. agents/core/llm/quota.py holds the rules. llm_async_client, the one constructor every cloud backend's HTTP client goes through (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, xAI, the Responses dialect, VLM), now hangs two hooks (agents/core/llm/egress.py:97-98). response_hook (agents/core/llm/quota.py:338) reads the provider's own quota headers with parse_headers (agents/core/llm/quota.py:146): OpenAI-style x-ratelimit-{limit,remaining,reset}-{requests,tokens}; Anthropic's anthropic-ratelimit-{requests,tokens,input-tokens,output-tokens}-{limit,remaining,reset}; and retry-after as seconds or an HTTP date read as UTC. It understands resets given as durations ("6m0s", "20ms") or RFC 3339 times, and it stores the latest numbers per backend, key and model. On a 429 it blocks that backend, key and model (request_model, agents/core/llm/quota.py:78: Gemini's path, else the JSON body's model), or the whole key when the request names no model, until the provider's retry-after, else 30 s, never over 900 s (QuotaStore.block, agents/core/llm/quota.py:207). request_hook (agents/core/llm/quota.py:317) runs before the egress recorder on every request. It refuses a request whose model or whole key is held with ProviderRateLimited before it is sent, so a refused request never reaches the provider or the egress ledger. Another key in the pool is not held: on a refusal the Anthropic backend (_post_messages, and the stream, which retries a refused open on the next key) and the Gemini backend (generate, tool turn, stream) fail over to the next key as on a 429, and ProviderRateLimited carries retry_in, so AuthProfilePool.report_failure(key, cooldown=retry_in) keeps the held key cool for its whole hold (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:98, agents/core/llm/gemini.py:204, agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:159). The H380 provider probe reports a held key as rate_limited, sends nothing, and caches that verdict no longer than the hold and at most 30 s (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:191). Retry-after and reset values must be finite ('inf', 'nan' and overflowing numbers are unreadable), a negative retry-after is unreadable so the 30 s default applies, and a reset time without a zone is read as UTC. The store drops its pre-model tables once. A local host is never tracked or held, even when the same backend is held in the cloud. The state lives in one SQLite file under the data folder (QuotaStore, agents/core/llm/quota.py:173), so the hub, the CLI, the scheduler and any worker see the same numbers and the same holds. A key is known only by a 12-hex fingerprint of its hash, and every failure is swallowed, so a quota reader never breaks a request. usage (agents/core/llm/quota.py:361) gives each backend's requests and tokens left, the fraction left (clamped, none for a missing or non-positive limit), time to reset and any hold. It is served by GET /api/llm/quota (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:439, admin, 503 quota_unavailable when unreadable or when a row cannot be serialised; each row carries its model, which /usage and the panel name), the HUD Provider Quota panel (frontend/src/panels/provider-quota.tsx, Admin group: bars, numbers, reset times, a hold tag), and /usage (agents/core/commands.py:225, admin tier, rendered by render). The router is not fed a forecast; Hermes' own guard is likewise a refusal before the request, which is what this does. tests/conftest.py gives each test its own quota store, so a mocked 429 never holds a later test (tests/conftest.py:187). tests/test_h373_provider_quota.py (78 cases) covers durations, retry-after (seconds, dates, no zone under another host timezone), OpenAI and Anthropic headers, unreadable values, key fingerprints, and the store: latest numbers, clamping, a negative limit, blocks with retry-after, the default and cap, a hold before numbers, two processes, damaged data and the default path. It also covers the hooks on a real llm_async_client (recording, no headers, a 429 hold refused before dialling and absent from the egress ledger, another key, the default hold, other errors, a local model, a local request of a held backend, a failing store), the local-host test, the hook order, rendering, the admin route and the admin /usage command. The review round added the fail-over on a refusal for both backends and their streams, the cooldown floor, per-model holds, finite and signed header values, zone-less resets, the route's serialisation, and the probe's held key (tests/test_h380_provider_probe.py). frontend/src/test/provider-quota-panel.test.tsx has 3 cases. There are 50 mutants, all killed; the review round's 18 mutants, all killed (5 by tests added after a first pass).

Choosing a model now passes one registry of guards, server-side and before the choice is stored, on every surface that picks a model, as Hermes' selection-guard registry does. agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py holds the registry: register (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:123) adds a guard, and evaluate (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:175) runs every guard once per choice, so a new guard appears on every surface at once. enforce (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:186) returns the findings once all are cleared, or raises SelectionRefused naming every finding and the flags still missing. A flag clears only a literal true. Two guards ship. The cost guard (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:130) asks confirm_expensive for a model whose output costs at least llm.cost_confirm_usd_per_mtok (agents/core/settings_db.py:189; $40 per million tokens by default, 0 never asks, in safe mode the stricter of it and $40 (0, never asking, takes the $40; H490), a negative value refused on write at agents/core/settings_db.py:898, an unreadable one read as $40). It names the input and output prices from cost_estimator.MODELS; price_of (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:84) prices a routed slug (vendor/model) or a variant (model:beta) by its model, and an unpriced model is not asked. The data-policy guard (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:153) asks acknowledge_training for a model or route whose vendor may train on the prompts. ProviderProfile now declares data_policy, one of DATA_POLICIES (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:30: local, no-training, trains-on-inputs, unknown), with a note and per-model glob rows (data_policy_for, agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:84), validated at construction and served in status() (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:155). LM Studio and Ollama are local; Anthropic and OpenAI Responses are no-training by their API terms; Gemini is unknown with a note (an unbilled key's prompts may be used); OpenRouter is unknown, with its :free variants trains-on-inputs (agents/core/llm/providers/__init__.py:243); llm.openrouter_data_collection=allow is a trains-on-inputs route choice. A pin with no provider is checked against every profile's model rows. The acknowledgement is a consent event: record (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:229) writes a model_training_consent row to the audit log before the choice is stored, naming the surface, the setting and the model, and a choice whose consent row cannot be written is not stored (ConsentNotRecorded). A cost confirmation writes a model_cost_confirmed row naming the price, best-effort. Nothing is stored with the choice, so the next choice asks again. The surfaces: the admin settings PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:195; AdminPutBody takes confirm_expensive / acknowledge_training as StrictBool, agents/core/routers/admin.py:112) and the settings import (agents/core/routers/admin.py:365; its dry run lists what the guards would ask) go through _guard_selection (agents/core/routers/admin.py:170), 409 selection_guard when not cleared, 503 when the consent cannot be recorded. choices_from_settings (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:256) reads llm.claude_model, llm.gemini_model, the compatible provider/model pair (either half changed, the other read from the store) and the OpenRouter data-collection switch; an ordinary write is not asked even with an expensive model stored. A job's model pin is guarded on create and edit (agents/core/routers/jobs.py:76), only when the pin changes, and the confirmation is never stored with the job. nerva config set (agents/cli/nerva.py:928) runs the same guards, names the flags --confirm-expensive / --acknowledge-training, and writes its rows through the hub's audit log opened from its own process (agents/cli/nerva.py:89). nerva jobs create/edit pass the flags to the hub and name them on a 409 (agents/cli/nerva.py:99). The HUD Settings panel and Jobs panel (and the modal job dialog) open frontend/src/selection-guard.tsx on a 409: the findings with their prices or policy, then the model's name typed (a money or external action under H168's tiers) to send the choice again with every flag the findings asked for; cancel keeps the edit unsaved. A configured cloud key is checked with its provider before a turn finds out. agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py asks each cloud provider once, with the key the hub would use (configured_key, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:87: for Anthropic and Gemini, the only providers with an AuthProfilePool (POOLED), the first of the `<VAR>S` pool split on commas and whitespace as the router splits it, else `<VAR>`; every other provider reads `<VAR>` only). The command center asks with the key the route's backend holds: the pool's current key for Claude and Gemini, the compatible backend's own api_key otherwise. It sends one authenticated GET (request_for, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:105): Anthropic /v1/models with x-api-key and anthropic-version, Gemini /v1beta/models with x-goog-api-key, OpenRouter `<base>/key` (its model list is public; the key record answers 401 to a key it does not know), and `<base>/models` with a bearer for the other OpenAI-shaped providers, honouring a configured base URL. The GET goes through llm_async_client, so it is in the egress ledger as `llm:<provider>`, and H368's host-protocol mandate refuses a mismatch before it leaves; the xAI and OpenAI Responses probes use trust_env=False, as their backends do (NO_ENV_TRUST, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:67). Nothing is generated. The verdict (probe, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:223) is one of: `ok` (any 2xx, with the listed model count); `no_listing` (404/405: nothing at that URL, so the key is not proven); `auth_failed` (401, or a 400 whose body names a bad key: Gemini API_KEY_INVALID/API_KEY_EXPIRED, xAI "Incorrect API key"; the body is read inside the probe and never returned); `forbidden` (403); `rate_limited` (429, or a key held by the shared 429 guard of H373, with nothing sent); `error` (any other status, which is named, or an unexpected failure); `unreachable` (any transport error); `refused` (the host mandate); `not_configured` (no key, nothing sent); or `not_cloud` (a local provider). Only `ok` proves the key (WORKING, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:61). The key and the response body are never in a result or a log line. A result is cached per provider, key fingerprint and probed URL, so a changed key or base URL is probed afresh: for TTL_SECONDS (300 s), and a transient verdict (rate_limited, error, unreachable) for TRANSIENT_TTL_SECONDS (30 s) or, for a guard-held key, no longer than its hold (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:53-56). Concurrent callers, forced ones included, share one in-flight request (_fresh, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:205). A forced re-check inside MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (30 s) answers the cached verdict marked `throttled`. last (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:263) reads the cache without a request. probe_all (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:301) asks every cloud provider concurrently, except one whose key variable belongs to a base URL on another host (_key_for_elsewhere, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:287): an OPENAI_API_KEY beside an OPENAI_BASE_URL on a gateway is not sent to api.openai.com unless llm.compatible_provider is openai-responses. POST /api/admin/llm/providers/probe (admin; admin_llm_providers_probe, agents/core/routers/admin.py:959) checks one provider or all, with `force`; an unknown provider is a 404. The Console's Provider Check panel (Admin; frontend/src/panels/provider-check.tsx) probes nothing until asked. It shows each verdict (`key rejected` with the HTTP status beside it; `key not verified (nothing at this URL)` in amber for no_listing), the model count and a named HTTP status, offers a forced re-check per provider, and says when a re-check was throttled. The command-center model block asks the provider for a selected cloud route (_cloud_probe, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:224; agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:339) and waits at most CLOUD_PROBE_WAIT_SECONDS (4 s), after which the verdict reads `unreachable` and the probe finishes in the background. The route is ready (`cloud_selected`) on `ok`; `rate_limited` keeps it runnable (`cloud_rate_limited`); `no_listing`, `error` and `unreachable` make it unknown (ready=None, `cloud_no_listing` / `cloud_error` / `cloud_unreachable`); `auth_failed`, `forbidden`, `refused` and `not_configured` make it not runnable (CLOUD_PROBE_REASONS, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:204). The block carries `cloud_probe` (provider, verdict, status code, time, cached; agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:370), and its hint names the provider, what it said and the HTTP status (_model_hint, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:391). `nerva doctor`'s runtime_resolves and `nerva status`'s runnable line read that block, so a wrong or revoked key now fails them with its reason instead of passing on "a key is set". tests/test_h380_provider_probe.py (30 cases) covers the request per provider with the key only in a header, the key resolution, one read and its model count across list shapes, nine statuses, three transport failures and an unexpected one, the protocol refusal recorded as not sent, the egress row, no request without a key or for a local provider, no key or body in results or logs, the cache per key with expiry, the throttled and then allowed forced re-check, the cache-only read, probe_all, the admin route (admin-only, one, all, force, 404) and the command center's key choice. tests/test_h380b_provider_probe_review.py (35 cases) covers the review round: OpenRouter asked about its key, not its public list; a gateway key kept away from api.openai.com and OpenAI asked when the key is its own; a 400 that names a bad key; a missing listing that proves nothing; the key read as the router reads it and the compatible backend's own key; a guard-held key rate_limited for the hold; concurrent callers sharing one request; the bounded wait; readiness per verdict and the short cache of a transient one; trust_env matching the backends; the hint; and the cache slot per URL. tests/test_first_run_command_center.py covers every `cloud_*` reason and `cloud_probe` in the model block. reviews.summary: **The SOUL body is scanned before it reaches the model, and the HUD is told when it was.** `Agent._read_soul` — the one builder behind `_load_soul` at construction and, since H672, `Agent.refresh_soul` at the compaction boundary — resolves the live file through `soul_path_for`, splits the front-matter, runs `_scan_soul_body` over the *uncapped* body (so truncation can never drop the very lines the detector would have flagged), quarantines flagged lines to a visible stub that names the FILE line, and only then caps the result; the verdict is announced by `_announce_soul_verdict`, one place for both moments a persona lands, so a quarantined persona is the same ERROR line whether it arrived at boot or under a running session, and the over-cap WARNING likewise. The scan is four passes: `strip_invisible` deletes TAG-plane characters and the decoded payload is scanned with `detect_injection`, so a smuggled phrase is named in the flags rather than silently deleted; every line is scanned with `detect_injection_normalized` — the union of the raw line, its Cf-stripped copy, its whitespace-collapsed copy and both together, with the ORIGINAL kept; `_wrapped_injection_hits` re-reads the non-blank lines as one normalised string and, through `quarantine.injection_spans`, quarantines exactly the lines a cross-line match covers, leaving single-line spans to the per-line pass so nothing is flagged twice; and the whole body is dropped for `_blocked_soul_body` (which carries `_SOUL_FALLBACK_RULES`) when flagged lines exceed `_SOUL_BLOCK_RATIO` of the non-blank lines OR when a non-empty body is left whitespace-only by the passes. Passes one, two and four are #1173; #1179 — wave two of the adversarial review — moved the per-line call from `detect_injection` on a Cf-stripped copy to `detect_injection_normalized`, added the wrap pass, and added the second trigger of the escalation. Wave two found the per-line scan defeated by a respacing ("Ignore  all  previous  instructions" with two spaces, a tab or a NO-BREAK SPACE scanned clean, because the patterns are literal with single spaces and stripping cannot answer a real separator without gluing two words together), by a line wrap through the phrase (no pattern contains a newline, and Markdown reflows prose freely), and by a persona written wholly in TAG characters, which returned `("", flags, False)` — an agent with no persona at all AND no fallback rules, so quality.py's persona-consistency rail read an empty forbidden-phrase list for the least-constrained agent on the box. The respacing fix lives in the shared normaliser (`quarantine.collapse_whitespace` + `_detection_variants`), so the catalog-row scan in `agents/core/skills/loader.py` gets it in the same change. `GET /api/agents/{id}/soul` keeps returning the raw bytes on disk — it is the editor view, and the owner has to see what they actually wrote — but carries a `guard` verdict beside it, computed by `_soul_guard_verdict` from the SAME helpers `_read_soul` uses (`_scan_soul_body`, `_cap_soul_body`, `_soul_max_chars`; the router's comments still say `_load_soul`, which still exists and delegates to the builder), so the HUD can no longer show a persona the model is not receiving without saying so, and the wave-two passes reach the verdict without the router changing. Before this the only trace of a quarantined persona was a `logger.error` nobody watches. **An independent review of the original slice found two blocking majors and both were fixed there.** The first was a records defect that would have turned the tree red on merge: the slice edits `agents/core/agent.py`, whose sha256 is pinned by eight evidence entries, and regenerated no reports — dropping the headline to 119/697 and flipping six rows to stale. The second was subtler and worse. The endpoint resolved only `agents/<id>/SOUL.local.md` → `agents/<id>/SOUL.md`, while `_load_soul` checks the user data home FIRST (`Documents/Jarvis/souls/<id>/SOUL.local.md`, the packaged-install overlay). So on a packaged box the HUD read one file, ran the guard over it, and reported `blocked: false` for a persona the model had in fact had dropped — **precisely the case the verdict exists to prevent**, reproduced with a real overlay. Both now resolve through one shared `agent.soul_path_for()`, because two resolutions of "which SOUL is live" is one too many, and `test_the_editor_endpoint_reads_the_file_the_model_reads` drives the real endpoint against a data-home overlay. #1179 left `routers/agents_api.py` untouched — same sha256 either side of the merge. Six new test functions (eleven collected cases) in `tests/test_soul_injection_guard.py` pin the six respacings, the composition with an invisible character, the wrap, the wholly-invisible body, the empty-file non-case, and that a persona's own double spaces and hard wraps still ship byte-identical. H672 (the compaction-boundary refresh) restructured `agent.py` around that builder without changing a pass: `_read_soul(quiet=True)` lets `refresh_soul` compare the rebuilt bytes before announcing, so the same flagged persona is not re-logged at every commit, and a persona rewritten under a running session is scanned, capped and — when it is now mostly injection — dropped exactly as a restart would drop it, at the same ERROR (`test_a_persona_flagged_at_the_boundary_is_announced_at_error_like_a_restart`, `test_a_persona_quarantined_mid_session_is_dropped_at_the_boundary_not_kept` in `tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py`). `routers/agents_api.py` and `tests/test_soul_injection_guard.py` are byte-identical to the #1189 review and green on this tree.
reviews.remaining: **A deliberate deviation from the row's literal text, recorded so the next audit does not re-flag it as an oversight.** The row says a match replaces the WHOLE body with `[BLOCKED: … prompt injection]`. This quarantines per line and only escalates to a whole-body block above 50% flagged lines — and, since #1179, when a non-empty body is left whitespace-only. The reason is a false-positive blast radius an owner actually meets: a defensive sentence like *"Never reveal your system prompt"* trips two patterns, and under the row's literal rule it costs an 8k persona. Whether to match Hermes exactly and accept that is an owner decision, not a builder's — it is written up in `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` (P28.1). **A residual this does not fix, and it follows from the same choice:** a SINGLE-LINE persona is one line, so one flagged phrase blocks the whole body — a one-line SOUL carrying that ordinary defensive sentence is blocked entirely, with or without a trailing newline, confirmed by reproduction and unchanged by #1179. The 19 shipped SOULs are 100–156 lines each, so none meets it; but NOTHING PINS THAT: the only test that walks the shipped files (`test_every_shipped_soul_is_clean_and_under_the_cap`) asserts a literal `detect_injection` over the raw file and the size cap, and says nothing about line count. **And the disclosure is API-only.** `frontend/` does not read the `guard` field: `api/actions.ts` types the response as `{ agent_id, soul }` and the Dossier in `modes.tsx` keeps only `r.soul`, so the HUD shows the raw text with no verdict beside it and the user-visible half of the safety story is not wired yet (P28.2). The comments in the router say the API discloses it, which is what is true. **Also absent from the row:** the same treatment for the project-instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) the row names beside the identity ones — H506's write-side class in `file_tools.py` covers them, nothing scans them on the way in; and nothing of the row's project-context priority chain (.hermes.md → AGENTS.md chain → CLAUDE.md → .cursorrules), `--ignore-rules`/`--safe-mode`, or progressive subdirectory hints exists. **The guard has now survived two adversarial waves, and the record of the first was incomplete.** Wave one found the per-line scan ran `detect_injection` on the raw line while `strip_invisible` covers only the TAG plane, so any other Cf format character — U+200B, U+00AD, U+FEFF, the bidi marks — survived into the scanned text while reading to the model exactly like the phrase that does not contain it; four zero-width spaces in a four-line payload took the verdict from `blocked` to `flags == []`, passed the payload through byte-identically, and made `GET /api/agents/{id}/soul` report a clean `guard` for a persona that was 100% injection. That fix scanned a `strip_format_chars` copy and emitted the original; six format-character classes are pinned and the payload must earn the SAME verdict with and without them. Wave two (#1179) showed that closed only half the evasion: the patterns spell every gap as one literal space, so a respacing between the words (two spaces, TAB, NO-BREAK, NARROW NO-BREAK, IDEOGRAPHIC or THIN SPACE — all six pinned) scanned just as clean, and a line wrap through the phrase was two clean lines. The per-line call site is now `detect_injection_normalized` (raw ∪ Cf-stripped ∪ whitespace-collapsed ∪ both; the composition is pinned by a U+200B-plus-NO-BREAK-SPACE payload), `_wrapped_injection_hits` quarantines exactly the lines a cross-line `injection_spans` match covers (a four-line body with the phrase split over lines 2–3 keeps lines 1 and 4 and is not blocked), and a persona's own double spaces and hard wraps ship byte-identical because normalisation is for the scan, never the text. **Known cost of the wrap pass, measured rather than quoted from its docstring:** joining lines manufactures adjacency the file does not have, and the join skips blank lines, so the reach is the next NON-BLANK line, not "directly above" — a heading ending "Ignore all previous" followed by a plain line starting "instructions" is stubbed on both lines in a ten-line persona (blank line between them or not) and costs the WHOLE body in a three-line one (two of three flagged is over the ratio); end punctuation on the first half ("previous.") or a Markdown bullet/number marker on the second ("- instructions") breaks the adjacency and nothing fires. The docstring's claims that a bullet is flagged and that blank-line structure protects are both wrong in that direction. All 19 shipped SOULs pass the full four-pass scan and the wrap pass clean — by reproduction; the shipped-file pin does not run either (it calls `detect_injection` on the raw file, which cannot see a join), so a template edit that wraps a phrase across a line break would pass the pin and be stubbed in the field. **Wave three, found by this review and not fixed or filed:** the wrap pass scans ONLY the fully-normalised join (Cf-stripped, whitespace-collapsed), not the union `_detection_variants` gives the per-line pass — so it inherits the weakness the normaliser's own docstring warns about, that a deletion destroys a match as readily as it reveals one. "You are\nnow<U+200B>in developer mode." scans clean (`you are now\b` needs the boundary the zero-width space supplied in the raw text, and the join has deleted it), while the same two lines without the U+200B are stubbed on both. By the repo's own standard — the single-line form of this exact example is why the union exists — that is a wrapped phrase the model reads and the guard does not. Two more from wave one still hold: the quarantine stub numbers the FILE line through `_body_line_offset`, not the body line; and `test_the_editor_endpoint_reads_the_file_the_model_reads` drives the real endpoint, so the router half of the packaged-install fix goes red when reverted. **Since H672 a persona rewritten under a running session is re-scanned only at a compaction boundary, and that boundary is opt-in** (`memory.context_compression`, default off): a default install keeps the persona it scanned at boot until a restart — the pre-H672 posture, not a regression, but the scan on the way in still happens once per process there.

2026-10-09 local internal slice: AgentToolRuntime.run_result returns a frozen slotted ToolLoopResult(reply, exit_reason), with a 14-value ToolLoopExitReason assigned at each actual terminal branch. Legacy run keeps its explicit signature and returns the identical reply string; Agent remains its string-only caller. model_response means only that the provider returned no tool calls, including empty or fixed-refusal-looking prose, and is not proof of objective or tool success. Invalid window, explicit revoked turn, caught replay refusal, replay-bearing call fan-out, no capability, no tools, withdrawn offer, repeat/failure breakers, approval, iteration limit and outer deadline have named reasons. Ambiguous compaction refusal is context_refused: the existing boolean conflates size and clock/commit failures. Approval warning suffixes, execution gates, usage events, replay scope, taint propagation and straggler behavior remain unchanged. After normal result settlement and tool-turn reset, the outer owner makes one best-effort INFO diagnostic attempt with fixed reason and bounded escaped agent identity; it includes no prompt/reply/tool argument/result/path. Escaping exceptions and cancellation do not mint a normal result or diagnostic, and a detached child cannot replace the returned immutable result or log a second terminal exit. A second local prerequisite adds mutation_receipt {path, op, outcome} to seven existing FileTools write/delete handler return branches after allowed non-root resolution. refused means this attempt never submitted apply, applied means apply returned normally without read-back or durability proof, and unknown is the caught apply OSError branch, including errors after bytes changed. reviews.summary: Every log record, from every process, now goes through two filters: H495's shape scanner and a catalogue of credential-bearing names plus the Romanian identifiers. agents/core/log_catalogue.py (outside security/, additive) is a scanner over the names that make a value a credential whatever it looks like: query parameters (QUERY_PARAMS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:54: access_token, refresh_token, id_token, token, auth, api_key, client_secret, secret, password, signature/sig, the AWS presign parameters, session, jwt), masked at any length up to the next separator; body, form and structured-log keys (SECRET_KEYS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:62), quoted in JSON or a Python repr, assigned with a quoted value, or unquoted when the value is six characters or more; the Authorization header after any scheme (Bearer, Basic, Token, Digest, ApiKey, HMAC…), or without one when the value is twelve characters or more and carries a digit, so `Authorization: denied` stays; the credential headers X-Api-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Access-Token, X-Goog-Api-Key, X-User-Token, X-Admin-Token, Api-Key and X-Webhook-Token (SECRET_HEADERS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:68); and the whole value of Cookie and Set-Cookie. It also runs PIIScanner's own CNP and IBAN patterns (agents/core/security/scanner.py:287-288) with their checksum validators, and an IBAN written in spaced groups of four; the other PII patterns stay out (an e-mail or phone number in a log is often the point of the line; card and SSN shapes carry no checksum). A bare `key` parameter (settings routes use it for a setting's name) and a bare `token:` key (token counts) are not in the catalogue. The accepted adaptation for the per-item path is not built. The route crosses only user_guard and calls d.forget directly (memory_kg.py:589). reviews.summary: Compaction now checkpoints the turns it is about to discard, and fails closed when a required checkpoint does not land. ContextCompressor takes a checkpoint callable (agents/core/context_compressor.py:321). compress() awaits it with exactly the turns the summary replaces (the evicted middle, all of it even when a prior summary covers part) and the whole transcript, before the summary is built (agents/core/context_compressor.py:579-586). The orchestrator builds that callable in _precompress_checkpoint (agents/core/orchestrator.py:392) and hands it to the compressor on every compacting history build (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3999). It calls precompress.run_checkpoint (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:107) over the registered providers, or the default transcript archive. The hook is versioned. A provider declares checkpoint_api_version, and only one at CHECKPOINT_API_VERSION 2 or above counts (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:63). The optional keyword arguments (evidence_messages, require_checkpoint, checkpoint_api_version, session_id) are passed only when the provider's signature accepts them (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:69). A synchronous provider runs off the event loop, and providers get copies, so they cannot change the transcript. The shipped provider, TranscriptArchive (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:174), keeps a raw per-session JSONL copy of the evicted turns. It appends each evicted turn once, by a hash of speaker, time and content, to a file whose name is a hash of the session, under the data folder (compaction_archive), owner-only (0600 in a 0700 folder); the append is flushed and fsynced before on_pre_compress returns (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:208). It remembers what it holds across restarts, skips damaged lines (including a line cut inside a multi-byte character), starts the next record on a new line after a torn last line, and writes images as [image]. It is not an extraction. Nothing mines those turns into episodes, consolidation or LivingMemory, and nothing checks that per-turn LivingMemory extraction landed for them. Recall and session_search never read the archive (TranscriptArchive.read() has no production caller), and no production code registers precompress_providers. The archive runs only while memory.persist is on (agents/core/orchestrator.py:404), and a chat's backup-first delete (H218, which the H262 sweep uses) removes it with the chat, while the sweep prunes orphaned archives (purge_orphan_compaction_archives, agents/core/retention.py:100). memory.compression_checkpoint_required (agents/core/settings_db.py:255, off by default; only a literal true turns it on) makes it fail closed. A failing checkpoint provider, or no checkpoint provider landing ("No active memory provider completed pre-compress checkpoint API v2"), raises CheckpointAborted. The compressor then summarises nothing. Old images are still dropped, with an images-tier lineage row when any were (agents/core/context_compressor.py:509-521). The orchestrator refuses the turn with the compaction refusal reply only when the image-dropped transcript does not fit the model's window (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4043). With the setting off, a failing provider is logged and compaction proceeds. A checkpoint that landed new turns, or had a provider fail, writes memory.precompress_checkpoint to the signed intent log with an archived count (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:148). One that landed nothing new, the steady state once over budget, writes nothing. Every abort writes memory.precompress_abort. The rows carry turn counts, provider names and the reason, never the turns, and every audit write runs off the event loop. tests/test_h427_precompress_checkpoint.py (54 cases) covers the contract (version, names, signature sniffing, copies, a synchronous provider, nothing to evict), the not-required and required paths (failing provider, old provider, no provider, a missing or non-callable hook, a failing audit), and the archive (write once, fsync, restart, damaged lines, hashed names, images and structured content, turn identity, default location). It also covers the compressor (exactly the evicted turns before the summary, a prior summary, abort, under budget, compact fail-closed) and the orchestrator (archived and audited, required failure keeps the transcript with no clock commit, not required proceeds, no provider, refusal exactly at the window, a literal-true switch, the default archive, the settings row, no turn text in the audit). The original build had 51 mutants: 49 killed and 2 equivalent (a non-callable hook fails with the same TypeError either way; re-reading the archive file each time is only slower). The review round added the retention prune, the memory.persist gate, the steady-state audit, the torn-line and multi-byte handling and the file modes, each with a case that fails without it. This needs an owner decision: Episodes E3.0 never copies source payloads automatically, and LivingMemory turn records are content-free digests.

Getting back into a conversation now comes with a free recap, rendered locally from the stored turns and never by a model, on resume, as /recap in every channel and in the HUD. render_recap (agents/core/memory/recap.py:80) groups a session's turns into exchanges (an owner turn and the replies that follow it), keeps the last 10 by default (DEFAULT_EXCHANGES, agents/core/memory/recap.py:24; at most 50, MAX_EXCHANGES, agents/core/memory/recap.py:25), and puts each turn on one line of plain text, whitespace folded, control and bidi characters removed and cut to 280 characters with an ellipsis (_clean, agents/core/memory/recap.py:35; the raw text is cut to four times the limit before cleaning, so a huge stored turn costs no more than a short one). A reply's tools collapse to a count and their distinct names, "[3 tool calls: web_search, web_fetch]" (tool_line, agents/core/memory/recap.py:57), names only, never arguments or results, and an owner turn never shows one. The answer carries the exchanges as data and the same recap as text lines (● you / ◆ the agent) with "the last n of m exchanges" when some are left out. The tools had to be recorded first: turns persisted only role, content, agent, time and tokens. The orchestrator opens a per-turn collection when an owner turn arrives (turn_tools.begin, agents/core/memory/turn_tools.py:23; agents/core/orchestrator.py:2014 and :2216), the agent's tool-event sink notes each finished call's tool (turn_tools.note, agents/core/memory/turn_tools.py:30, from the sink's record, agents/core/agent.py:903) while still landing every event in the trail, and the reply that closes the turn is stored with the names (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3621) on Turn.tools (Turn, agents/core/memory/conversation.py:36; a stored value that is not a list of names reads as none, _tool_names, agents/core/memory/conversation.py:62), persisted, reloaded at start, on resume and on an explicit session load (session_continuation._load_locked, agents/core/session_continuation.py:285), carried in a continuation's immutable seed (seed_json, agents/core/session_continuation.py:89), and absent from a turn that called none. The collection is a context variable, so concurrent turns in other sessions never mix, and a tool loop run through asyncio.to_thread still lands in its own turn. POST /sessions/resume answers with "recap" beside the last 20 raw turns it always returned (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:197), rendered from the whole stored session. /recap [n] (_recap, agents/core/commands.py:375; registered at agents/core/commands.py:408) answers in any admitted channel from that channel's own session (a chat's session is its own, pinned by the channel handler); on the owner's shared session (a widget visitor, an agent-target webhook, an MCP caller, or any channel with memory.cross_channel_sessions on) it answers only the owner and refuses anyone else before reading a turn, with n exchanges (at most 50; anything else, a non-ASCII digit included, is the default ten), and leaves out its own /recap line, recognised by the command parser in any case (/Recap, /recap@bot). file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). local_docs and agents/core/ingestion/ remain the bulk-ingestion path into memory.
