reviews.summary:
H456 re-read against 55d625f. The 2026-09-07 evidence ("no per-item toolset allowlist") is stale, but the row stays partial.

The enabled_toolsets half of the contract is shipped and well built. agents/core/job_toolsets.py holds:
- an immutable CATALOG (:7-11: basic/files/terminal);
- a strict `validate()` that refuses unknown, non-list or duplicate ids (:14-21);
- `resolve()`, which refuses a group whose members are not all registered ('enabled_toolsets contains an unavailable toolset', :30-37);
- `toolset_scope()` (:63-79), whose nested frame is `parent.names.intersection(names)` (:72) with a shared _Lifetime, so a closed parent raises 'job toolset scope expired' (:66-67) instead of falling back to defaults. Intersect-never-union is enforced.

It is enforced at three boundaries, not one:
- the offering boundary (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:226,234 `allowed = allows(name) and _posture_allows(...)`, narrowed again by agents.yaml patterns at :239-240);
- the runtime filter before and after the profile (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:285-294), re-applied at the in-turn compaction boundary by `_resolve_offer` (H672);
- RPC intake, ahead of preflight and handler (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:446-448, reason `job_toolset_not_allowed`).

Store boundary: agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:435 lists the option, :438-442 validates it and refuses it with `no_agent`, validate_action:310-311 refuses it on non-`ask` actions, and create and edit both re-resolve it (:1324, :1393). Fire time: jobs.py:1601-1603 `with toolset_scope(self._toolset_names(job.options)), selection_scope(job.options)`. Doctor reports the catalog, each job's `toolset_upper_bound` and a `toolsets_unavailable` problem (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_health.py:51-55, :113). Reachable from the CLI (`--toolsets default|none|<ids>`, agents/cli/nerva.py:264,275,1475-1481) and the HUD (frontend/src/panels/job-builder.tsx:35-49). PATCH /api/jobs/{id} refuses an unavailable toolset with 422 (tests/test_job_toolsets.py:327-328).

Hermes' two removal rules are met structurally. Every register_tool on the production server was enumerated: agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:518-835 (image_generate, H313's `speak` at :531-547, desktop_run, terminal_run, desktop_plan, operator_plan, osint_enrich, echo, time) and :839-928 (session_search, file_*, web_search/web_extract, search_memory, execute_code), plus H315's `todo`, registered after the tool profile (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:972), which writes only its session's own checklist (on the owner's shared session, only an owner's turn keeps one). None creates a job, and no `schedule.create` kernel capability exists. None is a messaging/clarify tool that needs a live human. The new `speak` announces into a room, but it is registered only with JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR on and is gated (ask-tier card, trusted execution only from an owner-accepted row), so it is never offered off the owner posture.

Verified green at 55d625f: 27 cases in tests/test_job_toolsets.py and 28 in tests/test_job_model_pins.py. The HUD cases in frontend/src/panels/job-toolsets.test.tsx were not re-run in this pass.

What keeps the row open is the contract's second half: a job cannot pin reasoning effort.
- Selection carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25).
- validate_options rejects any unknown option (jobs.py:435), so the pin cannot be stored; neither jobs.py nor job_selection.py mentions reasoning at 55d625f.
- _ask never enters `reasoning_scope`, so every scheduled run inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read in agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:339,352,390,419-420.
- The closed-lifetime transport machinery already exists (agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72), but only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1256, :1321).

Secondary gap: the bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~18 tools the server can register. A job that needs web_search, execute_code or search_memory must run unbounded on the default net, a residual that docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names itself. H513 fixture review: synthetic local backends now declare their actual LM Studio profile and loopback endpoint; original behavior assertions remain unchanged.
reviews.remaining:
(1) The per-job reasoning-effort pin (Hermes' `.cron-reasoning`, rolled into this row) is not implemented:
- `Selection` carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25), and `validate_pins` (:35-43) never sees an effort.
- `validate_options` rejects any option outside the known ten (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:435), so the pin cannot reach the store.
- `JobRunner._ask` (jobs.py:1601-1603) enters `toolset_scope` + `selection_scope` but never `reasoning_scope`. A job therefore always inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read at agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:339, :352, :390, :419-420.

The transport half already exists and is clamped: agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72; agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:83-88 with per-model overrides; agents/core/llm/gemini.py:135; agents/core/llm/xai.py:73; agents/core/llm/provider_request.py:46 and :54. Only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1256, :1321). Work owed:
- accept `reasoning` in validate_pins/validate_options against LADDER;
- enter `reasoning_scope(...)` in `_ask` beside the other two scopes;
- expose it on the CLI/HUD/doctor like the model and provider pins;
- test it in tests/test_job_model_pins.py.

(2) The bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~19 tools the production server can register. CATALOG (agents/core/job_toolsets.py:7-11) covers echo/time, the five file tools and terminal_run. These belong to no group: web_search, web_extract, search_memory, session_search, execute_code, desktop_plan, desktop_run, operator_plan, osint_enrich, image_generate and (with the Media Director on) speak, registered at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:518-835 and :839-928. A job that needs any of them must leave `enabled_toolsets` unset and run on the full default net. H315's todo is not among them: a job runs on the owner's shared session, where only an owner's turn keeps a plan, so no job uses it, with or without a group. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names this residual itself ("does not claim ... arbitrary plugin/delegation/code-runner groups"), and doctor reports the upper bound, not the effective offers.

(3) Minor: Hermes' middle precedence tier has no equivalent. That tier is a per-platform `cron` tools config that sets defaults for every scheduled job. Here, only the per-job list, the internal posture (`llm.internal_actuation`) and the agent's agents.yaml `tools:` patterns narrow an unattended run.

reviews.summary: The pieces around the feature exist, but nothing binds a standing instruction to a conversation. HeartbeatScheduler (agents/core/heartbeat.py:180) schedules per-agent routines from HEARTBEAT.md or agents.yaml, with MIN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL 3600 s (agents/core/heartbeat.py:52) and 15–30 s jitter. Since H506 it also refuses a HEARTBEAT front-matter that its injection scan flags. Admin routes /heartbeat/{agent_id}/start|stop|run (agents/core/routers/heartbeat.py:27) and the HUD HeartbeatPanel drive it. Owner-armed jobs accept plain-words schedules, can be paused, resumed and deleted, and include an `ask` action that sends a prompt to an agent. That prompt goes through a one-shot Orchestrator.process call on channel 'job' (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1609), and the reply goes to the owner's channel, not into the originating chat's history. The only chat slash commands are /help, /status, /sessions, /pause, /stop, /resume, /jobs, /remind and /voice. CommandContext (agents/core/commands.py:50) carries no explicit session id, but its principal is a Principal with channel and chat (agents/core/commands.py:37-46), and ctx.orch.session_id already resolves to the bound channel session because the channel handler sets the active session before handle_input dispatches a command. reviews.summary:
A work run can now be parked on real async work instead of being poked. Three barrier kinds hold a run's next tick without spending anything (BARRIER_KINDS, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:141):
- a registered process until it exits;
- a trigger until it fires: a queued task of this run reaching a terminal status, or an enabled webhook being called;
- a wall-clock time.

The barrier is a `barrier` column on the run (the _v2 migration, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:423). It also adds `run_events` (set and clear audit) and `run_procs` (processes registered for a run). Setting and clearing a barrier are events, not steps: they cost no budget, stay outside the fingerprint, and never change a verification result (set_barrier, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1457; clear_barrier_if, a compare-and-clear, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1532). A move to stopping or any terminal status clears the barrier in the same write, so stop always wins.

Validation, probes and stale clearing live in RunBarriers (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:280):
- request (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:314) refuses a spent or unparkable run and bounds every barrier. Its cap (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:355) is the earliest of its own wait (at most MAX_BARRIER_SECONDS, 7 days, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:74), the run's deadline, and the time the run's budget has left. Since H464b that is the EFFECTIVE budget (now + budget_state's seconds_left), so H487's proven approval-wait credit counts at barriers too; before, a run with credited wait time was refused `no_time_left` or capped early by the whole credit.
- A pid must first be registered for this run through the Python-only register_process (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:562). That refuses pid ≤ 1, the hub, its parent and dead processes, and allows at most 16 per run. It captures the process's start token, pid namespace and boot id.
- A trigger must be a task of this run or an existing, enabled webhook.
- active (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:589) is the one check the scheduler and the supervisor share. It clears the barrier on the next check if any of these hold:
  - the cap or the clock has passed;
  - the process has exited, its pid was reused, it is in another namespace, or it cannot be proven (default_pid_probe, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:229);
  - the trigger fired or vanished;
  - the probe raised.

  A check that fails ticks the run normally. So no barrier outlives its cap or the run's budget, and none can wedge the loop.

While a barrier holds, nothing is spent:
- ScheduleRuntime.due answers `waiting` after the budget check, so a spent budget still wins (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:222). Only the sweep clears a spent run's barrier.
- CompanySupervisor.tick returns `waiting` before planning or judging, so there is no step, no budget use and no judge call (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:271, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:302).

A planner sets a barrier with Action(kind="wait", barrier=…). _park (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:366) never enqueues:
- A wait with nothing to wait on is free, and so is one whose check failed for a moment (NOTHING_TO_WAIT_ON, WAIT_CHECK_FAILED, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:98, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:108).
- That is capped at MAX_FREE_WAIT_REFUSALS (3) in a row. After that, each is a failed plan step with one fixed reason, so the streak rule ends a planner that keeps asking (_free_refusal, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:447).
- The planner is told the last refusal.
- A malformed or forbidden wait is a failed plan step at once.

The judge sees the run's live background processes (RunBarriers.background, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:677) and can answer a third verdict, wait (WorkJudge.wait_probe, agents/core/autonomy/work_judge.py:124). That parks the run before grading, at most MAX_JUDGE_WAITS (3) times per run (_judge_parks, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:612). At settlement a `wait` answer withholds the pass.

H464b made one park path real in the shipped product. With JARVIS_COMPANY_MODE set at boot:
- The runtime builds from the orchestrator's real attribute names (_queue_reader, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:185; _governed_intake, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:199). Before, it looked only for `task_queue`/`queue` and `govern_enqueue`, which the orchestrator never had, so build_company_runtime returned None and no `company-mode-sweep` job was ever registered. Now the explicit arguments win, then `task_queue`, `queue`, `autonomy_queue` for the reader and `govern_enqueue`, then `autonomy.govern_enqueue` for the intake, each tested for presence rather than truthiness and only when callable. The same queue reader turns H487's approval-wait credit on in production, bound on the shared ledger only once the runtime actually builds (H464c; agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:414), and backs PendingRequests and RunBarriers (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:437). Every step still goes through the governed intake.
- The approved checklist is read back from the goal's own approval task (_read_back, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:228). The task named in the run's `approved_by` (`task:<id>:<decider>`) is re-read from the durable queue and re-minted through approve_from_task, which re-checks that a human accepted that very task. The goal is then bound to the run (the same approval and decider, title, deadline and budget, and, since H464c, the fingerprint pinned on the run when it opened) and given the run's own goal_id so the judge's goal-identity rule holds. What happens when it does not bind is H464c's M5 below. An explicit `goals=` still wins.
- When the checklist is done but a task this run queued was approved and is still executing, the hub parks the run on it before any grader is asked (_hub_parks, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:584, called first in _grade, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:556). RunBarriers.park_in_flight (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:382) picks the oldest such task (IN_FLIGHT_TASK_STATUSES = approved, running; agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:117) and sets a `task:<id>` trigger with source `hub`, a fixed reason "task N is still running" and the default 6 h wait, capped by the deadline and the budget left, each less a grading margin since H464c. The park is an event, not a step: it spends wall-clock time, never a step or a verdict. The hub waits on a task at most once per run (WorkRunLedger.barrier_sets, read from the append-only audit, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1605), so a capped wait is never renewed and a restart buys nothing. It never parks on a task the owner let the run go from, whoever set that wait, so the owner's "stop waiting" sticks against the hub too (the model-source rule itself is unchanged). A task that finished between the two reads is skipped. Any refusal or error (budget, no time left, barrier limit, a queue that cannot be read) falls through to grading exactly as before, and the tick never raises. The run resumes on the first sweep after the task is terminal.

H464c (the second review of H464b: six MINOR and two NIT findings) binds the chain to what the owner approved:
- M1: open_run pins the approved goal's fingerprint on the run (ApprovedGoal.approved_fingerprint, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:317; a nullable `approved_fingerprint` column, the _v5 migration, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:467), covered by the row's own fingerprint once set (identity, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:279). The read-back compares the re-minted goal with that pin, so an edit of the approval task after the run opened (a stale, recomputed or dropped fingerprint) drives nothing, and a run with no pin (opened before it existed) drives nothing.
- M2: a `task:<id>:…` approval opens ONE run, ever (open_run, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:782; _run_for_approval_locked, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:872). The check and the insert are one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that rolls back on any failure, so a commit that raised leaves no row for the retry's commit to write. A retried goal.approve gets the run the first attempt opened (same pin), reported with that run's goal id, or `approval_already_used`. This closes known gap 1 of the Codex review handoff (2026-09-28).
- M3 (sized exactly in H464d): the hub's park stops a grading margin short of the deadline and of the time the budget has left (the reserve in request, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:354). The margin is the floor the runtime passes, at least a minute (grade_margin, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:136; GRADE_MARGIN_SECONDS, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:133): the time from a tick to the next sweep on which the scheduler's per-run interval lets the run be due again (next_due_after_tick, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:115: the first multiple of the sweep cadence at or past the 300 s interval) plus a minute (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:434) — 360 s at the default 300 s cadence and at 60 s, 420 s at 120 s, 460 s at 200 s, 1,260 s at 1,200 s. It is never a share of the budget, and the same margin applies before a deadline. With nothing to spare past the margin the hub does not park and the run is graded now. Planner and judge waits are unchanged.
- M4: safe mode leaves company mode out: schedule_company_mode builds nothing and registers no sweep (a new `company_mode` safe-mode layer), and a sweep that finds safe mode on does nothing (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:134).
- M5: the read-back says why it has no goal (_ReadBack, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:216). "Cannot tell right now" (no reader, a read that raised) HOLDS the run: the planner returns Hold(stop=False) (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:164) and the tick is `idle` "held: …" with no step, no park and no grade (_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:408). Provably not bound (not opened from a goal card, no pin, a task that is gone, a policy decision, an edit, another run's goal, a binding check that raised, and since H464d anything re-minting the task raises) STOPS the run with `plan not bound to its approval: <reason>` as its stop reason, the way a stuck run is stopped, so the brief shows it. Neither is ever graded as a finished checklist.
- M6: a plan row's queued task kind must be inside the goal's scope (task_kind_in_scope, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:91: a scope kind, or under a whole one then a dot, `research.collect` under `research` and, since H464d, `file.write.append` under `file.write`). GoalDraft refuses the card (`plan_task_out_of_scope`, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:234), the planner clamp refuses the proposal (agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:184), and an approved row the checklist has to refuse stops the run with the reason (_walk, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:336; since H464d recorded as `approved row refused by scope: …`, not as unbound).
- N1: snapshot, and so every report route, is read-only (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1776). budget_state(settle=False) (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:960) reads only the tasks an open approval wait is on (_open_wait_tasks, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:537), writes nothing and opens no transaction; the tick path still settles. For 50 runs × 25 steps (the reviewer's perf_r5.py): 1,250 queue reads and 0.054 s before, 0 reads and 0.020 s after.
- N2: the reader is bound on the shared ledger only when the runtime builds.

H464d (the third review, of H464c: one MAJOR, four MINOR, four NIT, and two MINOR the closure found in older code) makes the grading margin exact and the rest of the chain honest:
- A1/B2/F1: the margin above. The 10 % share graded an 8 h run with 40 minutes left over its still-running task (the reviewer's e10: graded at minute 440 on `running`; now at minute 455 on `done`), and a sweep-only floor left a run parked into a window where the scheduler's own interval never let it be ticked again at cadences under 300 s. A run is now graded before its time runs out at 60, 120, 200, 300 and 1,200 s cadences through the real due() gate, whose per-run interval allows 1 s (at most 1 %) of timer jitter (due_slack, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:110; agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:249), so a sweep a moment early does not push grading a whole sweep past the margin.
- B1: anything re-minting the approved goal raises is provable (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:276): a budget edited to zero steps stops the run with `plan not bound to its approval: invalid_max_steps` (WorkRunError keeps its code; anything else is `approved_goal_invalid`) instead of failing every tick. Only the read is transient.
- B3: the reconciler records each still-open approval wait on every sweep (_observe_wait, agents/core/autonomy/pending_requests.py:307, a settling budget read), so an ask the owner edited before approving is credited up to the last sweep that saw it open whether or not the HUD polled (the reviewer's e1/e1b, ported with a sweep a minute: 180 s credit and 30 s used both ways, 0 and 210 s before). The report routes stay read-only.
- B4: a hold writes one `hold.start` run event per hold (note_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1631, deduplicated while the same hold is open), the first tick that can plan again writes `hold.end` (end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1648; _end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:436), the snapshot carries the open hold (hold_state, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1659), and the brief lists the run as held with a plain reason (_held, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:139). A run the scheduler skips as budget_spent is settled through the supervisor's settle_spent (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:520; _settle, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:269), which re-reads the budget, so a read that failed settles nothing; before, a spent run was never ticked and stayed open for ever.
- F2/F3 (older code): a checklist row whose step failed (the intake raised or returned no task, or the task vanished) is not done; it is tried again on a later sweep, at most MAX_ROW_ATTEMPTS (3, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:77) attempts, then the run stops with `approved row kept failing: <row> (3 attempts)`. A failed read of the run's own steps is a refusal (_run_steps, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:300) the runtime holds on, instead of reading "nothing done" and asking for row 1 again.
- M05/M43 test gaps closed; C4 stop wording; C2 an upgrade note (docs/UPGRADE.md) and plain stop reasons in the brief (_hub_stop, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:150): an in-flight run from before the pin stops once, as "opened before this version tied a run to the plan you approved; approve the goal again to run it"; C3, a rollback reading pinned runs as tampered, is documented there.

The owner can always let a run go:
- POST /api/company/runs/{run_id}/barrier/clear (user-guarded, agents/core/routers/company.py:179);
- `nerva company clear-wait`;
- the Company room's two-step "stop waiting".

The clear reports what it did, or what a newer barrier now waits on. A wait the owner cleared is not set again on the same target by the planner or the judge, nor by the hub's in-flight park. The brief and the HUD say "parked — waiting on …" only while the barrier is in force (_in_force, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:112).

A barrier only suppresses work. It grants nothing:
- no approval;
- no resume of a blocked run;
- no budget extension;
- no path around the governed intake.

tests/test_h464d_company_run_grading.py (19 test functions, 32 cases) ports the third review's repros (e1/e1b, e3, e4, e7, e8, e9, e10, intake_fail, steps_fail) and closes the M05 and M43 gaps; tests/test_h464c_company_run_binding.py (28 test functions) ports the reviewer's repros for M1–M6, N1 and N2, and pins the two survivors of the H464b pass that no test covered (a binding check that raises is a mismatch; an empty park answer is not a park). tests/test_h464_run_barriers.py (60 test functions) covers the barrier layer: bounds and caps (including the credited-budget cap), pid registration and probes (reuse, namespace, unprovable, EPERM), triggers, stale clearing, compare-and-clear, owner-clear stickiness, the migration, barrier_sets and park_in_flight (oldest in-flight task, undecided/missing/terminal ignored, once per task, the owner's clear, reader failures, a task finishing between reads, other refusals passed on, restart). tests/test_company_runtime.py (38) adds a real-shaped orchestrator (only `autonomy_queue` and `autonomy.govern_enqueue`), the checklist read back from a real TaskQueue approval task with eleven binding refusals (each case pins the draft's fingerprint, so it is refused by the check it names), and the AC11 end-to-end chain with no injected callables: approve a one-row goal, the step queues and blocks, the owner accepts the step's task, the next sweep parks the run on it (source hub), a RUNNING task keeps it `waiting` at no step, DONE clears it as `fired` and the run goes idle ("no grader is wired"); the owner's clear of the hub park sticks. tests/test_company_supervisor.py (55) pins the park before grading, with no grader wired, before the judge's wait probe, no re-park after the cap or the owner's clear, and fall-through to grading on every refusal or error. Barrier cases also live in test_schedule_runtime, test_work_run_ledger, test_work_judge, test_company_report, test_company_routes, test_company_planner and test_nerva_cli.

The goal is then bound to the run (the same approval and decider, title, deadline and budget, and, since H464c, the fingerprint pinned on the run when it opened) and given the run's own goal_id so the judge's goal-identity rule holds. What happens when it does not bind is H464c's M5 below. An explicit `goals=` still wins.
- When the checklist is done but a task this run queued was approved and is still executing, the hub parks the run on it before any grader is asked (_hub_parks, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:584, called first in _grade, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:556). RunBarriers.park_in_flight (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:382) picks the oldest such task (IN_FLIGHT_TASK_STATUSES = approved, running; agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:117) and sets a `task:<id>` trigger with source `hub`, a fixed reason "task N is still running" and the default 6 h wait, capped by the deadline and the budget left, each less a grading margin since H464c. The park is an event, not a step: it spends wall-clock time, never a step or a verdict. The hub waits on a task at most once per run (WorkRunLedger.barrier_sets, read from the append-only audit, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1605), so a capped wait is never renewed and a restart buys nothing. It never parks on a task the owner let the run go from, whoever set that wait, so the owner's "stop waiting" sticks against the hub too (the model-source rule itself is unchanged). A task that finished between the two reads is skipped. Any refusal or error (budget, no time left, barrier limit, a queue that cannot be read) falls through to grading exactly as before, and the tick never raises. The run resumes on the first sweep after the task is terminal.

H464c (the second review of H464b: six MINOR and two NIT findings) binds the chain to what the owner approved:
- M1: open_run pins the approved goal's fingerprint on the run (ApprovedGoal.approved_fingerprint, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:317; a nullable `approved_fingerprint` column, the _v5 migration, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:467), covered by the row's own fingerprint once set (identity, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:279). The read-back compares the re-minted goal with that pin, so an edit of the approval task after the run opened (a stale, recomputed or dropped fingerprint) drives nothing, and a run with no pin (opened before it existed) drives nothing.
- M2: a `task:<id>:…` approval opens ONE run, ever (open_run, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:782; _run_for_approval_locked, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:872). The check and the insert are one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that rolls back on any failure, so a commit that raised leaves no row for the retry's commit to write. A retried goal.approve gets the run the first attempt opened (same pin), reported with that run's goal id, or `approval_already_used`. This closes known gap 1 of the Codex review handoff (2026-09-28).
- M3 (sized exactly in H464d): the hub's park stops a grading margin short of the deadline and of the time the budget has left (the reserve in request, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:354). The margin is the floor the runtime passes, at least a minute (grade_margin, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:136; GRADE_MARGIN_SECONDS, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:133): the time from a tick to the next sweep on which the scheduler's per-run interval lets the run be due again (next_due_after_tick, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:115: the first multiple of the sweep cadence at or past the 300 s interval) plus a minute (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:434) — 360 s at the default 300 s cadence and at 60 s, 420 s at 120 s, 460 s at 200 s, 1,260 s at 1,200 s. It is never a share of the budget, and the same margin applies before a deadline. With nothing to spare past the margin the hub does not park and the run is graded now. Planner and judge waits are unchanged.
- M4: safe mode leaves company mode out: schedule_company_mode builds nothing and registers no sweep (a new `company_mode` safe-mode layer), and a sweep that finds safe mode on does nothing (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:134).
- M5: the read-back says why it has no goal (_ReadBack, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:216). "Cannot tell right now" (no reader, a read that raised) HOLDS the run: the planner returns Hold(stop=False) (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:164) and the tick is `idle` "held: …" with no step, no park and no grade (_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:408). Provably not bound (not opened from a goal card, no pin, a task that is gone, a policy decision, an edit, another run's goal, a binding check that raised, and since H464d anything re-minting the task raises) STOPS the run with `plan not bound to its approval: <reason>` as its stop reason, the way a stuck run is stopped, so the brief shows it. Neither is ever graded as a finished checklist.
- M6: a plan row's queued task kind must be inside the goal's scope (task_kind_in_scope, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:91: a scope kind, or under a whole one then a dot, `research.collect` under `research` and, since H464d, `file.write.append` under `file.write`). GoalDraft refuses the card (`plan_task_out_of_scope`, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:234), the planner clamp refuses the proposal (agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:184), and an approved row the checklist has to refuse stops the run with the reason (_walk, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:336; since H464d recorded as `approved row refused by scope: …`, not as unbound).
- N1: snapshot, and so every report route, is read-only (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1776). budget_state(settle=False) (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:960) reads only the tasks an open approval wait is on (_open_wait_tasks, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:537), writes nothing and opens no transaction; the tick path still settles. For 50 runs × 25 steps (the reviewer's perf_r5.py): 1,250 queue reads and 0.054 s before, 0 reads and 0.020 s after.
- N2: the reader is bound on the shared ledger only when the runtime builds.

H464d (the third review, of H464c: one MAJOR, four MINOR, four NIT, and two MINOR the closure found in older code) makes the grading margin exact and the rest of the chain honest:
- A1/B2/F1: the margin above. The 10 % share graded an 8 h run with 40 minutes left over its still-running task (the reviewer's e10: graded at minute 440 on `running`; now at minute 455 on `done`), and a sweep-only floor left a run parked into a window where the scheduler's own interval never let it be ticked again at cadences under 300 s. A run is now graded before its time runs out at 60, 120, 200, 300 and 1,200 s cadences through the real due() gate, whose per-run interval allows 1 s (at most 1 %) of timer jitter (due_slack, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:110; agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:249), so a sweep a moment early does not push grading a whole sweep past the margin.
- B1: anything re-minting the approved goal raises is provable (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:276): a budget edited to zero steps stops the run with `plan not bound to its approval: invalid_max_steps` (WorkRunError keeps its code; anything else is `approved_goal_invalid`) instead of failing every tick. Only the read is transient.
- B3: the reconciler records each still-open approval wait on every sweep (_observe_wait, agents/core/autonomy/pending_requests.py:307, a settling budget read), so an ask the owner edited before approving is credited up to the last sweep that saw it open whether or not the HUD polled (the reviewer's e1/e1b, ported with a sweep a minute: 180 s credit and 30 s used both ways, 0 and 210 s before). The report routes stay read-only.
- B4: a hold writes one `hold.start` run event per hold (note_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1631, deduplicated while the same hold is open), the first tick that can plan again writes `hold.end` (end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1648; _end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:436), the snapshot carries the open hold (hold_state, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1659), and the brief lists the run as held with a plain reason (_held, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:139). A run the scheduler skips as budget_spent is settled through the supervisor's settle_spent (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:520; _settle, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:269), which re-reads the budget, so a read that failed settles nothing; before, a spent run was never ticked and stayed open for ever.
- F2/F3 (older code): a checklist row whose step failed (the intake raised or returned no task, or the task vanished) is not done; it is tried again on a later sweep, at most MAX_ROW_ATTEMPTS (3, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:77) attempts, then the run stops with `approved row kept failing: <row> (3 attempts)`. A failed read of the run's own steps is a refusal (_run_steps, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:300) the runtime holds on, instead of reading "nothing done" and asking for row 1 again.
- M05/M43 test gaps closed; C4 stop wording; C2 an upgrade note (docs/UPGRADE.md) and plain stop reasons in the brief (_hub_stop, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:150): an in-flight run from before the pin stops once, as "opened before this version tied a run to the plan you approved; approve the goal again to run it"; C3, a rollback reading pinned runs as tampered, is documented there.

The owner can always let a run go:
- POST /api/company/runs/{run_id}/barrier/clear (user-guarded, agents/core/routers/company.py:179);
- `nerva company clear-wait`;
- the Company room's two-step "stop waiting".

The clear reports what it did, or what a newer barrier now waits on. A wait the owner cleared is not set again on the same target by the planner or the judge, nor by the hub's in-flight park. The brief and the HUD say "parked — waiting on …" only while the barrier is in force (_in_force, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:112).

A barrier only suppresses work. It grants nothing:
- no approval;
- no resume of a blocked run;
- no budget extension;
- no path around the governed intake.

tests/test_h464d_company_run_grading.py (19 test functions, 32 cases) ports the third review's repros (e1/e1b, e3, e4, e7, e8, e9, e10, intake_fail, steps_fail) and closes the M05 and M43 gaps; tests/test_h464c_company_run_binding.py (28 test functions) ports the reviewer's repros for M1–M6, N1 and N2, and pins the two survivors of the H464b pass that no test covered (a binding check that raises is a mismatch; an empty park answer is not a park). tests/test_h464_run_barriers.py (60 test functions) covers the barrier layer: bounds and caps (including the credited-budget cap), pid registration and probes (reuse, namespace, unprovable, EPERM), triggers, stale clearing, compare-and-clear, owner-clear stickiness, the migration, barrier_sets and park_in_flight (oldest in-flight task, undecided/missing/terminal ignored, once per task, the owner's clear, reader failures, a task finishing between reads, other refusals passed on, restart). tests/test_company_runtime.py (38) adds a real-shaped orchestrator (only `autonomy_queue` and `autonomy.govern_enqueue`), the checklist read back from a real TaskQueue approval task with eleven binding refusals (each case pins the draft's fingerprint, so it is refused by the check it names), and the AC11 end-to-end chain with no injected callables: approve a one-row goal, the step queues and blocks, the owner accepts the step's task, the next sweep parks the run on it (source hub), a RUNNING task keeps it `waiting` at no step, DONE clears it as `fired` and the run goes idle ("no grader is wired"); the owner's clear of the hub park sticks. tests/test_company_supervisor.py (55) pins the park before grading, with no grader wired, before the judge's wait probe, no re-park after the cap or the owner's clear, and fall-through to grading on every refusal or error. Barrier cases also live in test_schedule_runtime, test_work_run_ledger, test_work_judge, test_company_report, test_company_routes, test_company_planner and test_nerva_cli.

frontend/src/panels/company-room.test.tsx pins the HUD.

An adversarial review in four lenses confirmed 11 findings (6 MINOR, 5 NIT). Two verified fix rounds and a verify pass closed them all, along with 7 more the verifications found. Mutation results: 50 mutants in the first build, all killed (2 by cases added after a first pass). H464b: 36 more mutants on a scratch copy, all killed (the credited cap reverted or read from seconds_used; each reader and intake name dropped, truthiness instead of presence, the callable check dropped; each of the four goal bindings dropped, the goal_id kept random, a policy decider accepted, the read-back skipped; running dropped from or proposed added to the in-flight set, the hub-set and owner-clear exclusions dropped, newest-first order, a raise instead of a skip on a task that just finished, a raising reader skipped, the reader guard dropped, barrier_sets unfiltered or newest-first, the hub park removed, moved after the grader check or after the judge's wait, an idle result on a refusal or error, an error escaping the tick). H464c: 40 more mutants, all killed (2 by cases added after a first pass): the pin check, the no-pin guard, the stored pin, the pin in the row identity, a binding exception read as a match; the uniqueness check, the pin match, an unpinned re-open, the rollback, the coordinator's goal id; the hub reserve dropped, applied to every source, dropped from the deadline or the budget, the tenth-of-budget share, the sweep cadence and its extra minute, the cadence not passed; safe mode ignored at registration or at the sweep; each transient or provable classification, hold and stop swapped, doubt read as an empty plan, the Hold ignored or only idling, an empty park answer read as parked; the namespace rule, the exact-kind rule, a non-string kind, the card check, the planner clamp, a refused row graded; the report settling, writing or re-reading closed waits; the reader bound before the build. H464d: 43 more mutants, all killed (1 by a case added after a first pass): the interval slack dropped or widened; the next-due sweep as max(S, I) (the literal rule, graded never at a 200 s cadence) or ignoring the interval; the spent-run settle skipped, unwired or not re-reading the budget; the hub reserve dropped, unclamped or the tenth-of-budget share back; the floor from the sweep only or without its minute; a re-mint exception escaping, held, or WorkRunError unnamed; a spent or unreadable-steps row graded or an unreadable read stopped; each hold write, dedupe, end and snapshot field; the observation dropped or read-only; a failed row counted done, retried unbounded or once too often; the dotted-scope rule; the brief's held list, headline, plain unbound reasons and budget wording; M05 and M43. Test manual: GOV-294, GOV-297. Adapted from Hermes: its three goal-state barriers, the short-circuit that burns no turn or judge call, the judge's wait verdict with the live process list, and stale-barrier clearing. Every barrier is capped by the run's own effective budget and deadline, and pids are limited to processes the hub itself registered for the run. Image-recovery collateral review (2026-10-02): changes to shared CLI/image-turn or HUD local-panel disclosure are outside this row's claimed symbols. The exact command-tree expectation includes auth, and existing CLI/fish regressions pass. reviews.remaining:
Not reachable in production yet:
- **No process producer (owner decision 1; blocked on H302).** Nothing in the hub starts run-owned background work and registers its pid: register_process has no caller outside tests. The best first producer is `terminal_run` with `background: true` on the local-host transport. It needs WorkRunLedger.run_for_task; a spawn with start_new_session, bounded log files and a held proc.wait() that records the exit code; a lifetime cap and killpg on cap, ESTOP or stop; a reaper for stopped runs; schema, approval-card and parity updates; and a KillMode in deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service (today a restart kills the child and the barrier clears as `exited`, indistinguishable from success). The owner must say whether the task/hook trigger is an accepted adaptation of Hermes's pid/session barrier, or whether a pid wait must be reachable for "equivalent".
- **Pid waits are unusable on macOS/BSD.** There is no start token there, so every pid wait is refused `pid_unprovable`. The fix belongs in exec_cache.py (ctypes libproc proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)) or in a producer-held Popen handle, and needs macOS hardware or a macOS CI runner to verify.
- **The judge's `wait` verdict and planner waits are not reachable in production (owner decision 2).** WorkJudge.wait_probe needs a model rubric, and the shipped runtime passes no rubric, model planner or graders. Wiring one needs the owner's choice of local model and provider under H513 (auxiliary_request_scope, strict-local, security.data_training_ack) plus opt-in settings forced off in safe mode. Before any model planner, the rest of the intake arguments must be clamped: since H464c the task's kind is scope-checked as well as Action.kind, but the task's agent, title and payload still reach govern_enqueue unchanged.
- **No graders are wired in production.** After the hub park clears, a run idles until its budget ends. Deterministic verifier and judge adapters belong to the company-mode grading work; they must reuse an existing verdict, because _grade has no try/except and a judge that raises after the verifier recorded leaves `verdict_already_recorded` / `tick_failed` on every later sweep.

Deferred:
- Wake-on-fire: a parked run resumes at the next scheduled sweep.
- A `job:<id>` trigger.
- A process output-pattern trigger (needs the process producer).
- An owner-set wait like Hermes's `/goal wait` (owner decision 3): a clock or own-task wait only, never an owner-typed pid.
- Waiting between checklist steps: the checklist still advances when a step's task is approved, not when it finishes.
- A judge-sourced wait reserves no grading margin (only the hub's park does since H464c), so a judge wait that runs to the end of the budget still leaves the run ungraded. It is reachable only with a judge wait probe (owner decision 2).
- The grading margin bounds one run's way back to a sweep, not a queue: with several runs due at once (max_concurrent 1), a parked run can lose the sweep's one slot after its cap.
- A blocked run whose budget runs out is not settled (H464d settles only runs the sweep skips as budget_spent; a blocked one is skipped as blocked and its resume is refused once the owner answers), so it stays blocked on the record.
- The HUD's live wait credit for an open ask runs to now; if the owner then edits the ask, the durable credit falls back to the last sweep that saw it open (at most one sweep's worth).
- An owner stop of a working run is never closed out: request_stop moves it to `stopping` and settles only a second stop (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1382-1384), while ScheduleRuntime.due skips a `stopping` run (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:227-228), so the supervisor that would settle it is never ticked and the run reads `stopping` until the owner stops it again (reproduced on 03643762).

Needs network: re-checking Hermes's goal-wait behaviour at the pinned commit 59b2aeef (hermes_cli/goals.py was not among the inspected upstream sources). Review residuals after round 3 (latent or bounded): a dropped grading sweep is not absorbed by the margin; a transient queue read during the per-sweep wait observation cuts approval-wait credit; a hold open when a run stops is never ended; an expired ask would be re-asked; the upgrade note's 're-approve' advice needs a new card; four test gaps (docs/handoff/2026-09-28-handover/h464-round3-brief.md).

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine [focus] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand.

The command:
- /refine [focus] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:350, registered at agents/core/commands.py:416). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command.
- The focus is one line of at most 200 characters.
- It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list.
- Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed [… error …] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "[Note: … error", or one a later [1] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3).
- A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:513).
- It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does.

Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3476):
- It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it.
- The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path.
- In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long.
- A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3496). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1).
- A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged.

The learning loop's knobs are declared settings (category learning, agents/core/settings_db.py:311): review_max_tokens (512, 1–32768), review_daily_budget (20, 0–1000), review_cadence (every_turn, every_n_turns, idle_gap), review_every_n (3), review_idle_gap_s (90) and review_max_facts (3), with the defaults the code already used, bounded in _LEARNING_INT_BOUNDS (agents/core/settings_db.py:758). The admin settings API, the HUD and nerva config set can change them; nerva config get shows a number named …max_tokens as the number it is, not masked as a credential, and masks every key the settings store encrypts (the GA4 service-account JSON among them), and nerva config set echoes such a value masked too (review-H465e nit 3). A model id is masked only under a hinted name: llm.default_model shows as typed. Every knob reads within its declared bounds whatever the stored row (a row from before the bounds, restored or hand-edited, reads as the default), the review's model call's token cap included (bounded_learning_int, agents/core/settings_db.py:773). A declared 0 for review_max_facts or review_idle_gap_s is honoured, not read as unset; corrections have a cap of their own (3), so a review_max_facts of 0 keeps no facts, still records corrections, and /refine says what it found but did not keep (_number, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:293).

BackgroundReviewer.run_on_demand (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:335):
- It skips the cadence gate but spends the daily budget, rolling over at midnight, and refunds it when no review was had (a model down, a cut-off answer, a timeout, a cancellation), on the day the pass spent it (review-H465f nit 1). A budget of 0 means no reviews and /refine says so (reviews_off); 2.5 reads as 2, and a value that is not a number or lies outside 0–1000 (text, infinity, a boolean, a hand-edited -3, a fraction below one) is logged once and 20 used (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:268). A per-turn pass that does not run leaves a DEBUG line naming why. It keeps the strict-local model, and is bounded at REFINE_TIMEOUT_S (150 s, below the lease's 180-second wait); no setting raises it.
- It neither resets nor delays the per-turn cadence. It runs one at a time and never beside a per-turn review: a /refine while a per-turn pass runs is refused busy, and a per-turn pass that would start while /refine runs is skipped, not deferred. Independent #1233 review (historical scope): Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine [focus] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand.

The command:
- /refine [focus] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:350, registered at agents/core/commands.py:416). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command.
- The focus is one line of at most 200 characters.
- It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list.
- Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed [… error …] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "[Note: … error", or one a later [1] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3).
- A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:513).
- It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does.

Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3502):
- It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it.
- The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path.
- In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long.
- A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3522). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1).
- A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged.

reviews.summary: The inbound half exists with the governed posture. A2ARegistry (agents/core/a2a.py) allowlists peers and returns each peer's HMAC secret only once (add_peer / list_peers / remove_peer). receive_task (agents/core/a2a.py:224) checks the signature over the raw body in constant time, runs the a2a.inbound contract and parks every verified task in a bounded pending inbox. decide (agents/core/a2a.py:262) only flips the status ('Approval does NOT execute it'); test_decide_is_terminal_and_does_not_execute pins this. In agents/core/routers/a2a.py, POST /api/a2a/task stays off unless JARVIS_A2A_ENABLED is set, and peer CRUD and inbox decide are admin-guarded. Both have HUD callers: peer add/remove at frontend/src/gap.tsx:1771 and inbox approve/reject at frontend/src/gap.tsx:1867. NodeMesh.dispatch (agents/core/node_mesh.py:141, POST /api/nodes/{id}/dispatch in agents/core/routers/mesh.py) is kernel-mediated (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:34). It only enqueues an ask-tier task for a node client, and none exists.
reviews.remaining: Nothing sends outbound. Peer records store no endpoint, and no code signs a task and POSTs it to another machine's /api/a2a/task, so this box has no `peer dm` equivalent. An approved inbound task has no execution path: decide only changes the status, no turn runs and no reply reaches the sender. The accepted async handle is missing: there is no start/status/stop for an approved remote turn and no peer-authenticated status/result poll. Without them the sender cannot collect a result without holding a connection open. The row depends on H476 (Runs API), which is itself partial. Any execution must stay behind owner approval and node.dispatch/kernel mediation, and no peer-side grant may skip the pending inbox.

reviews.summary: `nerva send` trimite un mesaj către o destinație configurată fără apel de model, cu corpul rezolvat ca la Hermes: argumentul MESSAGE, altfel `-f PATH` (`-` citește stdin), altfel ce e legat pe stdin — un terminal nu e citit niciodată, nici cu `-f -`; un stdin închis e eroare de utilizare, nu traceback; se citește cel mult limita plus un caracter, iar un BOM UTF-8 e eliminat. `-s LINE` e un subiect pe o singură linie *imprimabilă* (orice caracter de control sau separator de linie Unicode e refuzat), purtat de ntfy ca titlu nativ — ASCII imprimabil, cel mult 120, refuzat cu motiv în loc să fie trunchiat tacit de adaptor — și de celelalte canale ca prima linie (subiect, linie goală, mesaj — forma Hermes); `-q` nu tipărește nimic la succes; `--list CANAL` filtrează țintele: un nume care nu poate fi canal direct-send e eroare de utilizare decisă offline, iar un canal pe care un hub mai vechi nu-l listează e exit 1 cu ce listează numit; un argument MESSAGE gol înseamnă „fără mesaj” și cade pe `--file`/stdin. Scara de ieșire e declarată în `--help`: 0 trimis · 1 nelivrat (hub-ul a refuzat sau transportul a eșuat) · 2 utilizare · 3 fără hub · 4 neautorizat. Un fișier binar la `-f` e refuzat cu îndrumarea pentru atașamente, fără să-i reflecte octeții; limita de 4.000 de caractere e regula seam-ului (`carried_length`: subiectul contează unde devine prima linie, nu la ntfy) și CLI-ul aplică aceeași regulă înainte de orice cerere; șirurile venite de la hub sau tastate sunt curățate de caractere de control înainte de terminal. `POST /api/channels/send` primește `subject` opțional (o linie, ≤200), iar seam-ul outbound aplică limita la ce se livrează efectiv. Rate-limit-ul și înregistrarea în IntentLog rămân pe drum. O recenzie adversarială independentă a găsit cincisprezece probleme (două majore: două pin-uri existente din `tests/test_nerva_send.py` rupte), toate remediate în același PR, fiecare cu test.
reviews.remaining: Atașamentele `MEDIA:<path>` nu sunt purtate: o rută care citește căi locale și le trimite pe un canal e egress de fișiere și trebuie să ajungă în spatele Action Kernel-ului, cu un director-sursă delimitat, înainte să existe. Cerința structurală „fără gateway pornit” rămâne o divergență documentată: `nerva send` trece prin hub ca să existe IntentLog și rate-limit. Corpurile peste 4.000 de caractere sunt refuzate, nu fragmentate (Hermes fragmentează per platformă). Slack și Discord rămân reply-only (restul H018); email-ul e exclus deliberat. Nu există adresare `platform:chat_id[:thread]` / `platform:#canal` ca la Hermes: `--channel telegram` înseamnă întotdeauna chat-ul owner-ului. Precedența diverge deliberat: la Hermes argumentul câștigă în fața `--file`, aici ambele deodată e eroare de utilizare. Erorile nu au prefixul `hermes send:`. `JobRunner._send` își păstrează propria rezolvare a destinației (lot-ul jobs). Fără probă live pe un canal real din această sesiune: verificarea a fost prin hub fals și prin ChannelManager-ul real cu adaptoare false.

reviews.summary: **The variant-expansion half of the row.** `hardline_match` no longer screens one spelling: the old single-pass body becomes `_scan_one`, and the public function screens the command in every spelling `_detection_variants` yields — as given, unwrapped from a shell wrapper (`_shell_c_payloads`, recursively to `_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH = 2`), and de-obfuscated (intra-word quotes and escapes collapsed, so `mk""fs` reads as `mkfs`), type-preserving so an argv stays an argv. A non-string command is materialised ONCE up front, which fixes a real one-shot-iterator drain that turned `hardline_match(iter(["rm","-rf","/"]))` from a refusal into a miss. The original slice changed nothing in HARDLINE or the contract, so that pass was additive: an 80,000-case differential fuzz against the pre-slice module returned `refusals_cleared_by_slice = 0`. **That invariant no longer describes the module after PR #1177** (re-assessed 2026-09-19 against the diff 1c5054ea→494a13b2): HARDLINE itself changed — `_CMD` and `network_to_shell` now carry a `_PATH_PREFIX`, so a command word and any wrapper in front of it are read by basename (`/sbin/mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda`, `/usr/bin/sudo /sbin/mkfs.ext4`, `curl … | /bin/sh` all refuse where they returned None; `_recursive_root_removal` compares basenames through `_command_name` too, so `['/usr/local/bin/rm','-rf','/']` refuses instead of only the two literal `/bin/rm` spellings) — and #1177 clears refusals in BOTH directions. Two false-positive classes are cleared on purpose (a `case` label; a heredoc body that quotes a catastrophe), and #1177's mechanisms for them ALSO cleared TRUE refusals the pre-#1177 module gave — **both closed by this slice (H481, branch `hermes/h481-cleared-refusals`, 2026-09-22).** `_strip_case_labels` acted on the flat text of any `case…esac` span and its first-label rule fired after any word-initial `in`, so `(echo case in; reboot); echo esac` — which /bin/sh, dash and bash all execute — went `power_cycle`→None, and the `$IFS`-spliced `(echo case in; mkfs.ext4$IFS/dev/sda); echo esac` / `wipefs$IFS-a$IFS/dev/sda` went mkfs/wipefs→None; the strip now fires only inside a real command-position `case WORD in … esac` region (a `case` keyword, confirmed per match by `_in_command_position`), so all three refuse again — and, made symmetric, a single-line `case $1 in wipe) rm -rf / ;; esac` refuses through the segment path too while `case $1 in shutdown) echo bye ;; esac` still does not. `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` looked only LEFT of `<<`, so `cat <<EOF | sh` / `rm -rf /` / `EOF` and `cat <<'EOF' >x.sh; sh x.sh` / `rm -rf /` / `EOF` went `recursive_root_removal`→None although both hand the body to a shell that runs it; it now also reads the heredoc's own pipeline stages AFTER the redirection and a file the body is written to that a shell later runs, so those refuse, while `bash <<EOF` and a heredoc written to a plain file (`cat > README.md <<'EOF'`) are unchanged. Each shape was reproduced against /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash first (harmless `echo RAN` stand-ins) and pinned red-first. **An independent review of that closure found nine items — three blocking, three major, two minor, one nit — and all nine are fixed in the same branch, each reproduced against the three shells first:** (1) the rewritten `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` counted a shell UPSTREAM of the heredoc's pipe stage (`bash -c echo | cat <<EOF` was `power_cycle` although every shell prints the literal body); (2) it took ANY word of a later shell statement as the run file (`cat > x.yaml <<'EOF'` / `shutdown: graceful` / `EOF` / `bash run.sh x.yaml` was `power_cycle` — the exact config case the heredoc-as-data rule exists for); (3) it read an `xargs`-reached shell as a consumer (`cat <<EOF | xargs -I{} sh -c 'rm -f {}'` with a `reboot.log` line was `power_cycle`; xargs hands lines to the shell as arguments); (4) `_in_command_position` read the compact `if true;then case $1 in` as the word `true;then`, skipped the strip and refused the label (`;then case` / `;do case` were `power_cycle`, label-only in every shell); (5) the new `_CASE_BLOCK_RE` (`\bcase\s+WORD\s+.*?\bin\b.*?\besac\b`) was super-linear on ordinary prose — 4000 chars of case/in prose 10 → 531 ms, eight argv items of it 0.28 → 128 s; (6) the redirect-target branch re-tokenised every later line for every heredoc — 400 `cat <<E >x` blocks in 4000 chars 25 → 2,471 ms, 33.6 KB 109 ms → 97.5 s; the first pass's '78.7 → 78.4 ms' held only for input with no `case` word and never entered that branch; (7) the named-shell file-exec claim was overstated: `(sh x.sh)`, `{ sh x.sh; }`, `if true; then sh x.sh; fi`, `cat x.sh | sh`, `sh -c '. x.sh'`, `. x.sh`, `source x.sh`, `tee x.sh <<EOF; sh x.sh` and a quoted `> "x.sh"` target all ran the body and returned None; (8) this row still said 'eleven across two reviews'; (9) the report said 11 items were red before the fix when 12 were, and the `case WORD in` tightening was pinned by nothing. Fixes: the consumer test looks only at the heredoc's own stage and the stages downstream of it, and a stage counts only when its shell reads its stdin as the script (`_interpreter_call`: a `-c` line, a file operand and an `xargs`-reached shell are data — unless the `-c` line itself launches a stdin-reading shell, so `bash -c sh <<EOF`, `sh -c 'eval "$(cat)"' <<EOF` and `sh -c '. /dev/stdin' <<EOF` still refuse, verified); the file test looks only at the operand a shell RUNS (`_script_runs`: `sh x`, `. x`, `source x`, the same behind `(`/`{`/`then`, a file piped into a stdin-reading shell, a `-c` line that runs it), collects `tee` operands and quoted targets, and the statement lines after a heredoc are tokenised once, lazily, shared across heredocs and decided last heredoc first; the `case` region is found by three single-purpose searches (`case WORD `, then the first `in`, then the first `esac`), each starting where the last stopped, and the keyword-before test accepts the compact `;then`/`;do`. A 671,995-case differential fuzz against origin/main (the suite's 275 pinned literals recombined with 14 statement prefixes, 10 suffixes, 17 heredoc heads, 13 pipe tails, 4 upstream stages, 18 same-line and 10 later-line follow-ups, plus 60,000 seeded-random recombinations) returns refusals_added = 55,059 and refusals_cleared = 22,304 — so the first pass's 'refusals_cleared = 0' is withdrawn, not restated. Every cleared case is explained by one of the two changed mechanisms and belongs to a class no shell executes, each verified with `echo RAN` stand-ins: 19,311 by the consumer rule — a heredoc redirected into a shell that carries its own script or `-c` line, or into `xargs sh` (`sh -c cat <<EOF`, `bash run.sh <<EOF`; main refused both, every shell prints the body) — and 2,993 by the command-position rule — `case` used as an ARGUMENT followed by `label) …` (`echo case $1 in`, `x=1 case …`, `sudo case …`: a parse error in every shell) or a `case … esac` quoted inside heredoc DATA, where main's unconditional strip put a `;` in place of `in label)` and so invented a command position the shell does not have (disabling main's strip makes every one of them None on main too). Every added refusal is explained by the same two mechanisms (33,619 consumer, 21,434 command position, 6 in garbage recombinations with unbalanced quotes reached through the de-obfuscated variant) and adds an executing shape of the kind pinned in the tests. Two false refusals main had are therefore cleared on purpose and pinned as such (`sh -c cat <<EOF`, `bash run.sh <<EOF`). The cleared classes are still cleared on purpose: a `case` label (`case $1 in shutdown) echo bye ;; esac` was `power_cycle`; `_strip_case_labels` drops the pattern inside `case … esac` while keeping the branch body a command position, so `case $1 in wipe) rm -rf / ;; esac` still refuses) and a heredoc body that merely quotes a catastrophe (`cat > README.md <<'EOF'` / `rm -rf / will destroy the box` / `EOF` was `recursive_root_removal` because `segments` ignored the body flag `text` honoured; a body line is now narrowed to its `$()`/backtick substitutions via `_substituted`, so `cat <<EOF` / `$(rm -rf /)` / `EOF` still refuses). **An independent review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed here, and every one was reproduced against a real shell first.** **(1)** The payload was taken as the token immediately after the first `-c`-shaped flag, and the search then stopped — but a shell keeps parsing options until the first non-option operand. `/bin/sh -c -x 'echo RAN'` runs, and `sh -c -x 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'`, `sh -c -- 'rm -rf /'`, `sh -c -e …`, `sh -c -u …` and `sudo sh -c -- 'wipefs -a /dev/sda'` all returned None. One decoy character defeated the entire mechanism, reachable end to end at the transport's spawn seam. The scan steps over options to the first operand now, `--` included. **(2)** A `sh -c` payload is a shell SCRIPT, and a newline separates statements exactly as `;` does — but the newline was squeezed into a space before segmentation, so nothing ever occupied a command position on line 2 and `sh -c 'echo hi` + newline + `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'` passed the floor. **Pressing Enter was the bypass.** Unquoted newlines are separators now, quote-aware so a newline inside a string literal stays data and ordinary prose is not screened as a command. #1177 closed the way that screening could be switched off again: any `<<` opened a heredoc and an unmatched delimiter swallowed every following line as body, so `grep "<<<<<<< HEAD" src/x.py` + newline + `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` returned None; `_heredoc_open` is now quote- and `$(( ))`-aware, skips `<<<` here-strings, and a delimiter that never comes back opens nothing. **(3)** `_CMD`'s command-position anchor learned four more shapes a shell steps over, each a live miss: a brace group (`{ mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda; }`), a compound-command keyword (`if true; then mkfs.ext4 …`), an assignment prefix (`FOO=1 mkfs.ext4 …`) and `env FOO=1 mkfs.ext4 …` — and, with #1177, a fifth: a directory prefix on the command word or on any wrapper before it, spelled as deterministic `component/` chunks with `=` excluded so `FOO=/sbin/mkfs.ext4` stays an assignment and `echo /sbin/mkfs.ext4` stays an argument. **(4)** `busybox` was named as a shell but not as a command-position wrapper, so `busybox mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` — the standard shape on exactly the container targets this module says it keeps the floor on — walked straight through. Four documentation claims were corrected rather than left standing, including the one that said the known-gap list was complete (the first review found five entries missing from it; #1177's second review found six more — a re-expansion budget filled with decoys, a path in front of the command word, a `<<` that opens no heredoc, a heredoc a shell reads as a script, a heredoc body screened as argv, and a `case` label — so the docstring now says twenty-two across four reviews) and the one that said an over-matched flag shape can never clear a refusal (it could: `powershell /c -Command Stop-Computer` returned None where `powershell -Command Stop-Computer` refused — fixed by the same change as (1)). A test whose NAME promised a bound on work it never measured was renamed to what it actually pins, which is the opposite: that depth-3 nesting is a deliberate miss (`test_nesting_past_the_depth_cap_is_a_miss_and_that_is_the_pin`, still present and green). **#1177 also removed the only breadth cap:** `_MAX_SHELL_EXPANSIONS = 8` bounded how many level-1 payloads were unwrapped again, in encounter order — an order the caller writes — so eight cheap `sh -c ok;` decoys in front of `sh -c "sh -c 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'"` returned None where seven refused, and padding a payload past `MAX_ARG_CHARS` had the same effect; every payload is now re-expanded and `_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH` is the only cap, with breadth bounded by the fact that each level's payloads are disjoint substrings of the level above. And the heredoc-as-data rule from the earlier review gained the exception it was missing: `bash <<EOF`, `sh <<'EOF'`, `bash -s <<EOF` and `cat x | sh <<EOF` hand the body to a shell that RUNS it, and `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` now keeps those lines as statements (`bash <<EOF` / `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` / `EOF` was None). All 303 tests in tests/test_local_transport.py pass (up from 206 on the #1177 module: 18 items for the two closures and 54 from the review round, which pin eleven false-refusal shapes and three own-stage data shapes as None, fourteen file-exec spellings, seven payload-launched-shell shapes and four downstream stdin-reading shells as refusals, the compact `;then case` (four), the `case WORD in` opener, four disclosed gaps as still-misses, and six wall-clock bounds two orders of magnitude above the fixed cost; every fix was neutered once — thirteen mutations, each turning its test red). Measured 2026-09-22. **Second adversarial pass (2026-09-22, round two).** A bypass hunter ran 64 shapes under /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash with a PATH-shim stand-in that touches a sentinel and found three the floor cleared while every shell (or bash alone) ran the body: a subshell as the final pipe stage with no `;` (`cat <<EOF | (sh)`, `( sh )`, `(exec sh)` — `_stage_words` left the trailing `)` and `_interpreter_call` read `sh` as running a script named `)`), a `<<<` here-string into a stdin-reading shell (`sh <<< reboot`, `cat <<< reboot | sh` — `_heredoc_open` skipped `<<<` as having no body and nothing modelled the WORD), and a heredoc opened inside a `<(...)` process substitution a leading `source`/shell runs (`source <(cat <<EOF …)`, `sh <(…)`). All three refuse now: `_stage_words` drops trailing group closers, `_herestring_scripts` screens a here-string WORD (dequoted) when its own or a downstream stage is a stdin shell, and `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` gains the process-substitution case; each pinned red-first with the exact bytes. The `_detection_variants` disclosure that the pipe machinery "misses two more pipe shapes" was an undercount and is corrected; the six disclosed gaps that remain (bare `./x.sh`, a variable-carried name, `BASH_ENV`, a heredoc inside `$( )`, `xargs -I{} sh -c '{}'`, `| (cd /tmp; sh)`) were each confirmed to execute exactly as disclosed.
