The logging half of the row, and only that half. `agents/core/security/log_redaction.py` adds `SecretRedactionFilter`, a `logging.Filter` that runs every record's message and its `args` through `SecretScanner.redact` before a handler can write it. The enable flag is snapshotted at import, so an agent-authored mid-session write to `JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION` cannot turn it off — Hermes's `_REDACT_ENABLED` rule, ported deliberately. A cheap length/substring pre-check runs before any regex (≈8.75 µs per clean record, ~1.9× faster than the full scan; the builder's report said 17.22 µs and ~2.1×, which did not reproduce and is corrected here). `setup_logging()` installs it. **Two majors found by an independent review and fixed before landing:** the module's own docstring tripped the AUD-14 raw-env-read ratchet — the prose contained a literal `os.environ[...]` subscript and the ratchet greps file text line by line, so `tests/test_o26_p2_env_config.py` was RED in the delivered tree; and `install_log_redaction()` walked only the root logger's handlers, while `uvicorn` and `uvicorn.access` set `propagate=False` and own theirs, so the production HTTP server's own access and error logs — the ones that carry an `Authorization` header — were structurally unreachable. `install_log_redaction_everywhere()` now covers every handler owned by any logger in `logging.Logger.manager`, and a test drives a real uvicorn `dictConfig` and asserts a key in an access line is masked. Three minors fixed with it: the length floor was defeated by an extra pattern whose NAME collided with a built-in (it now matches by regex SHAPE, one-to-one, and fails closed on any mismatch); an ordinary `%`-format bug was being swallowed into a bare `[redaction-unavailable]` instead of logging's loud diagnostic (now `[log-format-error]` with the message, args and exception, all scanned first); and the test fixture destroyed an ambient `JARVIS_LOG_FILE` for the rest of the session. 47 tests, each fix red-proofed by neutering it. **Follow-up in the same PR:** the blocking bandit gate flagged both swallowed exceptions as NEW findings. Only the filter's last-ditch blank was suppressed (`# nosec B110`, with its reason); `_cover`'s per-handler swallow became a counted, warned coverage figure and `_managed_loggers`' registry-walk failure became a warning, closing the gap this row disclosed. 52 tests at landing. **#1177 (2026-09-19) closed a log-integrity hole inside this same control, re-assessed here rather than refreshed:** the in-place path used to give up and flatten the record to `msg`/`()` whenever a secret straddled the boundary between the format string and an argument ("correctness beats shape"), and flattening is exactly what DELETES a uvicorn access line — `AccessFormatter` unpacks five `record.args`, raises on an empty tuple, and `Handler.handleError` swallows it. `password_assignment`'s `\s*[=:]\s*` jumps the space uvicorn's `'%s - "%s %s HTTP/%s" %d'` puts between the request path and `HTTP/`, so `/login?pwd=` is inert on its own — 11 characters, so the 10-char floor does not even apply; `password_assignment` needs at least six unquoted (four quoted) non-space characters after the separator and the bare argument has none — and a match once rendered: any unauthenticated client could erase its own access-log entry by appending `?pwd=` to a path. `SecretRedactionFilter._mask_joined_args` now replaces whole arguments — one at a time first, then cumulatively for a secret assembled from several — the cumulative pass can also mask an innocent argument that sits between two culprits (`"%s HTTP/%s and %s HTTP/%s"` with two `?pwd=` paths loses the `1.1` between them): over-redaction, never a leak, and the arity still holds — — until the re-rendered line is scanner-clean, keeping the tuple's arity, putting an argument back when its conversion refuses the mask (uvicorn's `%d` status code stays an int), and naming the mask after the pattern the scanner reports, `[REDACTED:straddling_secret]` when it cannot. Flattening survives only for a straddle no masking can clean, i.e. the secret sits in the format string itself (`pwd=%s`). Seven tests were added — four of them through uvicorn's real `dictConfig` plus `setup_logging()`, asserting the access line for `/login?pwd=`, `/admin?password=`, `/x?passwd:` and `/z?api_key="12345678` survives with the straddling text gone (three are `password_assignment` straddles; `/z?api_key="12345678` is `generic_api_key` matching `api_key="12345678 HTTP/1.1"`, the access line's own closing quote completing the quoted value) and the client, verb and status kept — and the earlier straddle test was inverted to assert `args == ("[REDACTED:anthropic_key]",)` instead of `()`. `agents/core/log.py` did not change and still installs the filter from `setup_logging()`. `tests/test_log_redaction.py` collects 64 tests, all green on 2026-09-19. Nothing in #1177 touches the other six paths the row names; the still-owed list below stands.
reviews.remaining: This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies `redact.py` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a `cat .env` from `terminal_run` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning `[redaction-unavailable]` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID `«redacted:ghp_…»` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), `code_file=True` sparing source constants, `_mask_control_split_tokens()` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared `.env` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose `addFilter` fails is counted and published through `uncovered_handler_count()` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a `loggerDict` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (`# nosec B110`), where a `logging.Filter` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. `install_log_redaction()` remains exported although the `everywhere` variant is what production uses. **A later slice's full-suite run surfaced one more thing about this control, recorded here rather than fixed:** the scanner's `high_entropy_secret` pattern matches an ordinary filesystem path. Under `-n auto --dist loadfile` a warning naming a pytest tmp file arrived as `truncated: [REDACTED:high_entropy_secret].md`, which is what a real operator would see when a log line names a file with a long random-looking segment — a debuggability cost the module docstring already warns about in general terms, now with a concrete case. Separately, `setup_logging()` installs the filter on every handler of every logger and nothing took it back off, so every later test on the same xdist worker ran under a live redactor. The installer is PRODUCTION code, not the tests: `agents/run.py` calls `setup_logging()` at module level, so importing it installs the filter during pytest COLLECTION — before any fixture runs — and eight test files import it; `agents/web.py` calls it from the FastAPI lifespan, so any test that drives the app installs it again; five test files call it directly on top of that. There is no list of leaking files to fix. The cleanup therefore lives in `tests/conftest.py` as an autouse fixture that strips unconditionally BEFORE each test as well as after — a snapshot-and-restore fixture, which is what the two neighbouring isolation fixtures do and what this was first written as, treats a collection-time install as pre-existing and preserves it for the life of the worker. That version went green locally and RED in CI on exactly the test it was meant to fix. The first attempt at it matched by `isinstance` and silently did nothing: `agents/` is on `sys.path`, so `core.security.log_redaction` and `agents.core.security.log_redaction` are two module objects over this one file with two distinct `SecretRedactionFilter` classes, and the root handler was carrying the other one. The match is by class name now, and four paired tests pin both halves — including the alternate import path, which is the case the first attempt missed.

reviews.summary: **Gap (a) of four, plus the row's `chmod 0600 atomic writes` clause.** Both pairing credentials stop being written in the clear: `SenderPairing._code` becomes `_code_hash`, and each deeplink entry moves from being keyed by its raw token to being keyed by an opaque 8-byte id with the token's salted digest inside the entry. Verification hashes the candidate and `hmac.compare_digest`s two fixed-length hex digests, so neither the length nor any prefix of the stored credential leaks and the deeplink failure reasons stay indistinguishable. A one-time migration accepts a pre-H497 plaintext file, rehashes it in memory and rewrites it, preserving each link's channel, `created_at` and `expires_at` — an upgrade never locks the owner out nor resurrects a spent link. `_digest` encodes with `surrogatepass` so a lone surrogate (from a hand-edited store, or from the body of the one pairing route a stranger is meant to reach) misses instead of raising. `atomic_write_json` lands every JsonStore file owner-only. **The review found three false claims and all three are corrected — two of them by changing the code rather than the prose.** (1) The module docstring said the store "holds nothing that can pair anybody". True of a 192-bit deeplink token; **false of the pairing code**, which is whatever the owner typed: a four-digit code was recovered from the file by exhausting 10,000 candidates in **0.006 s** and then used to pair. The code is now stretched with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 240,000 rounds, `kdf` and `rounds` stored beside each digest so raising the count later cannot lock an owner out, and a record written by the first cut is upgraded in place on the next successful pair — the one moment the plaintext is in hand — while a FAILED guess leaves it untouched. The deeplink token stays on plain SHA-256, deliberately: `redeem_deeplink` hashes once per outstanding link, so a slow hash there is a CPU lever for any stranger sending `/start junk`, and at 192 bits there is nothing for stretching to buy. (2) The salt comment defended leaving the code unstretched by pointing at the store-wide guess budget — an ONLINE control held in memory, which has no bearing on an attacker who has read the file, the exact threat at-rest hashing answers. Rewritten to say what stretching does and does not promise. (3) `atomic_write_json` claimed its chmod-before-replace ordering left no readable window. It left a shorter one: `write_text` creates the tmp at `0o666 & ~umask` and the whole payload is in it before the chmod runs. The tmp is now created EMPTY through a descriptor opened 0600 and closed again (json_store.py:74) before the unchanged `Path.write_text` call at json_store.py:78 opens that existing file — a mode `write_text` leaves alone — so no byte of a pairing digest ever lands in a file whose mode the umask chose; pinned by a test that neutralises `os.chmod` and still requires 0600. **#1179 (adversarial wave two) touched only this row's test file; `pairing.py` and `json_store.py` are byte-identical to the #1171 state.** The review claimed every inbound `/start` costs 240k rounds outside any budget. It does not, for two reasons worth keeping apart. First, `/start` never reaches the code KDF at all: a Telegram `/start <payload>` is routed by `TelegramChannel._maybe_pair_deeplink` (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:591-629) to `redeem_deeplink`, which is one plain-SHA-256 `_digest` per outstanding link, and every other chat message reaches `gate_inbound` through `ChannelGateway.route` with `code=kwargs.get("pairing_code")` (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:82), a kwarg no channel in the tree ever sets — so the one path on which a stranger can spend a KDF run is `POST /api/channels/pairing/request`, the route the new test's docstring names (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:469). Second, on that path the KDF sits behind a budget: `_code_guess_budget_spent` (pairing.py:606) is store-wide and is consulted at pairing.py:587, BEFORE `_code_matches` at pairing.py:592, so a stranger rotating sender ids — the per-sender bucket is keyed on an id the caller chose — buys at most `_MAX_CODE_GUESSES_PER_WINDOW` = 10 KDF runs per 10-minute window however many ids they present, and a request presenting no code never reaches the KDF at all. `test_the_kdf_a_stranger_can_trigger_stays_inside_the_guess_budget` (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:466) now pins that by counting `_stretch` calls rather than timing them, so a slow CI box cannot fail it: 60 requests from 60 fresh ids → 10 runs with 50 turned away `rate_limited` (with the budget check removed it is 60 runs and 0 refusals — re-reproduced at this re-verification), and zero runs for a code-less request. That is the code-side counterpart of the deeplink decision above — the token stays unstretched because nothing budgets `redeem_deeplink`'s per-link compare; the code may be stretched because its compare sits behind one. Nothing in #1179's persona-scan (`agent.py`, `quarantine.py`) or MCP-stdio (`mcp/client.py`) work touches this row. **Second slice (2026-09-22) — one store per process, and the one-use claim made true for the deeplink path.** The module promised a deeplink is "one use, ever", and inside one instance it was; production held two. The orchestrator registers the long-lived `sender_pairing` (the gateway gates on it, the pairing router mints and revokes on it) and `TelegramChannel` was built in `web.py` without one, so `_maybe_pair_deeplink` opened a throwaway `SenderPairing()` per `/start <token>`. A `JsonStore` reads its file once and every save writes the whole in-memory state back, so the two were two stores, not two views of one: a token redeemed over Telegram was spent in the throwaway and still outstanding in the orchestrator's copy, whose next save — any save; a stranger knocking is enough — wrote it back to disk, where the next throwaway redeemed it again and paired a second sender. With a relocated data root the two did not even share a file (the registry spelled a cwd-relative `memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`, the throwaway used `data_path(...)`), so under `JARVIS_HOME` no link ever redeemed. Fixed by wiring, not by hardening the store: `TelegramChannel` takes `pairing=` and `web.py` passes `gateway.pairing`, the same object by identity; an adapter handed nothing refuses to pair rather than building one (same reply as a bad token, a warning naming the cause, the message still swallowed); the registry entry spells the path through `data_path("sender_pairing.json")`. Five tests in `tests/test_telegram_pairing_shared_store.py` pin the resurrection with two instances over one file as the premise, a spent link staying spent after the owner's store saves, `revoke_deeplinks()` reaching the live adapter, an un-wired channel building nothing, and the real lifespan handing the channel `orch.sender_pairing` under the data root; red-proofed against the unpatched sources.
reviews.remaining: **The row names four hardening gaps; (a) is closed, (c) is closed for the deeplink path, (b) and (d) are open.** (c) *revocation reaching live adapters*: `revoke_deeplinks()` and `unpair()` now act on the one object the Telegram adapter redeems from and the gateway consults on every message, so there is no second copy for a link or an approval to survive in — pinned by `test_revoking_on_the_shared_store_reaches_the_live_telegram_adapter`. Slack and Discord have no deeplink path and gate through the same gateway instance. Still outstanding, from the row itself: (b) *no lockout after N failed attempts* — the row wants a 1 h lockout after 5 failed approvals, checked BEFORE the pending lookup so a code already in flight cannot be brute-forced past it; there is still only a rate limit and an in-memory guess budget, both of which reset on restart. (d) *no admin-vs-user command split on channels*, so any paired sender gets every command; the row wants a split with an always-allowed floor of `{help, whoami}`. **Unaddressed from the Hermes column:** pairing-code GENERATION (8 characters from a 32-char unambiguous alphabet via `secrets.choice`) and the code's 1 h TTL — the code here never expires; "max 3 pending per platform" (the store bounds 200 globally); "1 request per user per 10 min" (it is 5); `unauthorized_dm_behavior` treating inbox-shaped platforms differently from chat-shaped ones; and the ordered authorization union (allow-all flag → pairing approvals → per-platform allowlist → global allowlist → global allow-all → default DENY), which is still an ad-hoc sequence in `is_allowed`/`gate_inbound`. **Two honest limits of the second slice.** The store itself still has no defence against a second instance — the guarantee is one instance per process by construction, and the premise test says so in words. And an install that had relocated its data root (`JARVIS_HOME`) and paired senders through the HUD kept them in `<cwd>/memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`; the store now opens under the data root, so those senders are held once more until re-approved (the owner's allowlisted ids never lived in that file and are unaffected). **And the limit carried from the first slice.** Stretching is a work factor, not a wall: a four-digit code goes from milliseconds to minutes, an eight-character mixed-alphabet code becomes infeasible, and **nothing enforces a floor on what the owner types** — `PairingCodeBody` caps the length at 128 and sets no minimum — while generating the code for them, the row's own prescription, is not implemented.

reviews.summary: Nerva now warns about a dangerous host posture, as Hermes does, on top of a network half that was already stronger. assert_safe_bind (agents/core/boot_guards.py) still refuses an unauthenticated non-loopback bind and prints the exact env vars that fix it, and GET /api/security/posture still reports the secrets backend, skill signing, sandbox isolation and guardrails honestly. agents/core/host_posture.py adds the host half: three read-only checks that never block and never change anything, each answering ok, warn or unknown (it could not tell, never a false green), with a reason, what it saw and the fix. check_root (agents/core/host_posture.py:71) warns when the process runs as root (euid 0) on any host, headless included, or elevated on Windows (IsUserAnAdmin). check_sshd (agents/core/host_posture.py:168) reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config the way sshd does (_SshdScan, agents/core/host_posture.py:120): Include files are read in place, relative paths from /etc/ssh, each pattern's hits in lexical order, at most 16 deep; Keyword value, Keyword=value and trailing comments are accepted and keywords and values are case-insensitive; the first PasswordAuthentication outside a Match block wins, so a drop-in Included at the top overrides the main file; a Match block (to the end of its file, an Include inside it conditional) never sets the global value but a Match block that turns passwords on warns too; an absent directive is the sshd default yes and warns; no sshd_config is ok; an unreadable file is unknown unless the answer was read elsewhere; an unrecognised value is unknown. check_container_storage (agents/core/host_posture.py:241) detects a container (/.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, or a docker, kubepods, containerd, libpod or lxc cgroup of PID 1, in_container) and then finds the mount the data root (resolved through symlinks) lives on in /proc/self/mountinfo (parse_mountinfo with its octal escapes, mount_of taking the longest containing mount point and the later of two stacked mounts): the container's own root filesystem or a tmpfs warns, a volume or bind mount is ok, no mountinfo or no mount is unknown. run_checks and report (agents/core/host_posture.py:273, :287) run the three independently, a failing check becoming an unknown row. The hub logs each warning once per process at start, after logging is set up, off the event loop (log_startup, agents/web.py lifespan). GET /api/security/posture (admin) gains host: the three findings and a warnings count (agents/core/routers/security.py). python scripts/doctor.py and nerva doctor show them as the advisory rows host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords and container_storage at the end of the report: a warning is warn with the fix and never fails the verdict, a check that could not tell or could not run is skip, never ok (check_host_posture, scripts/doctor.py:247). The module is stdlib only so the doctor can use it on a broken install. The shipped Dockerfile has no USER, so a stock container now shows the root warning; running the image as a non-root user is left to the deploy. Tests: tests/test_h501_host_posture.py (42), with real sshd_config trees in a temporary directory (drop-ins read first and last, lexical order, absolute and quoted Includes, Match blocks in the main and in an included file, a trailing comment naming a file, an Include loop) and real mountinfo text. 55 mutants: 53 killed after five cases were added; the other two were dead code, removed.

**`JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE` flips from opt-in to default-on**, so a spawned stdio MCP server is handed the `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` baseline plus its own `env` instead of `os.environ.copy()` — API keys, tokens, proxies and every `JARVIS_*` setting withheld. A second flag, `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV`, is the owner-reachable migration remedy: a comma-separated list of host variable names that pass the baseline even when `_SECRET_LIKE` matches them. `_merged_env()` emits one INFO line per connect counting host values the child does not receive, carrying **no variable name and no value**. `GET /api/admin/mcp` rows gain `env_baseline`. And Nerva's own WorldView MCP server is handed its `WORLDVIEW_API_URL`, which the flip would otherwise have silently replaced with the built-in `http://localhost:4000`. **The review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed.** **(1)** `routers/mcp.py` asserted an invariant the code did not hold: the comment said a row that spawns no subprocess reports `None` "rather than a badge it has not earned" and enumerated two cases. A third exists and is the only one an owner can create today — `POST /api/admin/mcp` does no command validation, so a row with a whitespace-only command or a shell metacharacter persists, and `connect()` answers `unsafe_command` from `_command_argv()` **before** `create_subprocess_exec`. Such a row reported `env_baseline: true` for a child that never existed; the row now calls the same `_command_argv()` `connect` does, so the two cannot disagree, and the guard test carries both spellings. **(2)** `BACKLOG.md` still shipped the pre-flip claim and therefore stated the OPPOSITE of the code — "opt-in, default-off … keeps working until the owner opts in" — in the one file `CLAUDE.md` tells a reader to query for what is delivered. That is exactly the misreading the slice's own documentation work exists to prevent. Corrected, and `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` now covers BACKLOG.md too, including a check that the "opt-in, default-off" wording is gone. Two wording corrections went with them: the `env_baseline` field describes the live FLAG, i.e. the posture for the NEXT spawn, not the environment the running child holds (`_merged_env()` runs once at connect, the row is read per request); and the migration note steered the reader at auth failures only, when the flip also withholds `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` — plumbing whose absence produces an ImportError, a hang or a connect timeout, nothing resembling an auth error. **#1179 (cda4e19d, adversarial-review finding 4) widened the DISCLOSURE, not the guarantee, and touched two of the five cited files.** `agents/core/mcp/client.py`: the module docstring now names a SECOND route by which a hostile child recovers the withheld keys — not only `/proc/<ppid>/environ` but the **filesystem**, which the baseline narrows not at all: `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` in the child reaches the very file `plugin_manager.build` read those keys from (`client.py:17-36`). New `_CWD_SECRET_FILES = (".env", ".env.local")` and `cwd_secret_files(cwd)` (`client.py:215-242`; `None` → `Path.cwd()`, the inherited default; unreadable and missing both count as absent) report which of them the child can open, and `_merged_env()` calls it right after the withheld-count INFO line — only when something WAS withheld (`:555`) and such a file is readable — emitting one WARNING per connect, "withholding is undercut — .env readable in the server's working directory", carrying **filenames only, never a variable name** (`client.py:565-571`), because a variable name enumerates which providers the box holds while `.env` tells the owner nothing new. Deliberately not a refusal: refusing to spawn over a `.env` breaks every dev checkout and re-pointing `cwd` breaks every server that resolves a relative path, so the module's posture stays *withhold and say so*. `tests/test_mcp_transports.py` gains `test_cwd_secret_files_reports_what_the_child_can_open` (`:830`; a directory named `.env.local` is not a file) and `test_the_withheld_count_is_not_announced_alone_when_a_dotenv_is_reachable` (`:854`; WARNING level, `OPENAI_API_KEY` absent from the line, silent when no file is reachable). Everything else above is as assessed: the default-on flag (`client.py:90`, `:190`), `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST`/`_SECRET_LIKE` (`:161-176`), `stdio_env_extra_allowed` (`:197-208`), the count-only INFO line (`:556-559`) are untouched, and `worldview_write.py` and `tests/test_mcp_admin.py` are byte-identical to the prior stamp. **The later fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) touched two cited files without touching this slice:** `client.py` gained `tool_patterns_over_bounds` (`client.py:138-154`) and a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (`:407-418`), and `admin_mcp_add` now also refuses a `tools_allow`/`tools_deny` over the 64-pattern / 128-char bounds (`routers/mcp.py:216-222`); neither reads the environment, the baseline flags or `env_baseline`, so the env code above only moved (+19 lines up to `MCPServer.__init__`'s filter block, +31 after it). The docstring pin `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` (`test_mcp_transports.py:554`) survived the rewrite because both strings it asserts remain (`/proc/<ppid>/environ` at `client.py:21`, "defence in depth, not a security boundary" at `:30`). 41/41 cited tests green (33 + 8), re-run at the bounds-change head. MCP transport audit collateral review (2026-10-09): the route adds only fixed-field authentication telemetry at the existing RPC gate. This row's admin/listing, validation or transport-auth behavior and remaining limitations are unchanged; its previously current mcp.py pin and explicit coordinates were reviewed. MCP token audit collateral review (2026-10-10): the six-line insertion follows successful inbound token signing and only submits fixed-field telemetry. Existing admin configuration, stdio environment, outbound filters/trust and absence of ACP session-scoped servers or outbound approval/audit are unchanged; cited coordinates precede the insertion. Independent source review and all five cited/relevant MCP suites (67 tests) preserve this verdict and its gaps.
reviews.remaining: **The documented per-server `env` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.** `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field (`routers/mcp.py:145-157`, no `model_config`), `POST /api/admin/mcp` drops the key (pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`), and neither `to_config` (`client.py:798-812`) nor `load_from_config` (`:814-849`) writes or reads one — the module docstring says as much at `client.py:41-45`. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the **host-wide** `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV` (`:92-98`, "Host-wide, not per-server"), which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` §P28.3 with both options. **Related and also owner-level:** `XAUTHORITY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are both on `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` (`client.py:169`), and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped (`_SECRET_LIKE` at `:174-176` matches the `AUTH` in `XAUTHORITY`) while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. **And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:** this is **defence in depth, not a security boundary**, and since #1179 the module states that ceiling by TWO routes rather than one (`client.py:17-36`). The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of `/proc/<ppid>/environ`; and the baseline narrows the **filesystem** not at all — `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` hands back exactly the keys that were withheld, which `cwd_secret_files()` now says out loud at connect (WARNING, filenames only, `client.py:565-571`) rather than leaving the owner to infer a protection from the withheld count alone. What the baseline buys is that a *careless* or *curious* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's `JARVIS_*` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise; closing the filesystem route as well as the `/proc` one needs real process isolation (separate UID, namespace or container — `client.py:33-36`), which is not shipped. **Unaddressed from the row:** there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary (the docstring itself calls the screener "still-unshipped", `client.py:34`), and `POST /api/admin/mcp` still stores `req.command` verbatim after checking only transport, trust tier, tool-filter shape and bounds, and duplicate name (`routers/mcp.py:188-241`, `:184`); the only shape check is `_command_argv()`'s shell-metacharacter/NUL refusal at connect (`client.py:519-529`), which is not a screener. #1179 changed none of this — it explicitly chose disclosure over refusal. This slice hardens what the child *receives*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to *be*.

reviews.summary: archive_safe is the only module in Nerva that reads an archive. Backup verify and restore unpack through extract_tar_path (agents/core/archive_safe.py:573; agents/core/backup.py:598, agents/core/backup.py:667). Marketplace install_from_zip unpacks through extract_zip_bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:637; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:816). The old backup._safe_extract and the marketplace _safe_targets+extractall pass are gone. An AST scan (tests/test_archive_safe.py:702, with probes at tests/test_archive_safe.py:688) fails when any other product module imports tarfile or zipfile outside a write-only allowlist, opens an archive for reading or calls an extract-family method. normalize_member (agents/core/archive_safe.py:122) folds backslash to '/' first. It then refuses empty, NUL, POSIX-absolute, Windows-absolute, UNC and drive-lettered names, and any '..' or empty part. Only regular files and directories are written. Symlink, hardlink, device, fifo and sparse tar members raise (agents/core/archive_safe.py:504), and so do symlink, device, fifo, socket and encrypted zip entries (agents/core/archive_safe.py:596). _Planner (agents/core/archive_safe.py:182) validates every member before the first write: name, type, in-archive conflicts and duplicates, member count and declared bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:257). It also checks the destination's existing content (agents/core/archive_safe.py:286): a link on the way to a member is refused, and so is a directory where a file goes (tests/test_archive_safe.py:365, tests/test_backup.py:471). The pre-scan reads the stream to its end (agents/core/archive_safe.py:522), so a bad gzip CRC, trailing data or a corrupt header part-way through is a refusal, not a shortened tree (tests/test_archive_safe.py:482, tests/test_archive_safe.py:517). Bytes are counted again while streaming (agents/core/archive_safe.py:389). The byte budget is clamped to free space plus the blocks of the single-link files the archive replaces (agents/core/archive_safe.py:314), so an in-place --force restore fits (tests/test_backup.py:443). PAX and GNU long-name header payloads are capped before tarfile reads them, 1 MiB each and 256 MiB in total (agents/core/archive_safe.py:461, agents/core/archive_safe.py:483; tests/test_backup.py:515). A link or hardlinked name at a member's path is unlinked and the file is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, never written through (agents/core/archive_safe.py:373; tests/test_archive_safe.py:323, tests/test_archive_safe.py:349). Backups take their caps from JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_MEMBERS and JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES (agents/core/backup.py:86); skill packages use SKILL_PACKAGE_LIMITS (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:42). On the producing side, create_backup writes both the encrypted and the plaintext branch through atomic_write, a sibling temp file that is fsynced and then os.replace'd (agents/core/archive_safe.py:654; agents/core/backup.py:415, agents/core/backup.py:420). Archives are GNU-format tar (agents/core/backup.py:474). The export walk skips symlinks (agents/core/archive_safe.py:715; agents/core/backup.py:401). publish_skill uses it on the staged copy it signs (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:392); the copy itself is built from the bytes of one source snapshot, which refuses a linked folder, a link or non-regular member and a file that changed while read (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:375), which has its own test (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:219). Every other name, hardlinked ones included, is archived as its own regular member (agents/core/backup.py:434, agents/core/backup.py:458; tests/test_backup.py:388). verify and restore compare the manifest's file_count with what the archive held (agents/core/backup.py:625; tests/test_backup.py:430). install_from_zip stages inside skills_dir, runs the signature gate there, and only then renames the tree into place (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:854, agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:885). A non-zip upload is a 400 refusal (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:194). Staging left by a killed install is swept once it is an hour old (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:773; tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:203). Restore stays an operator CLI action. It prints 'partial restore' when a failure came after the first write (agents/core/backup.py:716) and 'nothing restored' only for a pre-scan refusal (agents/core/backup.py:722). tests/test_backup.py:606 pins that no product module, script or subprocess caller reaches it. The pre-scan also refuses a component longer than the destination's NAME_MAX or a path past PATH_MAX, which the existing-path walk cannot see under a new directory (agents/core/archive_safe.py:251; tests/test_archive_safe.py:726), and a write the destination refuses mid-restore (permissions, a full disk) is a named ArchiveRejected marked partial, never a traceback (agents/core/archive_safe.py:445; tests/test_archive_safe.py:738). A restore leaves the archive's manifest in the target; create_backup never archives a top-level backup_manifest.json from the data root (agents/core/backup.py:482), so a backup of a restored root carries one manifest and verifies, restores and serves the forget purge's verified pre-snapshot (tests/test_backup.py:636, tests/test_backup.py:675). A backup of a restored root made before this change carries that name twice; verify and restore accept exactly that one repeat, last wins as tarfile resolved it, and count the dropped copy against the manifest's file_count (agents/core/backup.py:599, agents/core/backup.py:642; tests/test_backup.py:651). The repeat is bounded: the dropped copy still counts against the member and byte caps, and a third copy or any other duplicate is refused (agents/core/archive_safe.py:220, agents/core/archive_safe.py:223; tests/test_archive_safe.py:768, tests/test_archive_safe.py:775, tests/test_archive_safe.py:790). Known limit: backups made on main from a data root holding a symlink or hardlink fail verify and restore by design.

Startup validates all configured CA bundle paths and certifi, loads them through SSLContext, requires actual certificates, and supplies named repair instructions. Model egress uses an explicit trust context; invalid CA paths never imply verify=False. Per-target insecure overrides are explicit, loudly logged and ignored in hardened mode. Functional adaptation retained from the existing implementation: custom bundles may contain a valid short EC or pinned self-signed certificate; the 1024-byte minimum is reserved for the multi-root certifi bundle. Actual SSL parsing and certificate presence validate custom trust material instead of rejecting a valid anchor by byte length. All 45 TLS tests plus 22 plugin-egress tests pass, including real generated certificates and a loopback HTTPS server that fails without and succeeds with the owner CA. No external-provider connection or host trust-store change was performed.

**The write half, as a generic mechanism rather than a special case.** `agents/core/tool_rpc.py` gains a registrar-owned *call classifier*: a gated tool may register a pure function over one call's args returning bounded labels. `handle()` stamps them onto the durable approval card's payload and appends the notice to the card title; `execute()` re-derives them from the args about to run and refuses with `approval_class_mismatch` unless the approved card carried the same `class` — so a card approved as a scratch note cannot be redeemed against a write to SOUL.md. `_classify` fails closed (a raising, non-Mapping, over-long or non-alphanumeric result refuses the call rather than letting it through unlabelled) and strips the reserved `tool`/`args`/`target` keys so labels cannot rewrite the card's identity. `agents/core/file_tools.py` registers `FileTools.classify_mutation` for `file_write` and `file_delete`, matches on the BASENAME in any directory inside the roots (an instruction file is wherever the harness that reads it looks — `_load_soul` alone searches three), carries a `steers_future_runs` flag into the kernel Action payload, and adds a secondary floor in `_mutate`. Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 26 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:89), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, require('child_process').exec, a bare exec( in a file that imports child_process, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or `%`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, createCipher without an IV on any receiver, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote `<script>` without integrity=. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags `${{ github.event.* }}` inside a GitHub Actions `run:` step, on the run line or in its `|`/`>` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a `- run: |` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: `model.eval()` and `obj.eval()`, `def eval(`, `yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)`, `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`, `regex.exec()`, an `===` comparison with innerHTML, `hashlib.md5(data)`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns `{rule, line, message}`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at `\n` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a `scan-incomplete` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. `.env`, `.env.*` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1182) adds `code_warnings` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), `code_warning_count` and a title notice (`code not fully scanned` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a `./` or `//` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's `approval_required` answer carries `code_warnings`/`code_warning_count` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:197), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1634): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:972), the model reads `code_warnings` with a `code_guidance` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer `code_warnings` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:506) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1208), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a `scan-incomplete` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's `code_warnings` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:462), and generate_skill resets them first, so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and [learn:] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is `security.code_guidance` (agents/core/settings_db.py:240, on by default; only an explicit off turns it off, an unreadable store keeps it on, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:105). An aliased child_process module (`cp.exec`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. The review round added crafted megabytes (one per quadratic rule) scanned in under a second and a card labelled promptly through the ToolRPC intake, the time and size cuts, the pause reply driven through the agent loop, skill_propose's warnings and the reset, the symlink and path spellings, a package padded with assets, the `- run: |` block, the wrapped and nested calls, the child_process and createCipher spellings, CR/form-feed/U+2028 lines, the dotfiles and the safe-mode switch. The review round's 44 mutants were all killed, ten after seven cases were added.

The row's other two asks hold, and lot 1 (H691) tightened the proxy half. Trusted-proxy entries are validated as bounded CIDRs at agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107 and :165 (note :308 only WARNS on a wide entry, it does not refuse). uvicorn's own forwarding-header allowlist (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, --forwarded-allow-ips) now refuses boot from the boot pass, which runs after the .env files load, when an entry is a wildcard, a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES and loopback (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570). serve.py switches uvicorn's proxy-header layer off, X-Forwarded-Proto is believed only from a listed peer, and the rate limiter's localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:779), so an unlisted same-box proxy is throttled. CORS is validated with reported rejections at agents/core/cors_policy.py, and no CORS middleware is installed at all by default. The WebSocket clause is excluded by the row itself and the exclusion still holds: no WebSocket server route exists in agents/ (lot 1's _ForwardedProtoMiddleware maps a listed proxy's scheme onto ws/wss scopes but adds no route), agents/web.py:798-799 says a future one must call host_accepted() itself, and agents/web.py:675 is the only ASGI app. 104/104 tests pass across the five relevant suites on the lot-1 head. What keeps this off "equivalent" is the residual the code names about itself at agents/web.py:800-802: _PROBE_PATHS is exempt from the guard (:824-825), so `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz. Re-confirmed live on the lot-1 head: a rebound page therefore still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts — cross-origin, because rebinding makes the browser treat them as same-origin. That is low severity and a deliberate operability trade, not an oversight, but it is a real deviation from Hermes' clause as written (which has no carve-out) and it is shippable work, so the row is partial rather than equivalent.
reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:767, applied at :824-825), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:800-802 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body.

A spoken reply now sounds like speech rather than read-out markdown, as Hermes requires, at every text-to-speech entry point. agents/core/voice/speech_text.py is the one normaliser (for_speech, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:152). It drops <think>/<thinking>/<reasoning> blocks, an unclosed one to the end, and everything before a closing tag that never opened. It drops fenced code (``` or ~~~, an unclosed fence to the end) and HTML tags. [text](url) reads as its text, ![alt](url) as its alt, and a bare or <autolinked> URL as "link"; the URL no longer eats a closing parenthesis or the sentence's full stop, so "doc (https://…)." is "doc (link).". Headings, list items (-, *, +, •, 1., 1), task boxes), block quotes and table rows lose their markers and end with a full stop (_line, :124). Table cells read with commas; separator rows and horizontal rules are dropped. Bold, italic, strikethrough and inline-code markers go and their words stay (_inline, :113), with word guards so 2*3*4 and my_var_name survive. Symbols are said in the reply's language (_symbols, :104, WORDS, :79): & as and/și, % as percent/la sută, -> → => as to/spre, and °, °C, °F as degrees/grade (Celsius, Fahrenheit). The language comes from the request, else a ro-RO-… voice, else the engine default (speech_lang, :95). Emoji go: pictographs, flags, keycaps, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, variation selectors and tag flags (_EMOJI, :61). Fish [emotion] tags are kept intact. Conducta de transcriere validează, pregătește și livrează: acceptă octeți direct (`BytesIO`, fără fișier temporar, deci vorbirea nu ajunge pe disc), îi mărginește, trece rezultatul prin filtrul de halucinații și întoarce santinele oneste în loc de text inventat. Are acum doi consumatori — ruta HTTP a browserului și canalul Telegram — peste un singur motor local partajat, nu unul per apelant. reviews.remaining: Un singur backend. Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, `local_command`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC `TranscriptionProvider`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin `plugin.egress` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. Cache-ul motorului stă tot în `routers/voice.py`, care e casa greșită pentru el; canalul îl importă în loc să-l dubleze, iar mutarea lui e o schimbare separată. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat.

reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul. Named speech compatibility review: the Whisper hallucination filter and decoded-duration handling remain on the native transcribe path; named commands preserve the existing exact-sentinel behavior. Hallucination and speech selection regressions pass.

A turn can read a document directly through file_read instead of relying on pre-indexed memory. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). Local 2026-10-09 parser-backed file_read admission refuses an observed on-disk PDF/DOCX size above 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB) as document_too_large before parser discovery or extraction. Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds.

reviews.summary: Nerva has no ACP editor-agent surface. No handler for session/new, load, resume or fork exists anywhere under agents/, and the editor-surface row H542 is itself still missing, so nothing can accept an mcpServers array from an editor. The only outbound MCP registry is the process-wide MCPManager (agents/core/mcp/client.py:728-730), which holds a single servers dict. It is filled by the admin-guarded POST /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:188-189) and the persisted global config. There is no per-session server scope, no per-session mcp-<name> toolset, no bounded discovery join and no late refresh of the tool registry. tests/test_mcp_client.py and tests/test_mcp_admin.py exercise only the global registry. Existing admin configuration, stdio environment, outbound filters/trust and absence of ACP session-scoped servers or outbound approval/audit are unchanged; cited coordinates precede the insertion. reviews.remaining: Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (4) A scheduled late refresh that re-reads the session's tool list after slow discovery finishes. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's.

reviews.summary: Filtrele allow/deny pe nume și glob (`tools_allow`/`tools_deny`, potrivite cu `fnmatchcase` pe numele original al uneltei) restrâng atât listarea, cât și apelarea uneltelor MCP; deny prevalează (`tool_visible`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:603-610). `_list_tools` nu oferă o unealtă ascunsă (:596-601), iar `MCPServer.call_tool` răspunde `tool_filtered` înainte să plece vreun frame (:616-617), deci scoaterea unei unelte din filtru o revocă imediat, și la apel, nu doar la înregistrare. Un filtru malformat îngustează, nu lărgește: un allow care nu e listă devine `[]` (`_clean_tool_patterns`, :124-135). Limitele (64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere, :120-121) sunt fail-closed. Ruta de add (`admin_mcp_add`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:214-223) refuză cu 400 `{"error": "invalid_tool_filter", "field": ...}` un `tools_allow` sau `tools_deny` peste limite, în loc să-l taie (`tool_patterns_over_bounds`, client.py:138-154), la fel ca pe o valoare care nu e listă sau pe o intrare goală. Un deny care nu poate fi păstrat (peste 64 de pattern-uri, un pattern peste 128 de caractere, sau care nu e listă) venit dintr-un config editat manual prin `load_from_config` îngustează serverul la nimic (`tools_allow = []`) și loghează un avertisment (:407-418), pentru că un deny tăiat ar face din nou vizibilă unealta pe care o numea. It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds. Local 2026-10-09 PDF text-layer coverage uses one shared parser traversal per request and adds coverage_warning beside unchanged extracted content when more than 20% of pages or at least ten pages yield no text. reviews.summary: The owner's own chat attaches @file:path, @file:path#L10-40 and @file:"a b.md" for the turn. agents/core/context_refs.py holds the rules. expand (agents/core/context_refs.py:209) finds a reference that starts a word or follows an opening bracket, quote or backtick, and not one inside a word or a path (x@file:, a/@file:, @@file:) (_REF_RE, agents/core/context_refs.py:49); a double-quoted path may hold spaces, #L7 is one line and #L2-L3 a range, and trailing punctuation or a closing quote is not part of it. The routes keep the owner's message as typed: commands, skills, LLM-backend control, the router and memory see only it. The "--- Attached Context ---" section is bound to the turn (bind_attached, agents/core/context_refs.py:251; agents/web.py:1245 on /chat, and inside the stream task at agents/web.py:1312) and appended after the message only in the model prompt (attached_block, agents/core/context_refs.py:266; Orchestrator._build_agent_turn_text, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3357), so the file text is never stored as the owner's words, replayed in a later turn's history or embedded. Hermes keeps the expanded message in the user turn; Nerva shows the attachment to the model for the attaching (tainted) turn only. Each file's text is in a fence longer than any backtick run in it, so no line of it can close the fence (_fence, agents/core/context_refs.py:194), under a header that names the file as typed and the lines actually attached, `(line 7)` or `(lines 2-3)`, as attached file content, not instructions; injection patterns and a forged Attached Context marker are flagged in that header (`flagged: …`, _flags, agents/core/context_refs.py:180), not withheld. Each path is resolved through the same FileScope as file_read (_attach_one, agents/core/context_refs.py:133), so outside the file roots, .. traversal, a symlink escape and a secret-looking path such as .env are refused. A missing file, a directory, a binary file (a NUL in its first 8 KB), a bad line range, a range past the end, an unreadable file, an over-long name, a denied stat and an unknown ~user each become a one-line warning in the same section instead of failing the message. With JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS unset, the file tools' default root <data home>/workspace is used; only an unusable JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS makes the section say nothing was attached. The limits are 8 distinct references per message, 64 KB per reference and 128 KB in all, counted in bytes. A cut reference says so, and a repeated one is attached once. A line range skips the lines before it a 64K-character chunk at a time, up to 64M characters into the file (MAX_SCAN_CHARS; past it, the warning "line N is too far into the file"), keeps at most the byte budget and never reads a line whole (_read_lines, agents/core/context_refs.py:105); invalid UTF-8 is read with replacement characters. The expansion runs on /chat and /chat/stream (agents/web.py:1234, agents/web.py:1399), off the event loop, so both the HUD and nerva chat get it. It never runs for a channel message, as Hermes' gateway does not expand either. A turn that attached anything is tainted: handle_input and handle_input_stream call _taint_attached_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:357, :1984, :2187), which raises the turn's action origin to recall:untrusted. An action planned from attached content therefore escalates GRANT to QUEUE at the kernel, while an inbound turn keeps its more specific origin. complete (agents/core/context_refs.py:272) lists in-scope completions for what follows @file:, with directories ending in / and a path with a space quoted (a name no reference could name is left out). It shows dot files only when asked and never secret paths or links out of the roots, is bounded to 50 entries, and returns nothing for a prefix over 1,024 characters. GET /api/context-refs (agents/core/routers/commands.py:63, user-guarded, read-only) serves it and the reference types, and answers 503 file_roots_unusable when the roots cannot be used. The HUD composer (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:228, :283, frontend/src/context-refs.tsx) offers the reference types while `@` or `@fi` is typed (Tab takes `@file:`), then the in-scope paths; a list is shown only for the text it was fetched for. tests/test_h579_context_refs.py (70 cases) covers the bounds, parsing, whole files, line ranges (single, L-form, past the end), every refusal and warning, a symlink, punctuation, word starts, dedupe, the byte cut, the shared budget, the reference limit, an unreadable file, invalid UTF-8, the roots, an explicit scope and the marker; completion (prefixes, dot files, secrets, roots, a long prefix, a file or missing folder, the bound); both routes, the completion route, the turn taint on both paths, and an inbound turn. The review round added attached text never read as the owner's command (a slash command, a skill, a backend switch) and never stored or carried to a later turn, through the real routes; a file that cannot close its fence; injection and a forged marker flagged; a range in one huge line bounded in memory and a range of many short lines linear; a range too far into a file; quoted paths and their completion; references after brackets and quotes and not inside words; the distinct-reference limit; the header's path and lines; paths the system refuses to look at; and the roots. frontend/src/test/context-refs.test.tsx has 6 cases. The row's 53 mutants predate this code; the review round's 34: 28 caught at once, five after five cases were added, and one equivalent (a kept read stops at the budget either way, since readline(0) answers ""). reviews.summary:
Both halves of the accepted adaptation are delivered: the HUD composer and the terminal. useComposerImages (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx) takes image paste and drag-drop (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:51-52) plus a file chooser. It accepts at most eight PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images of up to 4 MiB each, and the shared InputBar wires it in (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:246). App.submit sends an image draft to runVision (frontend/src/app.tsx:410, frontend/src/app.tsx:385). runVision posts to the user-guarded POST /api/vlm/composer/describe (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:221, registered at agents/web.py:1529). The route checks data-URI signatures and bounds raster decoding (validate_raster, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:53). It binds the request to the reviewed destination/model revision and refuses a non-local VLM unless the owner has acknowledged it (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:251). It then calls VLMBackend.generate_vision_checked (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:354). Since H513 the binding also covers the credential and the data policy, the H378 selection guards refuse a flagged model before any client is built (409), the configuration and the wire are checked again at the request and after cleanup (a change is never an answer: it is a 409 vlm_destination_changed, or a 502 vlm_generation_failed when the changed configuration is no longer a valid vision destination, such as a non-http(s) URL), and the status and the answer carry the data-policy warning, which the composer and the vision reply show (nerva chat --image does not print it). Images reach only the configured VLM, never the text chat model. The taint governance holds through isolation rather than a taint flag. The vision answer is a client-only transcript entry, and ordinary turns post only {message, agent} to /chat/stream (frontend/src/app.tsx:336), so no tool plan can be derived from image content. tests/test_composer_vision.py (33 passed) covers validation, auth, binding, the remote acknowledgement and error shapes, and, since H513, the warning on a pure status, a key rotation that revises the binding, a policy rotated during client construction, a key rotated during cleanup, the H378 selection refusal and a cancelled generation that closes the client. Intake and the vision turn are covered by frontend/src/test/composer-images.test.tsx, frontend/src/test/composer-vision-turn.test.tsx and frontend/e2e/composer-images.spec.ts, (the two vitest files, 12 cases, pass; the Playwright spec was not run here). The terminal: `nerva chat --image PATH` (repeatable, up to eight) and `--clipboard-image` (agents/cli/nerva.py:353) turn the chat verb into the same vision turn (_vision_turn, agents/cli/nerva.py:2403), dispatched before any /chat body is built (agents/cli/nerva.py:2050). Each file is opened once without blocking, must be a regular file, is read up to 4 MiB and sent by the type its signature says, never its name (_image_mime, agents/cli/nerva.py:2146; _read_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:2156). The clipboard is read by the platform's own reader with a fixed argv, no shell, its output read no further than the bound against a 10 s deadline, in a session of its own whose whole process group is killed at the deadline, past the bound or on an interrupt, so a descendant holding the pipe cannot stretch it (_run_reader, agents/cli/nerva.py:2256): wl-paste on Wayland, xclip on X11, pngpaste or else osascript on macOS, Windows PowerShell from the system directory, else the first powershell.exe or pwsh.exe in an absolute PATH entry that is not the current directory (never shutil.which, which puts the current directory back on Windows), on Windows, and through interop under WSL (the /mnt/c default, else the PATH's powershell.exe) (_clipboard_command, agents/cli/nerva.py:2231; _clipboard_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:2341). The verb reads GET /api/vlm/composer/status, sends that destination and binding with the images, so a model changed in between is refused (409), and a destination off the hub's machine is used only when --remote-vision names it, the terminal's form of the HUD's per-destination acknowledgement (agents/cli/nerva.py:2473). The describe call waits up to 240 s (the hub gives the model 180 s), and a timeout after the status answered is a failed turn, not a missing hub; the reply is checked as the HUD checks it (ok, a string answer of at most 128 KiB); a status without its destination, binding or local sends nothing. The --remote-vision address is compared as the hub names it (scheme and host in any case, the default port, a trailing slash); one with a user name, query or fragment is refused as a look-alike, and --remote-vision without an image is refused. A body the route refuses is answered with its first reason as {error, reason}, never FastAPI's default 422 that echoed the images back (_BoundedValidationRoute, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:22), and the CLI prints it, with the field a validation reason names; hub text is filtered before it reaches the terminal. --agent, --session and --reasoning are refused with images: the turn goes to the vision model only, never to /chat, an agent or a session. -z, --json and --usage-file keep their meaning. tests/test_nerva_chat_image.py (31 cases) covers the route taken, the real route answering the CLI, a model changed in between, each raster kind, the remote acknowledgement, the refusals before any request, the hub's answers and the clipboard readers; its 20 mutants are all caught. The first adversarial review (0 major, 6 minor, 9 nits) found the 30 s timeout reported as no hub, the clipboard buffered whole, the route's refusal without its reason, PowerShell resolved from the current directory, 16 surviving mutants of its own, and macOS/WSL gaps; all are fixed, and tests/test_h586b_image_review.py (50 cases) pins them, its 35 mutants all caught. Test manual: CHT-115, CHT-116. The second review (0 major, 4 minor, 8 nits) found an oversized clipboard image reported as empty, the deadline stretched by a descendant, the Windows fallback still reaching the current directory through shutil.which, and 8 real survivors; all are fixed, tests/test_h586c_image_review.py (23 cases, real processes for the deadline, the group kill, the exit code and the bound) pins them, and its 16 mutants are all caught but one equivalent. Known limits: the receipt's model stays null for an image turn, and the route's own 403 (no acknowledgement) is told apart from an auth 403 by its message, a case the binding already makes unreachable. Composer image recovery review (2026-10-02): enabled recovery is exposed by paired validated empty_retries/retry_notice metadata. HUD renders the notice before remote consent and resets acknowledgment on binding changes; CLI validates and prints the notice before acknowledgment/send. Default shapes and stdout/JSON stay unchanged. Actual CLI and web composer tests, full1847 frontend tests, typecheck, E2E TypeScript compilation and build pass; browser E2E execution was not run. Native composer normalization review (2026-10-02): VLM validates and normalizes compatible replies on both budget-disabled and active governed paths. Useful typed reasoning supplies an answer without an extra call; malformed envelopes remain failures. CLI/HUD entrypoints, acknowledgment and public shapes are unchanged. Parent696 integration includes composer/policy tests; frontend/schema/assets match the prior1847-test verified snapshot. Existing equivalent status preserved. Publication review correction (2026-10-02): agents/core/llm/native_response.py:72 now admits only legacy untyped, reasoning.text and reasoning.summary details. Encrypted, opaque, unknown and malformed typed details are skipped even if they contain string summary/content/text. Seven actual governed image/video regressions failed before the fix; the corrected normalization and empty-recovery union passed all163 cases. Opaque-only video refuses in one call without granting retry authority. All base evidence hashes were current before this two-file correction; unchanged authority, transport, route and UI contracts retain their existing assessment.

Each file is opened once without blocking, must be a regular file, is read up to 4 MiB and sent by the type its signature says, never its name (_image_mime, agents/cli/nerva.py:2204; _read_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:2214). The clipboard is read by the platform's own reader with a fixed argv, no shell, its output read no further than the bound against a 10 s deadline, in a session of its own whose whole process group is killed at the deadline, past the bound or on an interrupt, so a descendant holding the pipe cannot stretch it (_run_reader, agents/cli/nerva.py:2314): wl-paste on Wayland, xclip on X11, pngpaste or else osascript on macOS, Windows PowerShell from the system directory, else the first powershell.exe or pwsh.exe in an absolute PATH entry that is not the current directory (never shutil.which, which puts the current directory back on Windows), on Windows, and through interop under WSL (the /mnt/c default, else the PATH's powershell.exe) (_clipboard_command, agents/cli/nerva.py:2289; _clipboard_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:2399). The verb reads GET /api/vlm/composer/status, sends that destination and binding with the images, so a model changed in between is refused (409), and a destination off the hub's machine is used only when --remote-vision names it, the terminal's form of the HUD's per-destination acknowledgement (agents/cli/nerva.py:2550). The describe call waits up to 240 s (the hub gives the model 180 s), and a timeout after the status answered is a failed turn, not a missing hub; the reply is checked as the HUD checks it (ok, a string answer of at most 128 KiB); a status without its destination, binding or local sends nothing. The --remote-vision address is compared as the hub names it (scheme and host in any case, the default port, a trailing slash); one with a user name, query or fragment is refused as a look-alike, and --remote-vision without an image is refused. A body the route refuses is answered with its first reason as {error, reason}, never FastAPI's default 422 that echoed the images back (_BoundedValidationRoute, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:27), and the CLI prints it, with the field a validation reason names; hub text is filtered before it reaches the terminal. --agent, --session and --reasoning are refused with images: the turn goes to the vision model only, never to /chat, an agent or a session. -z, --json and --usage-file keep their meaning. tests/test_nerva_chat_image.py (30 cases) covers the route taken, the real route answering the CLI, a model changed in between, each raster kind, the remote acknowledgement, the refusals before any request, the hub's answers and the clipboard readers; its 20 mutants are all caught. Nerva reads a project's convention files into the turn, as Hermes reads its context files and subdirectory hints. agents/core/project_context.py walks from the nearest git root (never above the file root) down to the working directory (llm.project_dir when it is a folder inside the roots, H218; else the first JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS root), and reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc in each directory in that order (CONVENTION_NAMES, candidates). A directory that the model's file_read, file_list or file_search touches is noted for the session (note_tool_path, bounded to 8 directories and 256 sessions); its chain is read on every later turn, and the tool's own result carries the files the turn had not seen yet, marked tainted so the loop fences it (attach; agents/core/file_tools.py _with_project_context). A script's file call (execute_code, no tool turn) brings none. A local terminal_run runs only after approval, from the queue and outside any turn: ToolRPCServer.handle records the queuing session (note_task, agents/core/tool_rpc.py), and when the approved command ran locally, note_terminal notes its cwd for that session, so its next turn reads the chain (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py _rpc_terminal_run). The command's own result goes to the task row, not to the model. A project SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md or IDENTITY.md is never read, not even through a symlink (HUB_FILES, _admit). Every file is resolved through FileScope (outside the roots, symlink escape and secret paths refused), must be a regular file (a FIFO is never opened), and is bounded to 20 KB, with 40 KB and 12 files a turn and 8 rules a directory, shared by parallel tool calls under the turn's lock; a cut says how much was shown, a file past the budget is named, and files past a count cap are counted (load_file, collect, render). Each file's text and name are scanned with detect_injection_normalized, plus Unicode TAG characters (decoded and scanned) and the fence's markers. A flagged file becomes a [BLOCKED ...] line naming the rules (injection_flag_names) with none of its text, and a flagged name is withheld; other names have non-printable characters escaped and undecodable bytes replaced. The caveated block, which holds the files in the untrusted-data fence, sits after the core-memory block in _build_agent_turn_text; _begin_project_context builds it off the event loop at turn start in both turn paths and marks the turn recall-tainted when any file was given, so an action planned from it escalates GRANT to QUEUE. A noted directory's files are in every later turn of the session, so those turns are tainted too: web_search, web_extract and memory writes refuse until the setting is off or the hub restarts. A guest's turn is given none of them. It is off with llm.project_context_files and in safe mode (layer project_context, named on the HUD banner). tests/test_h594_project_context.py: 66 cases. The original build's 51 mutants were all killed; the review round's fixes each come with a case that fails without them.
