Built in #1207 and fixed after one adversarial review (review-H666: no major; five minors and eight nits, all fixed). Hermes nests the agent's subtasks with one optional parent on each todo item (the id of another item) instead of a nested array, so merge-by-id keeps working, and draws the list through one defensive tree builder. Nerva now does both, for the todo tool's items and for mission plan steps.

The tree builder:
- agents/core/todo_tree.py tree() (agents/core/todo_tree.py:48) returns (item, depth) pairs in depth-first order, children in list order under their parent, with every item exactly once. It is stdlib only, because the CLI imports it.
- Depth is capped at MAX_DEPTH = 4 (agents/core/todo_tree.py:30); a deeper item is drawn at depth 4, under its parent.
- An item whose parent is missing, itself, or not an id at all is drawn at depth 0 in its place (agents/core/todo_tree.py:65). ref() accepts only text or whole numbers as ids; a bool, a fractional float, a list or a dict is no id, and a whole-valued float is its number, as JSON's 1.0 is 1 to the HUD (agents/core/todo_tree.py:33). When two items share an id, the first holds it. Anything that is not a list is an empty tree.

Code execution no longer keeps its files on the system temp root. Where a Sandbox built without an explicit work_dir makes its run directory, first match wins: JARVIS_EXEC_TEMP_DIR in the process environment, then the owner's security.sandbox_temp_dir setting, then the managed cache <data root>/cache/exec (resolve_root, agents/core/exec_cache.py:149). A value that is not an absolute path, or cannot be read as one (a relative path, ~nosuchuser, a NUL byte), is skipped with a warning (_as_root, agents/core/exec_cache.py:117), and the setting refuses such a value on write, as it refuses an age outside 1-8760 hours (agents/core/settings_db.py:795); a choice that names the managed cache, however spelled (through a link or a '..'), is the managed cache, compared by identity (_same_dir, agents/core/exec_cache.py:138). Each run directory is an absolute private mkdtemp (mode 0700, named nerva-sandbox-*) under a root made 0700 when this user owns it; a root that cannot be used gives the system temp directory for that run, with a warning, unmanaged and never pruned (new_work_dir, agents/core/exec_cache.py:177). The Sandbox takes it at construction (agents/core/sandbox.py:85); the orchestrator's one production sandbox (agents/core/orchestrator.py:644) passes no work_dir, so it gets the managed cache. A run directory removed under a live sandbox, or there without its lock or wider than 0700, is made again 0700 and its lock taken again before the next run, and the tool-RPC runtime asks for that before it makes its mailbox inside the directory (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:381) (ensure_work_dir, agents/core/sandbox.py:100). Docker bind-mounts it with --mount, CSV-quoted, so a ':', ',', '"' or line break in the data root is data (_bind_mount, agents/core/sandbox.py:29). A managed run directory's lock lives outside it, in <root>/.locks/<name>.lock, where code run in the directory cannot remove, replace or forge it: an flock held for the sandbox's lifetime, recording host, pid, whether the flock was taken, the kernel's boot id and the pid's start time, written under a private temporary name and renamed into place so it is never seen empty and a link planted at its name is never written through, in a .locks directory that is private and not a link, and released (closed, then removed, as Windows needs) when the sandbox is gone (release, agents/core/exec_cache.py:312; hold, agents/core/exec_cache.py:257). An hourly job (schedule_exec_cache_prune, agents/core/scheduler_service.py:205; run_exec_cache_prune, agents/core/scheduler_service.py:583) prunes the managed cache whatever root is chosen now, off the event loop, never raising into the scheduler (prune, agents/core/exec_cache.py:499). Each run directory is aged as one group: the newest date anywhere inside it, links never followed, dates the whole directory (_newest, agents/core/exec_cache.py:327), a file being dated by the older of its mtime and ctime so a date set in the future never keeps it forever (_date, agents/core/exec_cache.py:323). A directory is removed only when that is older than security.sandbox_temp_max_age_hours (72 by default, never under an hour; max_age_hours, agents/core/exec_cache.py:596), it is not the hub's own live sandbox, and its lock is not held: on the kernel that wrote it (same boot id), a record whose writer took the flock is held exactly while the flock is, so a crashed sandbox whose pid came back (the hub is pid 1 in a container) is free; a record written without a flock is held while its pid is alive with the same start time, asked of the process table on Windows (OpenProcess and GetExitCodeProcess, never os.kill, whose signal 0 is a console Ctrl+C there) (_pid_alive, agents/core/exec_cache.py:390); only a busy flock reads as held, and any other flock error (a filesystem that refuses flock) reads the record; a record from before a reboot of this host, or from before the flag existed, is free when the probe gets the flock; a pid is read only in the pid namespace that numbered it; another host's record, another namespace's, a record whose flock the probe could not test and one with a pid no hold writes are kept until the directory is ten times the age limit old; a lock that cannot be judged is kept and logged and the sweep goes on (_held_safely); a lock that cannot be opened reads as held, and anything but a regular file is no lock (_held, agents/core/exec_cache.py:407). It is claimed by a rename before it is deleted, so a directory that cannot be claimed is kept whole; one swapped for a link after the checks is only unlinked and not counted; an unfinished claim is finished by the next sweep, and a lock whose directory is gone is removed (another host's once the lock is ten times the limit old). Its reply rules govern the agent's own replies to the owner: text drafted in someone else's voice (an email, a post, a message written as the owner) keeps that voice, greetings and sign-offs included, and a persona's warmth or curiosity lives inside the answer (review-H670 m-5); its honesty rules hold for everything an agent writes, drafted text included (review-H670b m-1). 2026-10-09 execution-admission continuation: the production coordinator now supplies a separate authorization-only live profile resolver to the agent loop. Each ToolRPC call rechecks its selected registered name/gated metadata after the independent job scope and registration checks, synchronously before preflight, gated approval intake or handler admission. Revocation during the tool_started await is therefore refused locally even without a context fold. Resolver failure or a missing selected tool denies with the existing tool_not_allowed reason. The check uses inherited principal/origin/job context and does not rebuild provider schemas, change the stable gate/taint views or write H661 turn-offer notes. A production-wiring regression checks the unchanged offer sentinel inside the handler child; a gated regression records no preflight, intake, pending approval or handler effects. This check itself makes no provider call. In-flight tools, direct/script RPC and already-approved execution are outside this admission increment. Standalone runtimes with only the offer hook retain legacy behavior unless execution_profile is wired; the sole production constructor wires both. Existing stale source pins are deliberately not globally restamped. The historical fold/persona assessment below keeps its original scope. Both refreshes from Hermes's row exist (`agents/core/session_refresh.py`, the parked mechanism commit 89b53e85 cherry-picked unchanged; its module docstring has since gained a note on where each half is wired) and are wired at Nerva's two compaction boundaries, each failing in its own direction. **Nerva is turn-based, so most of the row was already true between turns and is pinned as such**: `Orchestrator._prompt_context` reads the skills catalog per turn, the plugin block is rendered per turn, and `AgentToolRuntime._run_loop` resolves ToolRPC → capability registry → tool profile at the top of every run (`test_between_turns_the_offer_was_already_live`). Two things were not live. **(1) The system prompt.** `Agent._load_soul` ran once in `__init__` and `orchestrator.py` sent `agent.soul["content"]` for the life of the process, so a persona edited or quarantined mid-session needed a restart. `Agent._read_soul` is the one builder (same file resolution, same H387 scan, same cap) behind both `_load_soul` and `Agent.refresh_soul`, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (orchestrator.py, a module function so the bare-stub tests of that path keep working) calls it for every agent from `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` — after the clock CAS, never before it, and pinned as such: a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing, an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order. In front of the builder sits an `os.stat` probe (`_soul_signature`: resolved path, inode, size, mtime, ctime and the body cap), because once a session is over budget the conversation-level commit happens on **every** turn — `ContextCompressor.compact()` recomputes from the raw turns each call — and the walk is process-wide: an unchanged persona costs one stat, and only a file whose kernel signature moved reaches the builder (measured over the 18 shipped SOULs, 76 KB: 59.0 ms → 0.55 ms per boundary, 18 → 0 reads and scans). A file written within the last two seconds has no trusted signature (git's racy rule: a same-size edit in the same timestamp tick would be invisible to a stat) and is read and compared by bytes until it ages. Past the probe the keep path is byte equality of the builder's whole output — body *and* front-matter, so a tier or trait edit with the same body is adopted and the HUD's `soul["meta"]` follows — never a dirty flag; a builder that throws keeps the last-good bytes (fails OPEN); a file absent for the instant of an editor's save-by-rename keeps them with a plain warning, and an agent that had no persona and still has none is unchanged, not failed. A scan verdict is not a failure — a persona that is now mostly injection is dropped exactly as a restart would drop it — and it is announced exactly as a restart announces it: `_announce_soul_verdict` is the one place both moments log, so a quarantine at the boundary is the H387 ERROR line, not an INFO line. **(2) The tool set inside one turn.** A loop of up to `llm.tool_loop_max_iterations` model turns kept the list it resolved at the top. `_run_loop` treats a committed fold (`_compact_context` grew `compacted`) as the boundary and re-resolves through `_resolve_offer` (the same three steps, minus the turn-start side effects) via `session_refresh.refresh_tools`, which fails CLOSED: a resolver that raises withdraws every tool, an empty resolution is a revocation, and either ends the loop with `_TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY` after a `tool_loop_withdrawn` event rather than asking a provider a turn on a stale or empty list. The offer and the executor move together (`_specs_for` rebuilds the specs, the gate map the executor checks `offered` against, and the untrusted set) — pinned by a tool withdrawn through the *profile* while still registered in ToolRPC, the one shape that can tell the executor's `tool_not_allowed` from the RPC's own (keeping the stale gate map runs the handler, and that test goes red). Between folds the registry is not consulted at all, so the set stays stable between two folds; Nerva's fold happens inside one user turn, so Hermes's "mid-turn tool sets stay stable" reads here as *between folds*. A `tool_offer_refreshed` event (added/removed/reason) is written only when something moved. 17 mechanism tests (`tests/test_session_refresh.py`, red-proofed by mutation in the parked commit) plus 26 wiring tests (`tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py`). An independent review of the first cut found 14 items (4 major, 6 minor, 4 nits: the per-turn, process-wide re-read cost; the H387 verdict suppressed at the boundary; the overclaim that `ToolRPC.handle` refuses profile revocations; the unpinned gate map and CAS order; the front-matter blind spot; the traceback for a persona-less agent; the docstrings); 13 are addressed here and each code fix was neutered once and shown red (8 mutations, 11 distinct tests red).

reviews.remaining:
**The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates**: the conversation-level commit exists only with `memory.context_compression` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with `llm.tool_loop_enabled` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. **Execution-admission scope:** production coordinator-wired agent-loop calls now recheck live profile authorization before preflight/intake, including between folds. This does not cancel an already-running tool or rewrite queued approvals; direct/script RPC and approved task execution retain their existing contracts. A standalone runtime wired only with `tool_profile` must explicitly supply the separate `execution_profile` hook to gain this check. The model's offered schemas and gate/taint views still refresh only at their existing boundaries. **The persona migration is process-wide**: `orchestrator.agents` is every agent and `agent.soul` is the one dict every session's system prompt reads, so the session that commits migrates the persona for all sessions (the boundary log line says so); refreshing only the routed agents would need the route at `_history_for_prompt`, which it does not have. **On the staged shared-route path the turn's budget is computed against the persona in force before the commit** (`_shared_route_plan` → `build()` measures `agent.soul` while planning; the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`), so a persona that grew is sent that turn with a budget computed for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, self-correcting next turn; the H363 cached prefix and the H673 usage anchor under-count for one turn after a rebuild the same way. The probe trusts the kernel's signature; what the builder reads outside the file (the scan patterns) is code and needs a restart. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild `messages[0]`: a persona change reaches the *next* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" is only as true as the MCP manager's registration into ToolRPC is hot, which this slice did not verify. The lineage row stays at `nerva.context-compaction.v1`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. `refresh_tools` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. The stale comment at `agents/core/file_tools.py` saying `_load_soul` runs no injection scan predates H387 and is left for a hygiene commit (it would drift five unrelated rows). Nine ledger rows cite `agent.py`, `agent_runtime.py` or `orchestrator.py` and were drifted by this branch (and by #1188 on main: its registry path in `orchestrator.py`, and the pairing kwarg, refusal branch and lifespan hand-over in `telegram.py` and `web.py`, which H146, H449, H364 and H671 also cite and were read against — the pairing store is not their subject); each was re-read against the diff on its cited paths before its hashes moved. Six keep their text and take fresh stamps — H146, H298, H363, H364, H449, H679: the in-turn re-resolution runs through `_profiled`, which still applies the job toolset on both sides of the profile, and the result-spill, cache, reasoning and job-pin mechanism those rows cite is untouched. A compaction summary no longer holds the owner's turn past a short bound, and a silent summarizer is cut. Hermes keeps two clocks: how long the summary may make the user wait, and how long the summarizer may go quiet. Nerva awaited the strict-local summarizer inline with neither. Its only limit was the httpx read timeout (120 s for Ollama), a total-duration wait on a non-streaming call, and nothing told the owner. (1) Bounded hold. ContextCompressor takes a gate (agents/core/context_compressor.py:325, used at :596). The orchestrator builds it per turn (_summary_gate, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3776, passed at :3975) around SummaryHold (agents/core/compaction_hold.py:136). SummaryHold.wait (:146) waits at most memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds for the LLM summary (settings_db.py:276; default 10 s, 0 = never wait, clamped 0..120 by hold_seconds, compaction_hold.py:63). One summary per session is written at a time: a turn that finds one still in flight neither waits on it again nor starts a second. Past the hold the turn goes on without the summary, and compress marks the result summary_deferred (context_compressor.py:621). compact (:524) then sends the turns verbatim, their old images dropped, when they still fit the window under the owner's memory.compression_max_tokens; otherwise it sends the deterministic digest. The summary keeps being written. When it lands it seeds this session's iterative-merge prior (_ctx_summary_cache), but only if no newer turn has replaced the prior this turn started from, and never through the compaction-clock CAS: publish commits only what the prompt was built from, and never writes the digest over the pending summary (orchestrator.py:3999). A turn cancelled while it waits (Stop, a client gone) still leaves its summary for the next turn. A summary that fails later seeds nothing and is logged by name. aclose stops what is still being written within the task budget (orchestrator.py:4697; SummaryHold.aclose, compaction_hold.py:185). (2) The owner is told. record_turn_notice (agents/core/turn_notices.py:35; a per-turn sink collected like turn_approvals, one notice per code) carries DEFERRED_NOTICE (compaction_hold.py:38) out as notices on /chat (ChatResponse.notices, agents/web.py:1102, TurnNotice :1085) and on every /chat/stream end event, the failed one included (:1363, :1369). The HUD shows each notice as a system line under the reply (frontend/src/turn-notices.ts, app.tsx:352). The hub log says the summary was deferred and, later, that it landed. (3) Inactivity deadline. The summarizer now streams (stream_summary, compaction_hold.py:88, called at agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:64). It is cut after memory.compression_summary_idle_seconds with nothing received (settings_db.py:277; default 60 s, up to 600, no "off": idle_seconds, compaction_hold.py:71). Any chunk counts as life: a visible token, and a reasoning chunk that shows no text, through the new on_activity callback on the Ollama and LM Studio streams (agents/core/llm/base.py:665, :907). A slow stream that keeps talking is never cut. A cut stream is cancelled and given CLOSE_GRACE (1 s) to close its HTTP response. A backend with no stream is awaited whole. A degraded reply ("⚠️ …", "[backend error …]") or an empty one is now a failure, and so the digest is used. Before, the non-streaming generate could hand an error text over as the summary. It also covers the notice on /chat and every stream end event, the collector unbound after /chat, and on_activity on both local streams. frontend src/test/turn-notices.test.ts covers the HUD. 72 mutants: 70 caught after nine survivors got cases. Two were equivalent. m23 (busy ignoring done()) is equivalent because the done callback always pops the flight first. The other was a redundant typeof check in the HUD helper, which was removed. The summarizer now streams (stream_summary, compaction_hold.py:89, called at agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:143). reviews.summary: Re-read on main at 55d625f4. Telegram has the partial-then-edit mechanism: TelegramDraft (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:116) sends the first token as a message, then edits it in place through _edit_message (telegram.py:459) at most once per STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL (telegram.py:57, 1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; finish() (telegram.py:189) settles the final text in the streamed message, sends overflow as new messages, retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text and falls back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. The adapter declares supports_edit=True (telegram.py:232) and exposes begin_stream (telegram.py:475). The real caller is Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1659), invoked for every non-observed channel turn (orchestrator.py:1535): it opens a draft only when the adapter has begin_stream, its descriptor says supports_edit, the owner setting channels.streaming_replies is on (orchestrator.py:1667) and the delivery router would send to this source; the turn then runs through handle_input_stream with on_token=draft.push (orchestrator.py:1656) and draft.finish (orchestrator.py:1580) replaces the whole-reply send. The conservative default is declarative rather than a stub: ChannelDescriptor.supports_edit defaults to False (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:36), so an adapter that declares nothing gets the whole reply. Slack and Discord are deliberately excluded from streaming (orchestrator.py:1664) because their replies go through the governed channel.reply approval queue (_queue_workspace_reply, orchestrator.py:1589-1590); test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens pins that an editable transport alone cannot publish tokens before that approval. Tests: 82 passed, 1 skipped (tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py needs slack_sdk, absent on this box) across tests/test_telegram_streaming.py, tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py and tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py. #1188's change to telegram.py (the process's shared SenderPairing handed in at construction, deeplink pairing refused when none is wired) does not touch the draft, edit or send paths. Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability.
reviews.remaining: (1) No edit or delete in the base contract: ChannelAdapter (agents/core/channels/base.py:14) still declares only abstract start/stop/send plus receive, and no adapter implements a delete operation (no delete_message or deleteMessage anywhere in agents/), so a sealed streamed preview cannot be removed and there is no base method that fails loudly for a channel that cannot edit; the fallback to a whole reply is silent. (2) Slack and Discord do not stream: both descriptors declare supports_edit=True (agents/core/channels/slack.py:102, agents/core/channels/discord.py:32) but neither adapter implements begin_stream or an edit call (Slack's send posts via chat_postMessage only, slack.py:335), and _begin_channel_draft refuses both because a streamed draft would publish tokens before the channel.reply approval; streaming there needs an approval contract that covers output not yet generated. (3) No acknowledgement at ingest: Telegram sends a typing chat action only while reading an inbound attachment (telegram.py:998) and a record_voice action before a spoken reply, so an ordinary text message gets no receipt signal until the first streamed token or the whole reply; Slack and Discord send none (the Slack Socket Mode envelope ack is a transport ack to Slack, not a signal the sender sees).

reviews.summary:
2026-10-09 local first slice: both public orchestrator entrypoints measure their complete invocation through cleanup with a monotonic clock. A request-owned collector claims once, rejects nested or late publication and closes before transport projection; there is no per-session last-result cache. ChatResponse and every SSE end carry one optional outcome, currently null or {latency_ms: nonnegative integer}. Only a normal return publishes a measurement; commands and handled refusals can have a duration, while exceptions, cancellation, busy and uninstrumented paths have none. Duration does not imply successful model or tool execution. The declared display.status_bar_fields setting defaults to [latency], validates up to eight unique vocabulary entries and filters metrics server-side; an empty, invalid or unavailable selection hides the metric without breaking the answer. The existing Admin Settings editor exposes the preference. Both HUD cockpit and focus chat render one shared Turn duration strip from the current end and clear it on new work, stop, errors, session/agent changes and DEMO transitions; entering DEMO cancels an in-flight live turn. The field is not persisted in history. Mounted tests cover stale callbacks, malformed numbers and session resets; compiled browser regression covers 1280px and 390px, a no-data reply and reload. Focus composer shrink/wrap rules fix the measured 390px overflow. This is the common outcome transport requested by build-queue critic note 10; H220 context/cost and H396 exit/accounting must extend it. No token speed, model name, context percentage, cache ratio or compression counter is claimed. H18.33 now consumes the same server-selected explicit SSE end in native chat, accepting only nonnegative safe integers including zero. The accessible current-turn strip uses separate ephemeral state; new work, stop/error, history/session and connection changes clear it. Agent selection revokes the metric without cancelling a pending text reply, including A-to-B-to-A. Exact persistence projection and remount tests exclude duration from history. Physical-device and live-Hub acceptance remain open.

Independent #1233 review (historical scope): The per-turn data exists on the server. TokenUsage carries provider cache_read/cache_write (agents/core/llm/tool_protocol.py:70-72). The stream path sums provider usage per agent (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2511). The post-turn record writes input, output and cached tokens, a per-turn cache_hit boolean and usage_source into the learning ledger (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4515-4518). Aggregate readouts exist: /api/metrics/north-star (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:166) with %-local and p95 turn latency, shown as a HUD stat card (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:216), and the bench computes a chars/sec throughput (agents/core/bench.py:79). None of it reaches the chat surface live. The /chat/stream end event carries only agent, text, pending_approvals, H677's warming flag and H674's notices (agents/web.py:1363), and ChatResponse (agents/web.py:1090) has reply, pending_approvals, warming and notices only. No HUD component shows tokens/sec, latency, context % or cache hit for the current turn. There is no field-selection setting. Cache hit is not computed as a delta since the last invalidating event: the stored cache_hit is a per-turn boolean that does not reset on model switch or compaction. Nothing hides the readout when there are no cache reads. Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability.
reviews.remaining:
Complete H686 on the existing shared outcome: source-backed output tokens/sec over a defined generation interval; resolved-model context percentage from a complete single-request prompt observation, not a multi-request cost sum; accepted-compaction counts; and cache hit over a declared denominator since verified model-switch/accepted-compaction invalidation, omitted with zero cache reads. Current disjoint provider token categories require an explicit denominator; the historic 1000 input plus 800 cached equals 80% example is not a valid disjoint-counter formula. Render only selected available fields, including the 70/40 cache thresholds when that metric exists; model/background-task/duration vocabulary entries are reserved but not implemented by this latency slice. Add truthful metric-specific backend/HUD tests. Native H18.33 is implemented locally; physical-device accessibility and live-Hub acceptance remain open. H220 and H396 continue through the same outcome and strip, with their broader remaining scope unchanged.

Independent #1233 remaining limits: (1) Compute a per-turn readout: wall latency; output tokens/sec over generation time; context % of the resolved model window; compressions count; and cache hit as a delta since the last cache-invalidating event (model switch or accepted compaction), omitted when there were zero cache reads. Attach it to the /chat/stream end event and the /chat response, leaving fields absent when there is no data. (2) Add a display.status_bar_fields setting with a fixed field vocabulary shared by backend and HUD. (3) Add a HUD status strip on the chat surface that renders only the selected fields, hides omitted ones and colours cache hit at the 70/40 thresholds. (4) Backend and frontend tests.

reviews.summary: One durable 32-hex installation ID now belongs to the validated unprofiled root and is shared across default/named profiles; data, credentials and hub locks stay profile-local. Locked atomic publication adopts only one unambiguous legacy identity, preserves canonical/legacy bytes and refuses conflicting or damaged state. Activation migration requires the selected profile's matching legacy proof; foreign records require reconciliation. Missing ID refuses node grants/deeplinks with fixed 503; unbound old links cannot approve senders. Windows PID updates preserve the lock inode and byte. Nerva already has the shape of a small bundle plus a large on-demand catalog. 12 first-party skills ship under skills/ (for example skills/brief/SKILL.md). They are rendered into the 'Available skills' prompt block (agents/core/agent.py:852), which skills_index_component measures (agents/core/prompt_size.py:157). Hermes skills are not bundled; they are imported one at a time on request. POST /skills/import (agents/core/routers/skills.py:475) is user-guarded and DEV_MODE-gated, and frontend/src/panels/skills-import.tsx drives it. It calls SkillImporter.import_from_hermes (agents/core/skills/importer.py:206). That import checks an exact, digest-verified pin allowlist and fails before any network call (tests/test_hermes_import.py). The pin still predates the upstream reorganisation. agents/core/skills/hermes_pin_v1.json:4 and agents/core/skills/importer.py:50 are v2026.8.27 with 78 entries (tests/test_hermes_import.py:232). So the catalog still lists github-auth, github-code-review, github-issue-to-pr, github-issues, github-pr-workflow, github-repo-management, plan, session-librarian and blogwatcher. It has neither the consolidated github skill nor grill-me or the other new optional skills. _safe_pin_path requires every pinned path to start with skills/ (agents/core/skills/importer.py:113), so upstream's optional-skills/ tree cannot be pinned at all. Each pin entry digests only one SKILL.md, so reference files cannot be imported.
reviews.remaining:
1. Re-pin to upstream's current release (v2026.8.31 or later). Read the bytes, record sha256, execute nothing, and keep the fail-before-network posture.
2. Pin format. The pin must accept the optional-skills/ root, which agents/core/skills/importer.py:113 currently rejects. Each entry must digest-verify and import the skill's reference files as well as SKILL.md, because the consolidated github skill and the pdf and AgentMail skills keep their per-workflow detail in references.
3. Catalog content. The re-pinned catalog must expose the consolidated github skill and grill-me, and drop the merged/deleted skills.
4. Move importer constants, tests and the doc-consistency check to the new tag.
